safi-cedvel:13-13.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive; (الباء) is a preposition of causation; (ما) is redundant (zāʾida); (نقض) is genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (لعنّاهم), and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (ميثاق) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the maṣdar (verbal noun) نقض, and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (لعنّا) is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and (نا) is a pronoun, fāʿil (agent), and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) is a conjunction; (جعلنا) is like لعنّا; (قلوب) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (قاسية) is a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (يحرّفون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الكلم) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (عن مواضع) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يحرّفون), and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) is a conjunction; (نسوا) is a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (حظا) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (من) is a preposition; (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (حظّا); (ذكّروا) is a past verb in the passive, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is an attached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (الباء) is a preposition and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (ذكّروا); (الواو) is a conjunction; (لا) is negating; (تزال) is a defective imperfect verb, nominative, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «أنت»; (تطّلع) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is «أنت»; (على خائنة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تطّلع); (من) is a preposition and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt of خائنة; (إلّا) is a particle of exception; (قليلا) is accusative as the excepted (mustathnā) from the pronoun in (منهم); (منهم) is like the first, attached to a naʿt of (قليلا). (الفاء) is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; (اعف) is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «أنت»; (عنهم) is like منهم, attached to (اعف); (الواو) is a conjunction; (اصفح) is like اعف, indeclinable on the sukūn; (إنّ الله) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters) and its noun; (يحبّ) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is «هو»; (المحسنين) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
The clause «لعناهم» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «جعلنا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لعنّاهم.
The clause «يحرّفون …» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the third-person pronoun in (لعنّاهم) «[Note: It may be resumptive, with no grammatical position.]».
The clause «نسوا …» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يحرّفون.
The clause «ذكّروا به» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «لا تزال …» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يحرّفون …
The clause «تطّلع …» is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of لا تزال.
The clause «اعف عنهم» is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. «إن تابوا وأصلحوا فاعف عنهم».
The clause «إنّ الله يحبّ …» has no grammatical position, explaining the cause (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «يحبّ المحسنين» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(قاسية): feminine of قاس, an active participle from قسا يقسو, on the pattern فاعل. In (قاس) there is iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by conversion and by deletion: its origin is قاسو with a kasra on the sīn; the wāw was converted to yāʾ because it came after a kasra, so it became قاسي … then the yāʾ was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescents with the tanwīn, so it became قاس.
(نسوا): it contains iʿlāl by quiescence and by conversion. Its origin is نسيوا with a ḍamma on the yāʾ; the ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so the vowel was moved to the sīn and the yāʾ made quiescent — iʿlāl by quiescence — then the yāʾ was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescents — the sukūn of the yāʾ and the sukūn of the plural wāw — so it became نسوا, on the pattern فعوا.
(تطّلع): it contains the substitution (ibdāl) of the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form by ṭāʾ; its origin is تطتلع. This substitution is regular in every case where the tāʾ of iftiʿāl comes after a ṭāʾ. Its pattern is تفتعل.
(خائنة): either an active participle with the tāʾ for intensiveness, i.e. a treacherous person; or the tāʾ is for the feminine in the sense of a treacherous group, soul or deed; or it is a maṣdar like العاقبة, because there is a reading (خيانة). The alif in خائنة is converted from a wāw, because the verb is خان يخون. The word contains the substitution of the weak letter by a hamza after the alif, as with every hollow weak verb, where the weak letter in it is converted to a hamza.
(اعف): the word contains iʿlāl by deletion to suit the indeclinable form; its pattern is افع with a ḍamma on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:14-14.t:
* I'rab:
(من) is a preposition; (الذين) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive (majrūr), attached (mutaʿalliq) to (أخذنا) «[Note: The preposition phrase may be attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), with the mubtadaʾ (subject) implied (muqaddar) as قوم, i.e. «ومن الذين قالوا إنّا نصارى قوم أخذنا …».]»; (قالوا) is a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters), and (نا) is a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of إنّ; (نصارى) is the khabar, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the alif; (أخذنا) is a past verb and its fāʿil; (ميثاق) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (نسوا حظّا ممّا ذكّروا به) — its i'rab has already been given «[Note: In the previous verse (13).]»; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (أغرينا) is like أخذنا; (بين) is an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (أغرينا) «[Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of العداوة.]», and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (العداوة) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (البغضاء) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to العداوة by the wāw, accusative; (إلى يوم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أغرينا) «[Note: Or to العداوة and البغضاء.]»; (القيامة) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) is resumptive; (سوف) is a particle of the future; (ينبئ) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (الباء) is a preposition; (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (ينبّئ) «[Note: The returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. «بما كانوا يصنعونه» … It is also possible for (ما) to be a maṣdar-forming particle which, together with the verb after it, is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to the verb ينبئهم, i.e. «ينبّئهم الله بصنعهم» [Translator's note: the source prints «ي ينبّئهم», apparently a typo for «أي ينبّئهم».].]»; (كانوا) is a defective past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the noun of كان; (يصنعون) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «أخذنا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause «أخذ الله ميثاق» «[Note: In verse (12) of this surah … It may also be cut off as resumptive, in which case (من الذين) is attached to what (منهم) in the previous verse is attached to, because it is conjoined to it.]».
The clause «قالوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «إنّا نصارى» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «نسوا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أخذنا.
The clause «ذكّروا به» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «أغرينا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نسوا.
The clause «ينبّئهم الله» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كانوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «يصنعون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كانوا.

safi-cedvel:15-16.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) is a vocative particle; (أهل) is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative (manṣūb); (الكتاب) is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (قد) is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); (جاء) is a past verb, and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (رسول) is the fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (نا) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (يبيّن) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (اللام) is a preposition and (كم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يبيّن); (كثيرا) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (من) is a preposition; (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (كثيرا); (كنتم) is a defective past verb, and (تم) is a pronoun, the noun of كان; (تخفون) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (من الكتاب) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted pronoun in the verb تخفون, i.e.:
«تخفونه من الكتاب»; (الواو) is a conjunction; (يعفو) is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the wāw, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (عن كثير) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يعفو); (قد جاءكم) is like the first; (من الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (جاء) «[Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl of نور.]»; (نور) is the fāʿil, nominative; (الواو) is a conjunction; (كتاب) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to نور, nominative like it; (مبين) is a naʿt of كتاب, nominative.
The vocative clause «يا أهل …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «قد جاءكم رسولنا» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «يبيّن …» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of رسول.
The clause «كنتم تخفون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «تخفون …» is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كنتم.
The clause «ويعفو …» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يبيّن «[Note: This is if the fāʿil of (يعفو) refers to the Messenger, upon him be peace; it is also possible that the fāʿil is Allah, in which case the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.]».
The clause «قد جاءكم … نور» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
(يهدي) is like يعفو, and (الباء) is a preposition and (الهاء) is an attached pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يهدي); (الله) is the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (من) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as the first mafʿūl bihi; (اتّبع) is a past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (رضوان) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (سبل) is a second mafʿūl bihi, whose governor is يهدي, accusative «[Note: Or a badal (substitute) of رضوان, accusative like it. The verb يهدي either takes its second object without a preposition, or takes the second with (إلى) as in the rest of the verse, or with (اللام), as in the saying of the Exalted:
«إنّ هذا القرآن يهدي للتي هي أقوم».]»; (السلام) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) is a conjunction; (يخرج) is like يعفو, and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (من الظلمات) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يخرج); (إلى النور) is like من الظلمات; (بإذن) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يخرج) «[Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl of the third-person pronoun in (يخرجهم).]», and the bāʾ is causal, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) is a conjunction; (يهدي) is like the first, and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (إلى صراط) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يهديهم); (مستقيم) is a naʿt of صراط, genitive.
The clause «يهدي به الله» is in the position of nominative as a second naʿt of كتاب «[Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of كتاب, because it is qualified.]».
The clause «اتّبع رضوانه» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «يخرجهم …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause; the returning pronoun came in the plural in keeping with the meaning of (من) «[Note: The clause may be conjoined to the clause يهدي, with the linking pronoun implied, i.e. «يخرجهم به من الظلمات إلى النور».]».
The clause «يهديهم …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause «[Note: The clause may be conjoined to the clause يهدي, with the linking pronoun implied, i.e. «يهديهم به إلى صراط مستقيم».]»

* Morphology:
(السلام): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb سلم يسلم, of the pattern-class فرح; its pattern is فعال with a fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
Implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in the saying of the Exalted «قَدْ جاءَكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ نُورٌ» …
The light is likened to a person who guides people to good, the common ground in both being guidance; the thing compared to was deleted, the word for the deleted thing compared to was borrowed in the mind for the thing compared, and it was alluded to by one of its concomitants and characteristics, namely coming.
Explicit primary metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya al-aṣliyya): in the saying of the Exalted «وَيُخْرِجُهُمْ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إِلَى النُّورِ», i.e. from the varieties of disbelief and misguidance to faith; the relation is resemblance. The word for the thing compared [Translator's note: the source reads «وقد لفظ المشبه», apparently with a word such as «حذف» (deleted) missing] and the word for the thing compared to was borrowed in its place to stand for it. Since the thing compared to is explicitly stated in this figurative usage, the metaphor is called explicit (taṣrīḥiyya), and it is called primary (aṣliyya) because it occurs in a noun.

* Benefits:
«ادْفَعْ بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ فَإِذَا الَّذِي بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَهُ عَداوَةٌ كَأَنَّهُ وَلِيٌّ حَمِيمٌ» and «يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِنْ قَوْمٍ عَسى أَنْ يَكُونُوا خَيْراً مِنْهُمْ» … to the end of the verse, «وَلا يَغْتَبْ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضاً، أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَنْ يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتاً فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ» …
Among the guarantees of peace in the society of Islam: «يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ جاءَكُمْ فاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا أَنْ تُصِيبُوا قَوْماً بِجَهالَةٍ فَتُصْبِحُوا عَلى ما فَعَلْتُمْ نادِمِينَ», and also «يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيراً مِنَ الظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٌ وَلا تَجَسَّسُوا». This is but a drop from the flood of moral principles and values that the Noble Quran and the noble Sunna have laid down for establishing peace in society.

safi-cedvel:17-17.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) is the lām of the oath, for an implied (muqaddar) oath; (قد) is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); (كفر) is a past verb; (الذين) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); (قالوا) is a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters); (الله) is the Name of Majesty, the noun of إنّ, accusative (manṣūb); (هو) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) «[Note: Or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is المسيح, and the clause هو المسيح is the khabar of إنّ.]»; (المسيح) is the khabar of إنّ, nominative (marfūʿ); (ابن) is a naʿt (adjective) of المسيح or a badal (substitute) of it, nominative; (مريم) is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, since it is a diptote; (قل) is an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «أنت»; (الفاء) is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition; (من) is an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, carrying the sense of denial and rebuke; (يملك) is an imperfect verb, nominative; (من الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (شيئا) — an adjective placed before the noun it qualifies; (شيئا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (إن) is a jussive conditional particle; (أراد) is a past verb, indeclinable, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (يهلك) is an imperfect verb, accusative, and the fāʿil is a pronoun, its implied form being «هو».
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يهلك) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being أراد.
(المسيح) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (ابن مريم) is like the first; (الواو) is a conjunction; (أمّ) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to المسيح, accusative like it, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) is a conjunction; (من) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, conjoined to المسيح; (في) is a preposition; (الأرض) is genitive by في, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of من; (جميعا) is a ḥāl, accusative, of المسيح, his mother and the relative. (الواو) is resumptive; (لله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to a fronted khabar; (ملك) is a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (السموات) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) is a conjunction; (الأرض) is conjoined to السموات, genitive like it; (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, conjoined to السموات; (بين) is an adverb of place, accusative, attached to the omitted ṣila of ما; (هما) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (يخلق) is like يملك; (ما) is like the first, mafʿūl bihi; (يشاء) is like يملك; (الواو) is a conjunction; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (على كلّ) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قدير; (شيء) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (قدير) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative.
The clause «قد كفر الذين …» has no grammatical position, being the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «قالوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «إنّ الله هو المسيح …» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قل …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «من يملك …» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. «إن أراد الله إهلاك الناس فمن يملك منه شيئا», and the conditional clause together with its apodosis is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying.
The clause «يملك …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «إن أراد …» has no grammatical position, explicative … and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. «فمن يملك من الله شيئا».
The clause «يهلك …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «لله ملك السموات …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يخلق …» has no grammatical position, explaining the cause (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «يشاء» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «الله … قدير» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Benefits:
The saying of the Exalted: «لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ». (هو): the strongest view in its i'rab in cases like these is that it is a pronoun conveying emphasis and restriction, with no grammatical position. There is another view, for some parse it as a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, with المسيح as khabar, and the clause هو المسيح in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ. This construction occurs frequently in the Noble Quran, as in the saying of the Exalted in Surat al-Kahf: «إِنْ تَرَنِ أَنَا أَقَلَّ مِنْكَ مالًا وَوَلَداً». The pronoun أنا is for emphasis, with no grammatical position, and أقلّ is the second mafʿūl bihi of the verb ترني. There is a reading with ḍamma on the word أقلّ, so that the i'rab becomes: أنا is a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ, and أقل is the khabar, nominative, and the clause أنا أقل is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. But the first view is stronger, and it accords with the well-known reading; the verses in which such a case occurs are measured by this view.

safi-cedvel:44-45.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl), and (نا) a pronoun in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as the noun of inna (أنزلنا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, and (نا) a pronoun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as fāʿil (agent) (التوراة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (في) a preposition, and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an advanced khabar (predicate) (هدى) a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif (الواو) conjunction (نور) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to هدى, nominative (يحكم) an imperfect verb, nominative (بها) like فيها, attached to (يحكم), (النبيّون) fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as naʿt (adjective) of (النبيّون), (أسلموا) a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (اللام) a preposition (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (يحكم) [Note: It may be attached to (أنزلنا), or attached to an omitted naʿt of هدى and نور.], (هادوا) like أسلموا (الواو) conjunction (الربّانيّون) conjoined to (النبيّون), nominative like it, and likewise (الأحبار), (الباء) a preposition (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (يحكم) in the manner of badal (substitute) with repetition of the preposition [Note: (ما) may be a maṣdar-forming particle, the interpreted maṣdar being in the position of genitive.], (استحفظوا) a past verb, passive.. and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) (من كتاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied resumptive pronoun (al-ʿāʾid) (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الواو) conjunction (كانوا) a defective past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma.. and the wāw is a pronoun, the noun of kāna (على) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (شهداء) (شهداء) khabar of كانوا, accusative (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (rābiṭa) of an implied condition (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing (تخشوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (الناس) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الواو) conjunction (اخشوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (النون) the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya)..
The first-person pronoun — the object of اخشوا — was dropped for lightness (الواو) conjunction (لا تشتروا) like لا تخشوا (بآيات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تشتروا) by its being made to carry the meaning of تستبدلوا ("exchange"), and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (ثمنا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (قليلا) naʿt, accusative. (الواو) resumptive (من) a jussive-governing conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (لم) a particle of negation only (يحكم) an imperfect verb, jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (الباء) a preposition (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (يحكم), (أنزل) a past verb (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (أولئك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ.. and (الكاف) is for address (هم) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as a second mubtadaʾ whose khabar is الكافرون, and the nominal clause is the khabar of أولئك.], (الكافرون) khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «إنّا أنزلنا ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أنزلنا....»: in the position of nominative as khabar of inna.
The clause «فيها هدى....»: in the position of accusative as ḥāl of التوراة.
The clause «يحكم بها النبيّون»: in the position of accusative as ḥāl of the pronoun in (فيها).
The clause «أسلموا»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (الذين).
The clause «هادوا»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «استحفظوا»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «كانوا عليه شهداء»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause استحفظوا.
The clause «لا تخشوا....»: in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if you are put in a difficult position, then do not fear the people".
The clause «اخشون»: in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause لا تخشوا.
The clause «لا تشتروا»: in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause لا تخشوا.
The clause «من لم يحكم»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لم يحكم ...»: in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.].
The clause «أنزل الله ...»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «أولئك ... الكافرون»: in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
(45) (الواو) conjunction (كتبنا) like أنزلنا (عليهم) like عليه, attached to (كتبنا), (فيها) like the first one, attached to (كتبنا), (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb (النفس) the noun of anna, accusative (بالنفس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of anna, i.e.: "that the soul is taken for the soul".
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ النفس بالنفس) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governing word (ʿāmil) being كتبنا.
(الواو) conjunction in the five places (العين، الأنف، الأذن، السنّ، الجروح) nouns conjoined to النفس, the noun of anna, accusative like it (بالعين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar conjoined to the khabar of anna.. and likewise (بالأنف، بالأذن، بالسنّ), (قصاص) a khabar conjoined to the omitted khabar to which بالنفس is attached, nominative, (الفاء) resumptive (من) a jussive-governing conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (تصدّق) a past verb, indeclinable, in the position of jussive as the protasis, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (الباء) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تصدّق) (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (هو) a pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (كفّارة) khabar, nominative (اللام) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted naʿt of كفّارة [Note: It may be attached to كفّارة.], (الواو) conjunction (من لم يحكم ... الظالمون) like its counterpart above ...
The clause «كتبنا ...»: in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause أنزلنا.
The clause «من تصدّق ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تصدّق ...»: in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.].
The clause «هو كفّارة ...»: in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «من لم يحكم ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause من تصدّق, and the clause يحكم is in the position of nominative as khabar of (من).
The clause «أنزل الله»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «أولئك ... الظالمون»: in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(الأحبار), plural of الحبر, on the pattern فعل with fatḥa or kasra on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn, a derived adjective from حبر يحبر, of the pattern-class (bāb) نصر.
(العين), a primitive (jāmid) noun for the well-known organ, its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(الأنف), a primitive noun for the well-known organ, its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(السنّ), a primitive noun for the well-known organ, its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
[Translator's note: السنّ is in fact vowelled with kasra (السِّنّ); the source says fatḥa, and this is translated as written.]
(الجروح), plural of جرح, a primitive noun, its pattern is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn.
(قصاص), an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the four-letter verb قاصّ, its pattern is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ; as for the regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the verb, it is المقاصّة.
(كفّارة), a primitive noun for what is paid or done to cover a sin, its pattern is فعّالة with fatḥa on the fāʾ and a doubled ʿayn bearing fatḥa.

* Rhetoric:
1- In this verse there is a device that falls within the scope of iṭnāb (amplification) in the science of meanings (ʿilm al-maʿānī), in the context of His saying, the Exalted, in describing the prophets «الَّذِينَ أَسْلَمُوا». It is an attribute applied to the prophets by way of praise, not for specification and clarification; yet not with the intent of actually praising them by it — for prophethood is certainly greater than Islam, so describing them by it after describing them by prophethood would be a descent from the higher to the lower — but rather to exalt the standing of the attribute, for bringing forward an attribute in the setting of praising the great ones inevitably announces the greatness of the attribute's worth, as in describing the prophets with righteousness and describing the angels with faith, peace be upon them. Hence it has been said: "The attributes of the noble are the noblest of attributes."
2- Iltifāt (shift of address): in His saying, the Exalted, فَلا تَخْشَوُا النَّاسَ وَاخْشَوْنِ, it is an address to the leaders of the Jews and their scholars by way of iltifāt from the first person to the second person.

* Benefits:
1- Judging by the law of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: This verse, in His saying, the Exalted: وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْكافِرُونَ, conveys the obligation to judge by the law of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in the matters and affairs of life. An objector may object, saying: there are many things that have emerged in our age that did not exist in the age of the Prophet ﷺ. We say: the law of Islam is not rigid; rather there is ijtihād, consensus (ijmāʿ) and analogy (qiyās), and these are sources of legislation that give the law vitality, continuity and progress that meet all the problems of life in every time and place.
2- Is the law of those before us a law for us..
This verse dealt with one aspect of the rulings of the Torah concerning retaliation (qiṣāṣ). The scholars have differed over whether the law of those before us is considered a law for us or not. It has been reported from the companions of Abū Ḥanīfa, some of the companions of al-Shāfiʿī, and from Aḥmad in one of two narrations, that the law of those before us is a law for us by way of revelation, not by way of their altered books. Among the later scholars, Ibn al-Ḥājib chose this view, but he did not consider the condition of revelation in it, and that is the truth; otherwise the dispute would have no meaning, since no one denies the Prophet's ﷺ commitment to revelation, whether of his own law or the law of others. The Ashʿarīs and the Muʿtazila held that it is not, and that is the choice of al-Āmidī among the later scholars; but the first view is the relied-upon one, and the majority of scholars hold it. It is stipulated that nothing should have come in our law that contradicts this law that we adopt.
3 Retaliation and pardon:
His saying فَمَنْ تَصَدَّقَ بِهِ فَهُوَ كَفَّارَةٌ لَهُ: whoever gives up the retaliation voluntarily as charity — whether he is the guardian of the blood in the case of killing (the charity being by taking the blood-money in place of retaliation, or by waiving both the blood and the blood-money together, and this is the right of the guardian, since punishment and pardon are left to him, while the imam retains the right to impose a discretionary punishment (taʿzīr) on the killer as he sees fit) — or he is the one holding the right in the case of all wounds, and he waives retaliation: whoever gives it up as charity, this charity of his is an expiation for his sins, by which Allah removes them from him. Often this call to magnanimity and pardon, and the attaching of the heart to the pardon and forgiveness of Allah, stirs souls that material compensation does not satisfy, and from which retaliation itself does not remove [the pain over] whom they have lost or what they have lost. Retaliation is the utmost that can be achieved on earth to establish justice and secure society, but there remains in the soul a residue that nothing wipes away except attaching hearts to the compensation that comes from Allah.
Imam Aḥmad narrated, saying: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq narrated to us, from Abū al-Safar, who said: «A man of Quraysh broke the tooth of a man of the Anṣār, and he sought redress against him from Muʿāwiya. Muʿāwiya said: We will satisfy him. The Anṣārī insisted, so Muʿāwiya said: Deal with your companion as you will. Abū al-Dardāʾ was sitting there, and Abū al-Dardāʾ said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
«There is no Muslim who is afflicted with something in his body and gives it up as charity, except that Allah raises him a degree by it or removes a sin from him by it»
The Anṣārī said: Then I have pardoned.» Thus the man's soul was satisfied and found rest in what it had not been satisfied with from the wealth of Muʿāwiya, which he had dangled before him as compensation.

safi-cedvel:110-110.t:
* I'rab:
(إذ) an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember) [Note: It may be parsed as a badal (substitute) for (يوم) in the previous verse. It may also be an adverb of the future, because the speech is an introduction to what takes place on the Day of Resurrection in His saying, the Exalted: «إذ قال الله يا عيسى ابن مريم أأنت قلت ...».], (قال) a past verb, (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), (يا) a vocative particle, (عيسى) the one addressed, a singular proper noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative (manṣūb), (ابن) naʿt (adjective) of عيسى, following it in its position; [it is] accusative because it is a muḍāf, (مريم) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa, (اذكر) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت" (you), (نعمة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi, (على) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of نعمتي [Note: It may be attached to a ḥāl of نعمتي.], (الواو) conjunction, (على والدة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what عليك is attached to, and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi, (إذ) an adverb of past time, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, attached to نعمتي [Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl of نعمتي, or it is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from نعمتي.], (أيّدت) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ... (والتاء) fāʿil, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, (بروح) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أيّدت), (القدس) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, (تكلّم) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنت", (النّاس) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, (في المهد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil of تكلّم, i.e. "as a little child", (الواو) conjunction, (كهلا) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the preceding ḥāl contained in the preposition and its genitive noun, (الواو) conjunction, (إذ علّمتك) like إذ أيّدتك, (الكتاب) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, (الواو) conjunction in the three places, (الحكمة، التوراة، الإنجيل) nouns conjoined to الكتاب, accusative like it, (إذ) like إذ أيدتك and conjoined to it, (تخلق) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "أنت", (من الطين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تخلق), (الكاف) a noun meaning "like" (مثل), in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, (هيئة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, (الطير) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, (بإذن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تخلق) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil of تخلق.], and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi, (الفاء) conjunction, (تنفخ) like تخلق, (في) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (تنفخ) [Note: The pronoun in (فيها) refers back to the الكاف, which is a naʿt of an implied هيئة, i.e.: you create from clay a shape like the shape of birds, because it is the thing likened, and the mentioned (الهيئة) is that to which it is likened, and it is of the creation of Allah the Exalted.], (الفاء) conjunction, (تكون) a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, nominative, and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هي", referring back to the الكاف, the adjective of the implied هيئة, (طيرا) khabar (predicate) of تكون, accusative, (بإذني) like the first, attached to a naʿt of (طيرا), (الواو) conjunction, (تبرئ) like تخلق, (الأكمه) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, (الواو) conjunction, (الأبرص) conjoined to الأكمه, accusative, (بإذني) like the first, attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil of تبرئ, (الواو) conjunction, (إذ تخرج الموتى بإذني) like the preceding ones and conjoined to them, (الواو) conjunction, (إذ كففت) like إذ أيّدت, (بني) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ, for it is treated as a sound masculine plural, (إسرائيل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa, (عنك) like عليك, attached to (كففت), (إذ) an adverb attached to (كففت), (جئت a past verb and its fāʿil, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, (بالبينات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of the fāʿil of جئت. (الفاء) resumptive, (قال) like the first, (الذين) a relative noun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil, (كفروا) a past verb and its fāʿil, (من) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil of كفروا, (إن) a particle of negation, (ها) a particle of calling attention (tanbīh), (ذا) a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), (سحر) khabar, nominative, (مبين) naʿt, nominative.
[Translator's note: The source has an unclosed parenthesis in "(جئت"; it is reproduced as written.]
The clause «قال الله» is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of (إذ) to it.
The clause «the vocative and what is within its scope» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «اذكر نعمتي ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative.
The clause «أيّدتك....» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تكلم الناس» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the الكاف in أيدتك [Note: Or it has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).].
The clause «علمتك ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تخلق ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تنفخ ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause تخلق.
The clause «تكون....» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause تنفخ.
The clause «تبرئ ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause تخلق.
The clause «تخرج....» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «كففت ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «جئتهم» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قال الذين....» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إن هذا إلا سحر» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.

* Morphology:
(المهد), a primitive (jāmid) noun meaning the cradle, or the place prepared for the infant; it was originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a noun.
(كهلا), an adjective resembling the active participle (ṣifa mushabbaha), from the verb كهل يكهل, of the class of فتح and the class of كرم; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(الطين- هيئة- الطير- الأكمه- الأبرص): see their morphology in verse (49) of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān.

* Benefits:
1- إِنْ هذا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ.
The student of the language ought to be clear about the matter of «إن», for it may be lightened from «إنّ», which puts the noun in the accusative and the predicate in the nominative; it may be conditional, putting two imperfect verbs in the jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and it may be the one that operates like ليس, putting the noun in the nominative and the predicate in the accusative, as it is in this verse.
Here the questioner has the right to ask why it did not exert its effect in this verse even though it is negating.
The answer to that is that «إن» operating like ليس only exerts its effect under two conditions..
The first: that its predicate does not precede its noun; if it precedes, its effect is cancelled.
The second: that its negation is not broken by «إلّا», as occurs in this verse, and for that reason the predicate came in the nominative.
Among the strangest linguistic usages is what is related from al-Kisāʾī: that he heard a Bedouin say: إنا قائما. He objected to it, thinking it was إنّ, which puts the noun in the accusative and the predicate in the nominative, and that قائما ought properly to be nominative. When he asked him what he meant, it turned out he meant: «إن أنا قائما, i.e. ما أنا قائما (I am not standing)». He had dropped the hamza of «أنا» for lightness and then assimilated, as in His saying, the Exalted: «لكِنَّا هُوَ اللَّهُ رَبِّي».

safi-cedvel:73-73.t:
* I'rab:
(لقد كفر الذين قالوا إنّ الله) its i'rab has already been given [Note: in the previous ayah (72).], (ثالث) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ). (ثلاثة) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (الواو) conjunction. (ما) negative particle. (من) redundant (zāʾida). (إله) genitive in form, nominative in position, mubtadaʾ (subject); its khabar is omitted, its implied form being كائن (existing) or موجود (present). (إلّا) particle of exception. (إله) badal (substitute) of the pronoun in the omitted khabar [Note: or a badal of the position of إله.], (واحد) naʿt (adjective) of إله, nominative. (الواو) resumptive. (إنّ) a conditional particle that puts into the jussive. (لم) a particle of negation only. (ينتهوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the sign of the jussive is the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil (agent). (عن) preposition. (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ينتهوا) [Note: it may be a maṣdar-forming particle, and the interpreted maṣdar (ما يقولون) is in the position of the genitive, attached to (ينتهوا).], (يقولون) imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is fāʿil. (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath [Note: as for the preparatory lām (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa) that usually accompanies the conditional (إن), it is implied.], (يمسّنّ) imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative..
(والنون) the heavy nūn of emphasis. (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first. (كفروا) past verb and its fāʿil. (من) preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of كفروا. (عذاب) fāʿil of يمسّنّ, nominative. (أليم) naʿt of عذاب, nominative.
The clause «كفر الذين ...»: has no grammatical position, being the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «قالوا ...»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إنّ الله ثالث ...»: is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «ما من إله إلّا ...»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause that answers the oath.
The clause «لم ينتهوا ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يقولون»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يمسّنّ»: has no grammatical position, being the answer to an implied oath.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath.
The clause «كفروا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).

* Benefits:
The etiquette of address..
The Noble Qur'an has reached the utmost in its manner of address and guidance, in stirring the soul, calling it to faith and moving the impulses of good within it, and this ayah is evidence of that. Allah the Exalted said: لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ ثالِثُ ثَلاثَةٍ, and He did not say "the Christians have disbelieved". This is a stirring of their souls so that they turn back from disbelief, and an avoidance of wounding their dignity; rather it is a clarification of the falsehood of their saying and that it is disbelief in Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The ayah closes with His saying: وَإِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهُوا عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ لَيَمَسَّنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ. In His saying «ليمسن الذين كفروا منهم عذاب أليم» the door of repentance is opened wide, and those who persist in disbelief are the only ones who will be punished. This speech is the most splendid of speech in addressing the soul and returning it to the right path.

safi-cedvel:74-74.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the rebuking interrogative. (الفاء) conjunction. (لا) negative particle. (يتوبون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is fāʿil (agent). (إلى الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يتوبون). (الواو) conjunction. (يستغفرون) like يتوبون, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (غفور) khabar (predicate), nominative. (رحيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «يتوبون ...»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e. "Do they persist in their false beliefs, so they do not repent?"
The clause «يستغفرونه»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause يتوبون, falling within the scope of the negation.
The clause «الله غفور»: is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

safi-cedvel:75-75.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) negative particle. (المسيح) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ). (ابن) naʿt (adjective) of المسيح or badal (substitute) of it, nominative. (مريم) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa. (إلّا) particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (رسول) khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative. (قد) particle of realization (taḥqīq). (خلت) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was deleted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters..
and (التاء) for the feminine. (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خلت), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الرسل) fāʿil (agent), nominative. (الواو) conjunction. (أمّ) mubtadaʾ, nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (صدّيقة) khabar, nominative. (كانا) defective past verb (of kāna and its sisters).. and (الألف) a pronoun, the noun of kāna. (يأكلان) imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the retention of the nūn.. and (الألف) is fāʿil. (الطعام) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (انظر) imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنت. (كيف) interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), its governor being نبيّن. (نبيّن) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being نحن, for majesty. (اللام) preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (نبيّن). (الآيات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the kasra. (ثمّ) conjunction. (انظر) like the first. (أنّى) interrogative noun meaning كيف (how), indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, its governor being (يؤفكون), which is a passive imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «ما المسيح ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «قد خلت ... الرسل»: is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of رسول.
The clause «أمّه صدّيقة»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كانا يأكلان ...»: has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يأكلان الطعام»: is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of kāna.
The clause «انظر كيف ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «نبيّن»: is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the verb of looking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
The clause «انظر» (the second): has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause انظر (the first).
The clause «يؤفكون»: is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the verb of looking, suspended by the interrogative.

* Morphology:
(صدّيقة), feminine of صدّيق, a derived adjective; it is an intensive form of the active participle from the triliteral صدق; its pattern is فعّيل, with kasra on the fāʾ and on the doubled ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
1- Kināya (metonymy): in His saying كانا يَأْكُلانِ الطَّعامَ, the speech is a metonymy for relieving oneself, because whoever eats food needs to do that. Nothing is intended by it other than a refutation of the Christians in their foul claim and their repugnant belief.
2- Takrīr (repetition): in His saying «انظر» and His saying «ثُمَّ انْظُرْ», and that is for intensifying the expression of wonder; and «ثم» is to show the disparity between the two wonders, i.e. Our clarification of the signs is something marvellous of its kind, reaching the furthest limits of verification and clarity.

safi-cedvel:76-76.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنت. (الهمزة) for the interrogative of disapproval (inkārī). (تعبدون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is fāʿil. (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of ما. (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (ما) relative noun in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) [Note: He expressed it with (ما) to draw attention to the first of his states, since times passed over him — the state of pregnancy — in which he is not described as having reason.
. Or because it is vague and applies to everything.. Or He expressed it with it by giving predominance to what lacks reason, since most of what is worshipped besides Allah is what does not reason, such as idols and others; or what is meant by it is the kind that possesses neither harm nor benefit ...], (لا) negative particle. (يملك) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being هو. (اللام) preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a ḥāl of (ضرّا) — a naʿt (adjective) placed before what it qualifies — (ضرّا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb). (الواو) conjunction. (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasize the negation. (نفعا) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (ضرّا), accusative. (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (الله هو السميع العليم) like الله غفور رحيم [Note: in ayah (74) of this surah.], and (هو) is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is السميع, and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).].
The clause «قل ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «تعبدون»: is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لا يملك»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «الله هو السميع»: is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of تعبدون [Note: or it has no grammatical position, being resumptive.].

* Morphology:
(ضرّا), a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb ضرّ يضرّ, of the class of نصر; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:77-77.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) its i'rab has already been given [Note: in the previous ayah (76).], (يا) vocative particle. (أهل) the one addressed (munādā), muḍāf, accusative (manṣūb). (الكتاب) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (لا) prohibitive particle that puts into the jussive. (تغلوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the sign of the jussive is the deletion of the nūn.. and the wāw is fāʿil (agent). (في دين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تغلوا), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (غير) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it is its description [Note: it may be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of تغلوا, i.e. "do not exceed bounds, not overstepping the truth".], accusative, i.e. "an exceeding other than the truth". (الحقّ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الواو) conjunction. (لا تتّبعوا) like لا تغلوا. (أهواء) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative. (قوم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (قد) particle of realization (taḥqīq). (ضلّوا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is fāʿil. (من) preposition. (قبل) a noun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of the genitive, attached to (ضلّوا). (الواو) conjunction. (أضلوا) like ضلّوا. (كثيرا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الواو) conjunction. (ضلّوا) like the first. (عن سواء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ضلّوا). (السبيل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «قل ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The vocative clause: is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لا تغلوا ...»: has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «لا تتّبعوا»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause answering the vocative.
The clause «قد ضلّوا»: is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of قوم.
The clause «أضلّوا»: is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause ضلوا.
The clause «ضلّوا» (the second): is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the first clause ضلوا.

safi-cedvel:46-46.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (قفّينا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn.. and (نا) a pronoun, fāʿil (agent) (على آثار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قفينا), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (بعيسى) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قفّينا), the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif (ابن) naʿt (adjective) of عيسى, or a badal (substitute), following it in the genitive (مريم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa because it is a diptote (مصدّقا) ḥāl (circumstantial) of عيسى, accusative (manṣūb) (اللام) redundant (zāʾida), for strengthening [Note: The particle may be a genuine one, so that it, together with its genitive noun, is attached to (مصدّقا) because it is an active participle.], (ما) a relative noun whose near position is the genitive by the lām and whose second position is the accusative, for it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle (بين) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما (يدي) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (من التوراة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl of ما (الواو) conjunction (آتينا) like قفّينا, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (الإنجيل) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (في) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an advanced khabar (predicate) (هدى) a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif (الواو) conjunction (نور) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to هدى, nominative like it (الواو) conjunction (مصدّقا) conjoined to the ḥāl clause فيه هدى (لما بين ... من التوراة) like the first (الواو) conjunction (هدى) conjoined to (مصدّقا), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the alif (الواو) conjunction (موعظة) conjoined to (مصدّقا), accusative (للمتّقين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to هدى and موعظة.
The clause «قفّينا ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: Or conjoined to the clause أنزلنا التوراة in verse (44) of this surah.].
The clause «فيه هدى ...»: in the position of accusative as ḥāl of الإنجيل.
The clause «آتيناه ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Morphology:
(آثارهم), plural of أثر, which is the noun from أثر يأثر, of the pattern-classes (bāb) نصر and ضرب, its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.

* Rhetoric:
1- Repetition (takrīr): in His saying, the Exalted, لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ; it is repeated for added affirmation.
2- The eloquent simile (al-tashbīh al-balīgh): it is the likening of the Gospel to light and guidance; the particle of comparison is dropped so that they become the Gospel itself, for hyperbole.

safi-cedvel:47-47.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (اللام) the lām of command (يحكم) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) (أهل) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) (الإنجيل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) (الباء) a preposition (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يحكم), (أنزل) a past verb (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (في) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنزل), (الواو) resumptive (من لم ... هم الفاسقون) the i'rab of its counterpart has already been given [Note: In verse (44) of this surah.].
The clause «يحكم أهل الإنجيل»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أنزل الله ...»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «من لم يحكم ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لم يحكم بما أنزل الله»: in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (من) [Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.].
The clause «أنزل الله (the second)»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
The clause «أولئك هم الفاسقون»: in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:48-48.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction (أنزلنا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn..
and (نا) a pronoun, fāʿil (agent) (إلى) a preposition, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزلنا), (الكتاب) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) (بالحقّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الكتاب, or of the fāʿil of أنزلنا, or of the kāf in (إليك), (مصدّقا لما ...
الكتاب) like مصدّقا لما ... من التوراة [Note: In verse (46) of this surah.] (الواو) conjunction (مهيمنا) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (مصدّقا), accusative (عليه) like إليك, attached to (مهيمنا), (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (rābiṭa) of an implied condition (احكم) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (بين) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (احكم), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (بما أنزل الله) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (47) of this surah.], (الواو) conjunction (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing (تتّبع) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (أهواء) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (عن) a preposition (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil of تتّبع, i.e.: "deviating from what has come to you" (جاء) a past verb, and the fāʿil is "huwa", and it is the resumptive pronoun (al-ʿāʾid), and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (من الحقّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil of جاء (لكل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جعلنا), which is a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn. And (نا) is the fāʿil (من) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (كلّ), i.e. "for every prophet among you" [Note: Despite the separation of the naʿt from the qualified noun by an extraneous element, the meaning does not prevent this, and in the Noble Quran there are parallels to it; He, the Exalted, said: أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَتَّخِذُ وَلِيًّا فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ (Surat al-Anʿām, verse 14) with kasra on the rāʾ of فاطر], (شرعة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الواو) conjunction (منهاجا) conjoined to شرعة, accusative. (الواو) conjunction (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle (شاء) a past verb (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ) (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لو (جعل) a past verb, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (أمّة) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (واحدة) naʿt of أمة, accusative (الواو) conjunction (لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk) (اللام) of causation (يبلو) an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed أن after the lām, and (كم) mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "huwa", i.e. Allah.
(في) a preposition (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (يبلوكم), (آتى) a past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", and (كم) a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi, and the second object is omitted, i.e. "He gave it to you".
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يبلوكم) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being فرّقكم ("He divided you").
(الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition (استبقوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (الخيرات) accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "to the good things".. and it is a mafʿūl bihi if the verb is made to carry the meaning of ابتدروا ("hasten to"), the sign of the accusative being the kasra. (إلى الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted advanced khabar (predicate) (مرجع) a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (جميعا) ḥāl of the pronoun in مرجعكم, accusative, because it is the fāʿil of the maṣdar (الفاء) conjunction (ينبّئ) an imperfect verb, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (بما) like the first, attached to (ينبّئ), (كنتم) a defective past verb..
and (نا) a pronoun, the noun of kāna [Translator's note: so in the source; the pronoun in كنتم is (تم), not (نا).] (فيه) like عليه, attached to (تختلفون), which is an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «أنزلنا ...»: in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause أنزلنا التوراة [Note: In verse (44) of this surah; it may also be cut off as resumptive, so that it has no position.].
The clause «احكم بينهم»: in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: "if you are asked, then judge".
The clause «أنزل الله ...»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (ما).
The clause «لا تتّبع ...»: in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause احكم.
The clause «جاءك ...»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
The clause «جعلنا منكم ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لو شاء الله»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause جعلنا منكم.
The clause «جعلكم ...»: has no grammatical position, apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The implied clause «(فرّقكم)»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لو شاء.
The clause «يبلوكم ...»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «آتاكم»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the third relative noun (ما).
The clause «استبقوا ...»: in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "if you are in the place of testing, then race...".
The clause «إلى الله مرجعكم»: has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «ينبّئكم»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the causal clause.
The clause «كنتم ... تختلفون»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the fourth relative noun (ما).
The clause «تختلفون»: in the position of accusative as khabar of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(مهيما) [Translator's note: so in the source; the word is مهيمنا.], active participle of the four-letter verb (هيمن), its pattern is مفعلل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the first lām. Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī said: «The origin of مهيمن is مؤيمن because it is derived from الأمانة (trustworthiness), since the مهيمن is the witness, and there is no همن in the language such that the hāʾ would be a root letter.
(شرعة), the noun of شرع يشرع, of the pattern-class (bāb) فتح, meaning the law (al-sharīʿa), and what Allah has prescribed for His servants of practices and rulings.
(منهاجا), a noun of place, irregular, from نهج ينهج, its pattern is مفعال with kasra on the mīm.

* Rhetoric:
Simile (tashbīh): in His saying, the Exalted, لِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنا مِنْكُمْ شِرْعَةً وَمِنْهاجاً; the شريعة is the path to water, and religion is likened to it because it is a way leading to what is the cause of eternal life, just as water is the cause of transient life.

* Benefits:
Religion (dīn) and law (sharīʿa)..
Verses have come indicating the unity of religion, and that there is no difference between the religion of one prophet and another, and verses have come indicating a divergence in the law, as in this verse in His saying, the Exalted, لِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنا مِنْكُمْ شِرْعَةً وَمِنْهاجاً. The way of reconciling these verses is that every verse that indicates the absence of divergence indicates the fundamentals of religion: belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers and the Last Day, all of which the messengers brought from Allah and did not differ on. As for the verses indicating that divergence occurred between them, they are understood as referring to the branches (furūʿ) and what relates to the outward forms of worship, for it is possible for Allah to require His servants at every time to worship with what He wills. This is the way of reconciling these verses. Therefore it is not permissible to call them "heavenly religions", because religion is one with all the prophets, namely the affirmation of the oneness of Allah and belief in what He has told us; but it is permissible to say "heavenly laws", because they differ from prophet to prophet according to his time, place, nation and the requirements of his age.

safi-cedvel:111-111.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction, (إذ أوحيت) like إذ قال الله [Note: In the previous verse (110).], (إلى الحواريين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أوحيت), and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ, (أن) a particle of explanation (tafsīr) [Note: Or a maṣdar-forming particle, and the interpreted maṣdar (أن آمنوا) is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) governed by أوحيت ... or in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, the implied form being أوحيت إليهم بأن آمنوا ...], (آمنوا) an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent), (الباء) a preposition and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (آمنوا), (الواو) conjunction, (برسول) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (آمنوا), and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), (قالوا) like كفروا [Note: In the previous verse (110)], (آمنّا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn ... (ونا) a pronoun, fāʿil, (الواو) conjunction, (اشهد) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "أنت" (you), (الباء) a preposition and (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters) and (نا) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of أن, (مسلمون) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), and the sign of the nominative is the wāw - and the interpreted maṣdar (أننا مسلمون) is in the position of the genitive by the الباء, attached to (اشهد).
The clause «أوحيت....» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «آمنوا بي» has no grammatical position, being explicative [Note: Because the verb (أوحيت) contains the meaning of saying without its letters.
(2, 3) In verse (110) of this sūra.].
The clause «قالوا....» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنا» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «اشهد» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause of the maqūl al-qawl.
[Translator's note: The line "(2, 3) In verse (110) of this sūra." inside the last footnote belongs to the footnote markers «2» and «3» of the following entry (verses 112-113); it is reproduced as it stands in the source.]

safi-cedvel:112-113.t:
* I'rab:
(إذ قال الحواريون) like إذ قال الله «2», (يا عيسى ابن مريم) its i'rab has passed «3», (هل) an interrogative particle, (يستطيع) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), (ربّ) fāʿil (agent), nominative, and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle, (ينزل) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (he), (على) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ينزل), (مائدة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, (من السماء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ينزل) [Note: Or attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of مائدة.], and the interpreted maṣdar (أن ينزل) is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi governed by يستطيع.
(قال) a past verb, and the fāʿil is "هو", (اتقوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative, (إن) a jussive-governing conditional particle, (كنتم) a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) ... (وتم) a pronoun, the noun of كان, (مؤمنين) the khabar (predicate) of كان, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
The clause «قال الحواريون....» is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of (إذ) to it.
The clause «يا عيسى....» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «هل يستطيع ربك....» has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative.
The clause «ينزّل....» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «قال....» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «اتقوا....» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «كنتم مؤمنين» has no grammatical position, being resumptive ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: if you believe in the power of Allah, then fear Allah in this request.... or: then fear Allah so that He may answer you.
(113) (قالوا) a past verb and its fāʿil, (نريد) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "نحن" (we), (أن نأكل منها) like أن ينزل علينا.... and the preposition [with its noun] is attached to (نأكل).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نأكل) is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi governed by نريد.
(الواو) conjunction, (تطمئن) an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (نأكل), (قلوب) fāʿil, nominative, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi, (ونعلم) like وتطمئن, (أن) lightened from the doubled أنّ, and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), i.e. أنه, (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq), (صدقتنا) a past verb with its fāʿil and its object, (الواو) conjunction, (نكون) a defective imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (نأكل), and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "نحن", (عليها) like علينا, attached to الشاهدين, (من الشاهدين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of نكون, and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «قالوا....» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «نريد....» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «نأكل» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «تطمئن قلوبنا» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause of the particle-relative.
The clause «نعلم....» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause of the particle-relative.
The clause «قد صدقتنا» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of أنّ - the lightened one -.
The clause «نكون ... من الشاهدين» has no grammatical position, being a ṣila conjoined to the ṣila clause of the particle-relative.
[Translator's note: The references «2» and «3» are footnote markers whose text appears at the end of the previous entry (verse 111): "In verse (110) of this sūra."]

* Morphology:
(مائدة), a primitive (jāmid) noun for a table on which there is food [Note: This restriction has parallels in the language ... one does not say كأس unless there is wine in it, otherwise it is a قدح; one does not say ذنوب and سجل unless there is water in it, otherwise it is a دلو; one does not say جراب unless it is tanned, otherwise it is, إناب; and one does not say قلم unless it is sharpened, otherwise it is a أنبوب.], and it is - according to one view - of the pattern فاعلة, derived from ماد يميد, of the class of باع, as though it sways (تميد) with the food on it. According to another view it is of the meaning of مفعولة, derived from ماده meaning "he gave him", so it is like عيشة راضية (a pleasing life), and its origin is that its owner gave it out (ميد بها), i.e. it was given. A third said:
It was called مائدة because it is relief and a gift. And in al-Miṣbāḥ: ماده ميدا, of the class of باع: he gave him; and المائدة is derived from that, and it is فاعلة in the sense of مفعولة, because the owner gave it (مادها) to the people, i.e. gave it to them; and it is said that it is derived from ماد يميد, i.e. to move, so it is an active participle in the regular way ... end quote.
[Translator's note: In the footnote, "otherwise it is, إناب" is reproduced as written; the expected word is likely إهاب (untanned hide).]

* Benefits:
1- «يا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ» ...
What is the case vowel of the one addressed, «عيسى»? The answer is that the grammarians have permitted two ways in a vocative like this, saying:
If the one addressed is a singular proper noun followed by «ابن» with nothing separating them, and ابن is then annexed to a proper noun, as in the mentioned verse, it is permissible for us to make it indeclinable on the ḍamma, as with the vocative «singular proper noun», and it is permissible for us to make it follow the vowel of «ابن», which is the accusative. An example of that is the saying of ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm:
بأي مشيئة عمرو بن هند ... تطيع بنا الوشاة وتزدرينا
(By what will, O ʿAmr son of Hind, do you obey the slanderers against us and scorn us?)
So «عمرو» can be considered indeclinable on the ḍamma, just as it can be considered accusative, following the vowel of «ابن», which is the accusative: so reflect ... !

safi-cedvel:114-114.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) a past verb, (عيسى) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, (ابن) naʿt (adjective) of عيسى, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied on the alif, (ابن) naʿt of عيسى, nominative like it, or a badal (substitute) from it, or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), (مريم) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa, (اللهم) the one addressed, from which the vocative particle has been omitted, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative ... and the doubled mīm is a compensation for the yāʾ of the vocative, (ربّ) naʿt of the Name of Majesty, following it in the accusative because it is a muḍāf, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi, (أنزل) an imperative verb of supplication, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت" (you), (على) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (بأنزل), (مائدة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), (من السماء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb أنزل [Note: Or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of مائدة, since it has been qualified by the preposition.], (تكون) a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, nominative, and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هي", (اللام) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a ḥāl of (عيدا), which is the khabar (predicate) of the defective verb, accusative, (لأول) a preposition and its genitive noun, a badal from (لنا) with repetition of the preposition, and (نا) muḍāf ilayhi, (الواو) conjunction, (آخرنا) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to أولنا and parsed like it, (الواو) conjunction, (آية) conjoined to (عيدا), accusative, (من) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a naʿt of آية, (الواو) conjunction, (ارزق) like أنزل, and (نا) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, (الواو) resumptive, (أنت) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), (خير) khabar, nominative, (الرازقين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
[Translator's note: The source repeats the phrase "(ابن) naʿt of عيسى, nominative ..." twice, the first time with "the ḍamma implied on the alif", which does not apply to ابن; both are translated as written.]
The clause «قال عيسى....» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «اللهم and what is within its scope» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «أنزل علينا....» has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative.
The clause «تكون ... عيدا» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of مائدة.
The clause «ارزقنا» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «أنت خير ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(عيدا), a noun derived from العود (with fatḥa on the ʿayn and sukūn on the wāw), because it returns every year. It contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change): the wāw was converted into yāʾ because it came vowelless after a kasra; its origin is عود with kasra on the ʿayn and sukūn on the wāw.
