But they formed its diminutive as عييد and its plural as أعياد, to distinguish between it and عود (wood).
(الرازقين), plural of الرازق, which is the active participle of رزق يرزق, of the class of نصر; its pattern is فاعل.

* Benefits:
1- The vocative, when it is the Name of Majesty, is distinguished by matters not found in the other kinds of vocative. Among them is that the hamza of the Name of Majesty is obligatorily made a disjunctive hamza (hamzat qaṭʿ), as in our saying «يا الله».
And among them is that it is most common to omit the vocative particle with the Name of Majesty and compensate for it with a doubled mīm with fatḥa, to indicate magnification, as in «اللهم ارحمنا».
Thirdly: it is not permissible to qualify the Name of Majesty when it is addressed, neither according to the wording nor according to the position; this is the correct view among the majority, and they interpreted His saying, the Exalted:
اللَّهُمَّ، فاطِرَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ» as a second vocative, i.e. يا فاطر السماوات والأرض.
2- The word «اللهم» is used in three ways:
The first: for pure address, as in «اللهم اغفر لي».
The second: it comes to establish the answer firmly in the mind of the listener, as when someone says to you: "Did Khālid do this?" and you say: اللهم نعم.
The third: it is mentioned to indicate the rarity of something and the infrequency of its occurrence, as when you say to the fighter in jihad:
"Allah will reward you for your deed - اللهم إن أخلصت النية فيه (if indeed you made your intention sincere in it)."
Whoever wishes to gain more of the jurisprudence of grammar should consult the discussion of the vocative in the extensive works.

safi-cedvel:18-18.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (قالت) is a past verb, and (التاء) is for the feminine; (اليهود) is the fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (الواو) is a conjunction; (النصارى) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to اليهود, nominative like it, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the alif; (نحن) is a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (أبناء) is the khabar (predicate), nominative; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (أحبّاء) is conjoined to the Name of Majesty by the wāw [Translator's note: so in the source; أحبّاء is grammatically conjoined to أبناء], and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (قل) is an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «أنت»; (الفاء) is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; (اللام) is a preposition; (ما) is an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يعذّب), which is an imperfect verb, nominative, and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو», i.e. Allah; (بذنوب) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يعذّب), the bāʾ being causal, and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (بل) is for digression (iḍrāb) and a fresh start; (أنتم) is a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (بشر) is the khabar, nominative; (من) is a preposition; (من) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of بشر; (خلق) is a past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو», and the returning pronoun is omitted; (يغفر) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is «هو»; (لمن) is like ممّن, attached to (يغفر); (يشاء) is like يغفر, and likewise (يعذّب) and the second (يشاء); (من) is a relative, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لله ما في السموات … بينهما) — its i'rab was given in the previous verse; (الواو) is a conjunction; (إلى) is a preposition and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a fronted khabar; (المصير) is a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative.
The clause «قالت اليهود …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «نحن أبناء الله …» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قل …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لم يعذّبكم» is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. «إن صح قولكم فلم يعذّبكم», and the conditional clause together with its apodosis is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying.
The clause «أنتم بشر» has no grammatical position, resumptive «[Note: Or in the position of accusative as the object of the saying of an omitted verb (قال), i.e. «قال بل أنتم بشر».]».
The clause «خلق» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «يغفر …» has no grammatical position, resumptive within the scope of the saying.
The clause «يشاء» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative (من).
The clause «يعذّب …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يغفر.
The clause «يشاء (the second)» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the third relative (من).
The clause «لله ملك السموات …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يغفر.
The clause «إليه المصير» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لله ملك السموات.

* Morphology:
(أحبّاء): plural of حبيب, a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) of the verb حبّ يحبّ, of the pattern-class ضرب; its pattern is فعيل, and the pattern of أحبّاء is أفعلاء.

safi-cedvel:19-19.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أهل الكتاب … يبين لكم) — its i'rab has already been given «[Note: In verse (15) of this surah.]»; (على فترة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of يبين or of the pronoun in لكم «[Note: It may be attached to the verb جاء, i.e. «at a time of a lull in the sending».]»; (من الرسل) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to a naʿt (adjective) of فترة; (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (تقولوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (ما) is negating; (جاء) is a past verb, and (نا) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (بشير) is genitive (majrūr) in form and nominative (marfūʿ) in position, the fāʿil of جاء; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لا) is redundant, to reinforce the negation; (نذير) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to بشير, following it in the genitive in form.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقولوا) is in the position of genitive by an omitted lām together with the negating lā, attached to (جاءكم) «[Note: The interpreted maṣdar may be in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), with a muḍāf omitted, i.e.:
«مخافة أن تقولوا».]», the implied form being «لئلا تقولوا».
(الفاء) is a conjunction; (قد جاءكم بشير) is like قد جاءكم رسولنا; (الواو) is a conjunction; (نذير) is conjoined to بشير, nominative; (الواو) is resumptive; (الله … قدير) — its i'rab has already been given «[Note: In verse (17) of this surah.]».
The vocative clause «يا أهل …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «قد جاءكم رسولنا» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «يبيّن لكم …» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of رسول.
The clause «تقولوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «ما جاءنا من بشير» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قد جاءكم بشير» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause answering the vocative, and so it reinforces its content.
The clause «الله … قدير» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(فترة): a noun for the time between two missions [of prophets], derived from the verb فتر يفتر, of the pattern-classes نصر and ضرب, meaning to become still; its pattern is فعلة with a fatḥa on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:20-21.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (إذ) is an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being «اذكر». (قال) is a past verb; (موسى) is the fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the alif; (لقوم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (قال), and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (يا) is a vocative particle; (قوم) is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the omitted first-person yāʾ, which is the muḍāf ilayhi; (اذكروا) is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (نعمة) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (على) is a preposition and (كم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of نعمة «[Note: Or attached to نعمة.]»; (إذ) is an adverb of past time, indeclinable, attached to نعمة «[Note: Or a badal (substitute) of نعمة.]»; (جعل) is like قال; (فيكم) is like عليكم, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi; (أنبياء) is the first mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) is a conjunction; (جعلكم ملوكا) is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, a first object and a second object; (الواو) is a conjunction; (آتى) is like قال, and (كم) is a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi; (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi «[Note: (ما) may be an indefinite qualified noun, the second mafʿūl bihi, with the clause after it as its naʿt (adjective).]»; (لم) is a particle of negation, jussive and conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning]; (يؤت) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (أحدا) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and the second object is omitted, i.e. «ما لم يؤته أحدا» …; (من العالمين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to a naʿt of أحد, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «قال موسى …» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يا قوم …» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «اذكروا نعمة …» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «جعل فيكم» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «جعلكم …» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause جعل فيكم.
The clause «آتاكم …» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause جعل فيكم.
The clause «يؤت …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
(21) (يا قوم ادخلوا الأرض) is like يا قوم اذكروا نعمة; (المقدّسة) is a naʿt of الأرض, accusative; (التي) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as a second naʿt of الأرض; (كتب) is like قال; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (لكم) is like عليكم, attached to (كتب); (الواو) is a conjunction; (لا) is the prohibitive, jussive-governing lā; (ترتدّوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (على أدبار) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil of ترتدّوا «[Note: Or attached to the verb ترتدّوا.]», and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) is the fāʾ of causation «[Note: It may be for simple conjunction, and the verb after it is jussive, conjoined to the verb ترتدوا.]»; (تنقلبوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ of causation, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (خاسرين) is a ḥāl, accusative, of the fāʿil of تنقلبوا, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تنقلبوا) is conjoined to a maṣdar (verbal noun) extracted from the preceding speech, i.e. «لا يكن منكم ارتداد فانقلاب» …
The clause «يا قوم …» has no grammatical position, a fresh start falling under what is reported from Moses.
The clause «ادخلوا …» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «كتب الله …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (التي).
The clause «لا ترتدّوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause answering the vocative.
The clause «تنقلبوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(المقدّسة): masculine المقدّس, a passive participle from the quadriliteral قدّس, on the pattern of its passive imperfect with the imperfect prefix replaced by a mīm with ḍamma.
1- The saying of the Exalted: «يا قَوْمِ». Notice the deletion of the first-person yāʾ from the one addressed. This is permissible in the language and occurs frequently in the Noble Quran: «رَبِّ اغْفِرْ وَارْحَمْ», i.e. «يا ربّ». In such a case we parse the deleted yāʾ as an attached pronoun in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).
2- A precious point:
Vowels are implied on the end of a noun or verb (because of impossibility on the alif) and (because of heaviness on the wāw and yāʾ). What I would like to point out is that we imply the vowel on the final yāʾ for heaviness when the yāʾ belongs to the root of the word, such as قاضي and راعي. But when the yāʾ is the first-person yāʾ and does not belong to the root of the word, the vowel is implied on the letter before the first-person yāʾ, its appearance being prevented by the place being occupied by the fitting vowel. So when I say «جاء صديق», it is a fāʿil, nominative with the ḍamma; but when the first-person yāʾ is added I say «جاء صديقي» with a kasra on the qāf to suit the yāʾ. This is the meaning of our saying "its appearance is prevented by the place being occupied by the fitting vowel", and in such a case we parse the first-person yāʾ as an attached pronoun in the position of genitive by annexation.

safi-cedvel:22-22.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا) is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (يا موسى) is a vocative particle and the one addressed (munādā), a singular proper name, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative; (إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters); (في) is a preposition and (ها) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached (mutaʿalliq) to the khabar (predicate) of إنّ; (قوما) is the postponed noun of إنّ, accusative (manṣūb); (جبّارين) is a naʿt (adjective) of (قوما), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (الواو) is a conjunction; (إنّا) is a particle resembling the verb and its noun; (لن) is a particle of negation and the accusative; (ندخل) is an imperfect verb, accusative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «نحن», and (ها) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (حتّى) is a particle of limit and the genitive; (يخرجوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after حتّى, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (منها) is like فيها, attached to (يخرجوا); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (إن) is a jussive conditional particle; (يخرجوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn,
and the wāw is the fāʿil; (منها) is like the first; (الفاء) is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (إنّا) is like the first; (داخلون) is the khabar of إنّ, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «قالوا …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يا موسى …» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّ فيها قوما» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «إنا لن ندخلها» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the vocative.
The clause «لن ندخلها» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The first clause «يخرجوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The second clause «يخرجوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إنّا لن ندخلها.
The clause «إنّا داخلون» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يخرجوا منها) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (ندخلها).

* Morphology:
(جبارين): plural of جبّار, a derived adjective from the quadriliteral (أجبرت). Al-Azharī said: (جبّار), as an attribute of Allah the Exalted or as an attribute of servants, was made from الإجبار, which is subjugation and compulsion, not from جبر. It is reported from al-Farrāʾ that he said: I have not heard فعّال from أفعل except in two words: جبّار from أجبرت and درّاك from أدركت «[Note: From Lisān al-ʿArab by Ibn Manẓūr, entry (جبر).]». Its pattern is فعّال with a fatḥa on the fāʾ and a doubled ʿayn, and it is one of the intensive forms.
(داخلون): plural of داخل, an active participle from the triliteral دخل; its pattern is فاعل.

safi-cedvel:23-23.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) is a past verb; (رجلان) is the fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (من) is a preposition; (الذين) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached (mutaʿalliq) to a naʿt (adjective) of (رجلان); (يخافون) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (أنعم) is like قال; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (على) is a preposition and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنعم); (ادخلوا) is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (عليهم) is like عليهما, attached to (ادخلوا); (الباب) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, attached to the content of the apodosis; (دخلتم) is a past verb indeclinable on the sukūn, and (تم) is a pronoun, fāʿil, and (الواو) is redundant (zāʾida), being the lengthening of the vowel of the mīm, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الفاء) is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters), and (كم) is a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of إنّ; (غالبون) is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (الواو) is a conjunction; (على الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (توكّلوا); (الفاء) is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis of an implied (muqaddar) condition; Abū Ḥayyān called it the answer to an omitted command, its implied form being «تنبهوا فتوكلوا»; (توكّلوا) is like ادخلوا; (إن) is a jussive conditional particle; (كنتم) is a defective past verb, indeclinable, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and (تم) is a pronoun, the noun of كان; (مؤمنين) is the khabar of كان, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «قال رجلان …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يخافون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «أنعم الله …» is in the position of nominative as a second naʿt of (رجلان) «[Note: It may be a parenthetical clause of supplication between the saying and what is said, with no grammatical position. It may also be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (رجلان), since it is qualified; Ibn Hishām considered that weak.]».
The clause «ادخلوا …» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «دخلتموه» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) … and the condition, its verb and its apodosis are in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause that is the object of the saying.
The clause «إنكم غالبون» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «توكّلوا» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition … i.e. «إن كنتم مؤمنين فتوكّلوا».
The clause «كنتم مؤمنين» has no grammatical position, explicative, and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, namely His saying «فتوكّلوا على الله».

* Rhetoric:
The saying of the Exalted: «قالَ رَجُلانِ مِنَ الَّذِينَ يَخافُونَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمَا». Ibn Hishām mentioned several views in the i'rab of the clause «أنعم الله عليهما», saying: it may be a supplication, in which case it is parenthetical (i.e. it intervenes between the saying and what is said), or a statement, in which case it is a second adjective of the two men; its being a ḥāl is weak in terms of meaning, though not weak in terms of grammatical technique, since it [the noun] is qualified.
What Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī says:
As for al-ʿUkbarī, he mentioned several views in its i'rab: another adjective of the two men; and it may be a ḥāl with قد implied, i.e. «قد أنعم الله عليهما», the owner of the ḥāl being the two men or the pronoun in الذين. The most evident and strongest of these views is to make it a second adjective of (رجلان).
This is what al-ʿUkbarī preferred, because this i'rab is the first to come to mind, suits the meaning, and requires no interpretation or implication; for when a word can equally be parsed in several ways, one of which requires implication and the other does not, then no implication is preferable, as the scholars of the principles of grammar have stated.

safi-cedvel:78-78.t:
* I'rab:
(لعن) passive past verb. (الذين) relative noun in the position of the nominative, nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (كفروا) past verb and its fāʿil (agent). (من بني) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of كفروا; the sign of its genitive is the yāʾ, since it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural. (إسرائيل) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa, since it is a diptote. (على لسان) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (لعن). (داود) like إسرائيل. (الواو) conjunction. (عيسى) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to داود, genitive like it, and the sign of the genitive is the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa; a diptote. (ابن) naʿt (adjective) of عيسى, genitive like it. (مريم) like إسرائيل. (ذلك) demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address. (الباء) preposition. (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: or a relative noun, in the position of the genitive, attached to the khabar (predicate) of ذلك, and the returning pronoun is omitted.], (عصوا) like كفروا.. and the ḍamma is implied on the alif that was deleted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما عصوا) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to the omitted khabar of ذلك.
(الواو) conjunction. (كانوا) defective past verb (of kāna and its sisters), indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the noun of kāna. (يعتدون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is fāʿil.
The clause «لعن الذين كفروا»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «كفروا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ذلك بما عصوا»: has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «عصوا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «كانوا يعتدون»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause that is the ṣila of the particle relative.
The clause «يعتدون»: is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كانوا.

* Morphology:
(عصوا), contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is عصاوا. Two vowelless letters met, the alif and the wāw; the alif was deleted and the letter before the wāw was given a fatḥa to indicate it.
The deleted alif is originally a yāʾ, because its verb is عصى يعصي, on the measure of شفى يشفي.
(يعتدون), contains iʿlāl by making vowelless and iʿlāl by deletion; its origin is يعتديون, with ḍamma on the second yāʾ. The ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made vowelless and its vowel was transferred to the dāl — iʿlāl by making vowelless — then the yāʾ was deleted because it came vowelless before the vowelless wāw of the plural — iʿlāl by deletion — so it became يعتدون; its pattern is يفتعون.

* Benefits:
1- (ما)..
(ما) sometimes occurs in a single sentence with three meanings: a relative noun meaning الذي (that which), maṣdar-forming, or an indefinite noun meaning شيء (a thing). It has occurred in this ayah with these meanings, in His saying:
ذلِكَ بِما عَصَوْا. If we consider it a relative noun meaning الذي, the clause after it is the ṣila of the relative; if we consider it maṣdar-forming, the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and the implied meaning is "that is because of their disobedience"; and if we consider it an indefinite noun meaning شيء, it is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ and the clause after it is in the position of the genitive as a description. This is a feature found only in this noble language, and on all the readings the meaning remains sound.
2- Annexing two parts to their two owners..
Whenever two single parts belonging to their two owners are annexed to them without separation, three ways are permissible in them:
1- The plural form; you say: قطعت رؤوس الكبشين (I cut off the heads of the two rams).
2- The dual form; you say: قطعت رأسي الكبشين.
3- The singular form; you say: قطعت رأس الكبشين.
And His saying in the ayah على لسان داود وعيسى is in the singular, not the dual or the plural.

safi-cedvel:79-80.t:
* I'rab:
(كانوا لا يتناهون) like كانوا يعتدون, and (لا) is a negative particle. (عن منكر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يتناهون). (فعلوا) past verb and its fāʿil (agent). (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (اللام) occurring in the answer to an implied oath. (بئس) an inert (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame. (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative, fāʿil [Note: or in the position of the accusative as a tamyīz (specification) of the latent pronoun that is the fāʿil of بئس; the one specified for blame is omitted, its implied form being "their action of abandoning forbidding".], (كانوا يفعلون) like كانوا يعتدون [Note: in the previous ayah (78).].
The clause «كانوا لا يتناهون»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لا يتناهون»: is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of kāna.
The clause «فعلوه»: is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of منكر.
The clause «بئس ما ...»: has no grammatical position, being the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «كانوا يفعلون»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يفعلون»: is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of kāna.
(ترى) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنت. (كثيرا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb). (من) preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted naʿt of (كثيرا). (يتولون) like يعتدون [Note: in the previous ayah (78).] (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi. (كفروا) like فعلوا. (لبئس ما) like the first. (قدّمت) past verb, and (التاء) for the feminine. (لهم) like منهم, attached to (قدّمت). (أنفس) fāʿil, nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle. (سخط) past verb. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (عليهم) like منهم, attached to (سخط).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن سخط الله) is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being هو; this is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "it is what necessitates Allah's anger" [Note: the interpreted maṣdar may be in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and it is the one specified for blame.].
(الواو) conjunction. (في العذاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (خالدون). (هم) a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (خالدون) khabar, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
The clause «ترى كثيرا ...»: has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يتولّون ...»: is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) [Note: or a second mafʿūl bihi, if the verb is one of the heart (qalbī).].
The clause «كفروا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «بئس ما ...»: has no grammatical position, being the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «قدّمت لهم أنفسهم»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «سخط الله»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «هم خالدون»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause that is the ṣila of the particle relative; so it is within the scope of the one specified for blame, i.e. "it is what necessitates Allah's anger and their abiding forever in the punishment".

* Morphology:
(يتناهون), contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is يتناهاون. The alif was deleted because it came vowelless before the vowelless wāw of the plural; its pattern is يتفاعون.
The deleted alif is originally a yāʾ, because the bare form of the verb is نهي, its maṣdar نهي.
(يتولّون), contains iʿlāl by deletion, proceeding in the same way as يتناهون ... and the deleted alif is originally a yāʾ as well.

safi-cedvel:81-81.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction. (لو) a conditional particle that does not put into the jussive. (كانوا) defective past verb (of kāna and its sisters), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the noun of kāna. (يؤمنون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is fāʿil (agent). (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يؤمنون). (الواو) conjunction. (النبيّ) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the Name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr). (الواو) conjunction. (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the Name of Majesty. (أنزل) passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو. (إلى) preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to the verb أنزل. (ما) negative particle. (اتّخذوا) past verb and its fāʿil, and (هم) a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (أولياء) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb). (الواو) [Translator's note: the source gives no role for this wāw.] (لكنّ) a particle resembling the verb (of inna and its sisters), for rectification (istidrāk). (كثيرا) noun of lākinna, accusative. (من) preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (كثيرا). (فاسقون) khabar (predicate) of lākinna, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
The clause «كانوا يؤمنون»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ترى [Note: in the previous ayah (80).].
The clause «يؤمنون»: is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كانوا.
The clause «أنزل إليه»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «ما اتّخذوهم ...»: has no grammatical position, being the answer of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «لكن كثيرا منهم فاسقون»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause كانوا.

safi-cedvel:82-82.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath. (تجدن) imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative ... and the nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنت. (أشد) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (الناس) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (عداوة) tamyīz (specification), accusative. (اللام) preposition. (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) عداوة. (آمنوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is fāʿil. (اليهود) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: (اليهود) may be the first object and (أشد) the second object, and this is the apparent view.], (الواو) conjunction. (الذين) relative noun in the position of the nominative, conjoined to اليهود [Translator's note: the source says "in the position of the nominative", although اليهود, to which it is conjoined, is accusative.]. (أشركوا) like آمنوا. (الواو) conjunction. (لتجدن أقربهم مودة للذين آمنوا) like the first. (الذين) like the previous one, second mafʿūl bihi. (قالوا) like آمنوا. (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (of inna and its sisters), and (نا) a pronoun in the position of the accusative, noun of inna. (نصارى) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), and the sign of its nominative is the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma. (ذلك) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject) ... and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address. (الباء) preposition. (أن) like إنّ. (من) preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted khabar placed first. (قسّيسين) noun of anna, placed later, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ. (الواو) conjunction. (رهبانا) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to قسّيسين, accusative like it.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن منهم قسّيسين) is in the position of the genitive, attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك.
(الواو) conjunction. (أنّ) like أنّ, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative, noun of anna. (لا) negative particle. (يستكبرون) imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنهم لا يستكبرون) is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the first maṣdar.
The clause «لتجدنّ ...»: has no grammatical position, being the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لتجدن» (the second): has no grammatical position, being the answer to an implied oath, conjoined to the first.
The clause «آمنوا» (the second): has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the third relative noun (الذين).
The clause «قالوا ...»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the fourth relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إنّا نصارى»: is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «ذلك بأنّ منهم ...»: has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «لا يستكبرون»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of anna.

* Morphology:
(قسيسين), plural of قسّيس, which is an intensive form of the active participle on the pattern فعيل, with kasra on the fāʾ and on the doubled ʿayn, like صديق. It originates from تقسّس الشيء, when one follows a thing and seeks it out by night; the قسّيس was so named because he pursues knowledge.
(رهبانا) plural of الراهب, which is an active participle, or a noun for one who has withdrawn from people to a monastery.

safi-cedvel:83-83.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction. (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, in the position of the accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis ترى. (سمعوا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is fāʿil (agent). (ما) relative noun [Note: or an indefinite noun that is described, in the position of the accusative ... and the clause after it is its naʿt (adjective).] indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (أنزل) passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو, and it is the returning pronoun. (إلى الرسول) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أنزل). (ترى) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being أنت. (أعين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (تفيض) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being هي. (من الدّمع) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تفيض), on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "from the abundance of tears" [Note: it may be attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of تفيض, i.e. "filled with tears" ... and it may be a tamyīz (specification) with the addition of the explicative من.], (من) preposition. (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to (تفيض). (عرفوا) like سمعوا. (من الحق) like من الدّمع, attached to a ḥāl of the object of عرفوا. (يقولون) imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is fāʿil. (ربّ) the one addressed (munādā), with the vocative particle omitted from it; it is muḍāf, accusative, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (آمنّا) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ... (ونا) a pronoun, fāʿil. (الفاء) conjunction, linking the effect to the cause. (اكتب) imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being أنت, and (نا) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (مع) adverb of place, accusative, attached to (اكتب). (الشاهدين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «سمعوا ...»: is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أنزل ...»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «ترى ...»: has no grammatical position, being the answer of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «تفيض ...»: is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of أعين.
The clause «عرفوا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
The clause «يقولون ...»: has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The vocative clause «ربنا ...»: has no grammatical position, the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). [Translator's note: so in the source; elsewhere the object of the saying is given the position of the accusative.]
The clause «آمنا»: has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «اكتبنا»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the answer to the vocative because it falls within the scope of the answer [Note: the clause may be the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if You accept us, then write us ..."].

* Rhetoric:
1- Istiʿāra (metaphor): in His saying «تَرى أَعْيُنَهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ», i.e. they fill with tears. The overflowing (fayḍ), which is pouring out from fullness, was borrowed for it by way of hyperbole; or their eyes, from excessive weeping, were made as though they themselves overflowed.
2- Hyperbole in the tamyīz: in His saying «تَرى أَعْيُنَهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ». This expression is among the most eloquent and ultimate of expressions, and there are three degrees. The first: فاض دمع عينه (the tears of his eye overflowed), and this is the original. The second is transformed from this, namely the speaker's saying: فاضت عينه دمعا (his eye overflowed with tears); you have transferred the verb to the eye figuratively and by way of hyperbole, then drawn attention to the original and the reality by making accusative, as a tamyīz, what was the agent. The third contains this same transformation, and it is the one occurring in the ayah, except that it is more eloquent than the second by discarding what draws attention to the original, not making the tamyīz accusative, and presenting it in the form of a cause — and Allah knows best. The speech with the cause is further from the original than with the tamyīz only because the tamyīz in such cases is established as having originally been the agent, as in: تصبب زيد عرقا (Zayd dripped with sweat) and اشتعل الرأس شيبا (the head blazed with grey hair). So if you say فاضت عينه دمعا, this original is understood, as is customary in its like. As for the cause, that is not customary in it: do you not see that you say فاضت عينه من ذكر الله (his eye overflowed from the remembrance of Allah) just as you say فاضت عينه من الدمع? So the cause does not convey what the tamyīz conveys.

safi-cedvel:49-49.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or an explicative particle, because the verb أنزلنا إليك occurring in the previous verse (48) means "We said"..
and the clause after it is explicative, with no grammatical position.
(2, 3) in the previous verse (48).], (احكم بينهم بما أنزل الله) its i'rab has already been given «2», and likewise (لا تتبع أهواءهم) «3», (الواو) conjunction (احذر) an imperative verb, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (أنّ) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle [Translator's note: so in the source, with shadda; the Quranic word is أن.] (يفتنوا) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (عن بعض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يفتنوك), (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi (أنزل) a past verb, indeclinable (الله) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), and it is the resumptive element (al-ʿāʾid) [Translator's note: so in the source; the ʿāʾid would normally be the omitted object pronoun, i.e. أنزله.] (إلى) a preposition, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنزل).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن احكم) is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) omitted, i.e. "your judging by what Allah has sent down is Our command".. or "it is obligatory that you judge by what Allah has sent down" [Note: The interpreted maṣdar may be conjoined to the word الكتاب in the previous verse, i.e. "We sent down to you the Book and judging by what Allah has sent down"; it may also be conjoined to الحقّ, i.e.: "We sent down to you the Book with the truth and with judging".].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يفتنوك) is in the position of accusative as badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) of the pronoun in (احذرهم) [Note: Or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with the preposition dropped from it.].
(الفاء) resumptive (إن) a jussive-governing conditional particle (تولّوا) a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (rābiṭa) (اعلم) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (أنّما) a restraining particle and the restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa) (يريد) an imperfect verb, nominative (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (أن يصيبهم) like أن يفتنوك (ببعض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يصيب), (ذنوب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يصيبهم) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governing word (ʿāmil) being يريد.
(الواو) resumptive (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl) (كثيرا) the noun of inna, accusative (من الناس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (كثيرا), (اللام) it is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) (فاسقون) khabar of inna, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «(حكمك) ... أمرنا»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to a preceding resumptive clause «1».
The clause «أنزل الله»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (ما).
The clause «لا تتّبع أهواءهم»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause «2».
The clause «احذرهم ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لا تتّبع أهواءهم.
The clause «يفتنوك ...»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أنزل الله إليك»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
The clause «تولّوا»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «اعلم ...»: in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يريد الله ...»: in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of اعلم, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by (أنما).
The clause «يصيبهم ...»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «إنّ كثيرا ... لفاسقون»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
Ambiguation (ibhām): in His saying, the Exalted, بِبَعْضِ ذُنُوبِهِمْ; this is to magnify their turning away and their excess in committing it, as in the saying of Labīd: أو يرتبط بعض النّفوس حمامها ("or its fated death binds some souls"). He meant his own soul:
He only intended to magnify its standing by this ambiguation, as if he said: a great soul, and a soul — what a soul!
So just as indefiniteness gives the meaning of magnification, which is the meaning of "some-ness", so likewise when "some" (البعض) is stated explicitly.

* Benefits:
The shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa)..
The shifted lām enters the khabar of inna and adds emphasis and strength to the speech, as in this verse وَإِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنَ النَّاسِ لَفاسِقُونَ, and when the people of the town disbelieved the messengers, they said to them رَبُّنا يَعْلَمُ إِنَّا إِلَيْكُمْ لَمُرْسَلُونَ. But if the khabar is a quasi-clause (i.e. an adverb or a preposition and its genitive noun) and precedes its noun, this lām enters the noun, as in His saying, the Exalted, إِنَّ عَلَيْنا لَلْهُدى. وَإِنَّ لَنا لَلْآخِرَةَ وَالْأُولى

safi-cedvel:50-50.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the rhetorical question of disapproval (istifhām inkārī) (الفاء) resumptive [Note: Or a conjunction joining the mentioned verb to an implied verb required by the meaning, i.e.: "Do they turn away from your judgement, and so seek the judgement of the Jāhiliyya?"] (حكم) an advanced mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), its governing word (ʿāmil) being يبغون (الجاهليّة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) (يبغون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) (الواو) conjunction (من) an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) (أحسن) khabar (predicate), nominative (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أحسن (حكما) tamyīz (specification), accusative (لقوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (حكما) [Note: It may be attached to (حكما).. or to something implied, i.e. "this question and address is for a people who are certain", or "that is made clear for a people who are certain". Some grammarians made the lām mean عند ("in the view of"), so that it is attached to أحسن; al-ʿUkbarī said: the one who is certain reflects on the judgement of Allah, so it is good in his view.], (يوقنون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «يبغون»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «من أحسن ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يوقنون»: in the position of genitive as naʿt of قوم.

* Morphology:
(الجاهليّة), either the Jāhiliyya creed, which is following desire that leads to bias and compromise in judgements, or it is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the people of the Jāhiliyya". The word is a relational form (nisba) of الجاهل, which is the active participle of جهل يجهل, of the pattern-class (bāb) فرح; or it is of the type of the artificial maṣdar (al-maṣdar al-ṣināʿī), which ends with a doubled yāʾ and tāʾ marbūṭa.
(يبغون), in it there is weakening (iʿlāl) by deletion after weakening by sukūn; its origin is يبغيون with ḍamma on the second yāʾ. The ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was given sukūn and the ḍamma was moved to the ghayn — weakening by sukūn — and when two sukūns met, the yāʾ was dropped; its pattern is يفعون.

* Rhetoric:
1- The question departing from its original meaning: in His saying, the Exalted, أَفَحُكْمَ الْجاهِلِيَّةِ يَبْغُونَ and His saying وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ حُكْماً. The first is disapproval of, and amazement at, their state and a rebuke to them; the advancing of the object is for specification, which serves to emphasise the disapproval and the amazement, because turning away from the judgement of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and seeking another judgement is astonishing, and seeking the judgement of the Jāhiliyya is uglier and more astonishing.
The second is a denial that anyone's judgement is better than the judgement of Allah the Exalted, or equal to it, as usage indicates, even though the outward construction does not address the negation of equality.
2- The device of al-īghāl (extension): in His saying, the Exalted, وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ حُكْماً لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ. It is a fine device, whose gist is that the speaker completes his speech before bringing its close; then, when he wishes to bring that, he brings something that conveys a meaning additional to the meaning of that speech. It is of two kinds: īghāl of choice and īghāl of precaution, and in this verse it is īghāl of choice.
For the meaning was complete with His saying: «وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ حُكْماً», and since the speech needed a verse-ending (fāṣila) suited to what precedes and follows it, it came conveying an additional meaning which would not have been obtained without it: namely that no one knows that the judgement of Allah is better than every judgement except one who is certain that He is One, Wise and Just. That is why it turned away from saying «يعلمون» ("who know") to saying «يوقنون» ("who are certain").

safi-cedvel:51-51.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (1) of this surah.], (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing (تتخذوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) (اليهود) first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) (النصارى) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to اليهود by the wāw, accusative like it, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif (أولياء) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (بعض) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (أولياء) khabar (predicate), nominative (بعض) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) (الواو) conjunction (من) a jussive-governing conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (يتولّ) an imperfect verb, jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (من) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يتولّى (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (rābiṭa) (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl), and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna (منهم) like منكم, attached to the khabar of inna (إنّ) like the first (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna (لا) negating (يهدي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is "huwa" (القوم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الظالمين) naʿt (adjective) of القوم, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «يأيّها الذين ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
The clause «لا تتخذوا ...»: has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
The clause «بعضهم أولياء ...»: has no grammatical position, parenthetical — or causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «من يتولّهم ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «يتولّهم منكم»: in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.].
The clause «إنّه منهم»: in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إنّ الله لا يهدي ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لا يهدي ...»: in the position of nominative as khabar of inna.

* Morphology:
(يتولّ), in it there is weakening (iʿlāl) by deletion on account of the jussive; its pattern is يتفعّ.

safi-cedvel:52-52.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction (ترى) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (في قلوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted advanced khabar (predicate), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (مرض) a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (يسارعون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (في) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive (majrūr), attached to (يسارعون), on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "in befriending them" (يقولون) like يسارعون (نخشى) like ترى (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle (تصيب) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and (نا) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (دائرة) fāʿil, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تصيبنا) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governing word (ʿāmil) being نخشى [Note: Or in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, its implied form being "من أن تصيبنا".. attached to (نخشى).].
(الفاء) resumptive (عسى) a defective, non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of ʿasā, nominative (أن يأتي) like أن تصيب, and the fāʿil is "huwa" (بالفتح) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يأتي).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتي) is in the position of accusative as the khabar of ʿasā.
(أو) a conjunction (أمر) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الفتح, genitive like it (من عند) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of أمر, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الفاء) a conjunction of causation (sababiyya) (يصبحوا) a defective imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (يأتي), the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the noun of yuṣbiḥ (على) a preposition (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun, the resumptive pronoun being omitted and the clause being the ṣila.. or an indefinite noun qualified (nakira mawṣūfa), the clause being its naʿt.], (أسرّوا) a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil (نادمين) khabar of أصبحوا, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما أسرّوا) is in the position of genitive by (على), attached to (نادمين).
The clause «ترى الذين ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إنّ الله لا يهدي [Note: In the previous verse (51). If the seeing is mental (qalbiyya), the clause is the second object of the verb of seeing.].
[Translator's note: the footnote reads so in the source; presumably it is the clause «يسارعون» that would be the second object if the seeing is mental.]
The clause «في قلوبهم مرض»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يسارعون»: in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of the relative noun.
The clause «يقولون ...»: in the position of accusative as ḥāl of the fāʿil of يسارعون.
The clause «نخشى ...»: in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «تصيبنا دائرة»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «عسى الله ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يأتي ...»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يصبحوا»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause that is the ṣila of the particle-relative.
The clause «أسروا»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(دائرة), feminine of دائر, which is the active participle of دار, its pattern is فاعل. It is a predominant adjective (ṣifa ghāliba) with which the qualified noun is dropped. In the word there is substitution of the weak letter by a hamza, because the weak letter comes after the alif of فاعل, and this change is regular.

safi-cedvel:115-115.t:
* I'rab:
(قال الله) like قال عيسى [Note: In the previous verse (114).], (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters) and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of إنّ, (منزّل) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the active participle منزّل, (الفاء) conjunction, (من) a jussive-governing conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), (يكفر) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (he), (بعد) an adverb of time, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative, attached to (يكفر), (منكم) like عليكم, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يكفر, (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), (إنّي أعذّبه) like إنّي منزّلها, (عذابا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), for it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), accusative (manṣūb), (لا) negating, (أعذّب) an imperfect verb, nominative - and likewise the first one - and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, for it is the pronoun of the maṣdar, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنا" (I), (أحدا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, (من العالمين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (أحدا), and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «قال الله....»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «إنّي منزّلها»: is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «من يكفر ...»: is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause of the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «يكفر....»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «إنّي أعذّبه....»: is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the الفاء.
The clause «أعذّبه (the first)»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «أعذّبه (the second)»: is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of (عذابا).

* Morphology:
(منزّلها), active participle of the quadriliteral نزّل; its pattern is مفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the doubled ʿayn.
(عذابا), a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) of the quadriliteral verb عذّب; its regular maṣdar is تعذيب.

* Benefits:
- «فَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بَعْدُ مِنْكُمْ».
The grammarians pay attention to these two adverbs «قبل and بعد». We summarise for you what has come concerning them by way of discussion and examination: they are two adverbs of time, put in the accusative as adverbs or put in the genitive by من, as in «جئت قبل الظهر أو بعده (I came before noon or after it), and من قبله أو بعده is also correct».
They may come for place, as in «داري قبل دارك أو بعدها (my house is before your house or after it)», and they are declinable, in the accusative, or in the genitive by من.
They are made indeclinable on the ḍamma when they are cut off from annexation in wording while the meaning remains intended, as in the mentioned verse. For the muḍāf ilayhi remains in intention and implication, «i.e. من بعد نزول المائدة (after the sending down of the table)»; and like that is His saying, the Exalted: «لله الأمر من قبل ومن بعد», i.e. before the victory and after it. If they are cut off from annexation in both wording and meaning, they are declinable, as in: «جئت قبلا أو بعدا», and from that is the saying of the poet: فساغ لي الشراب وكنت قبلا ... أكاد أغصّ بالماء الفرات
(Then drink became pleasant to me, whereas before I would almost choke on fresh water.)
To establish the sum of this discussion we say:
If you mean a specific "before" or "after", you specify that by annexation, as in جئت قبل الشمس أو بعدها, or by omitting the muḍāf ilayhi and making قبل and بعد indeclinable on the ḍamma, as in «جئتك قبل وبعد أو من بعد»; for the adverb here, even if cut off from annexation in wording, is not cut off from it in meaning. If you mean a non-specific "before" or "after", you say جئتك قبلا أو بعدا أو من قبل أو من بعد, by cutting them off from annexation in wording and meaning and giving them tanwīn, since indefiniteness and vagueness are intended by them.

safi-cedvel:116-118.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive, (إذ قال ... مريم) its i'rab has passed [Note: In verse (110) of this sūra. And (إذ) here is an adverb of the future, because the speech is about what the state will be on the Day of Resurrection.], (الهمزة) for interrogation, (أنت) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), (قلت) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), (للناس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قلت), (اتّخذوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (النون) is for protection (al-wiqāya), and (الياء) a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), (الواو) conjunction, (أمّ) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the pronoun of the first person, following it in the accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on what precedes the yāʾ, and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), (إلهين) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ, (من) a preposition, (دون) genitive (majrūr), attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (إلهين) [Note: Or it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of اتّخذوا, i.e. "passing over".], (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, (قال) a past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (he), (سبحان) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "أسبّح" (I glorify), and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi, (ما) negating, (يكون) a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), (اللام) a preposition and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to the omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of يكون, (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle, (أقول) an imperfect verb, accusative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنا" (I), (ما) a relative noun [Note: Or an indefinite noun qualified (nakira mawṣūfa) in the position of the accusative, and the clause after it is its naʿt.], indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, (ليس) a defective, inflexible (jāmid) past verb, and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو", referring back to ما, (لي) like the first, attached to حقّ [Note: Or attached to an omitted ḥāl of حقّ - an adjective placed before what it qualifies -.], (الباء) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, (حقّ) genitive in wording, accusative in position, the khabar of ليس [Note: It is permissible to make the الباء original (non-redundant), the preposition and its genitive noun being a ḥāl of the yāʾ in (لي), and (لي) then becomes the khabar of (ليس).].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أقول) is in the position of the nominative as the postponed noun of يكون.
(إن) a jussive-governing conditional particle, (كنت) a defective past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) ... and the tāʾ is the noun of كان, (قلت) a past verb and its fāʿil, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq), (علمت) like قلت, (تعلم) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "أنت" (you), (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, (في نفس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما, and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi, (الواو) conjunction, (لا) negating, (أعلم ما في نفسك) like تعلم ... نفسي, (إنّك أنت علّام الغيوب) its i'rab has passed [Note: In verse (109) of this sūra.].
The clause «قال الله....»: is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يا عيسى ...»: is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «أأنت قلت ...»: has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative.
The clause «قلت للناس ...»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of أنت.
The clause «اتّخذوني ...»: is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «قال ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «(أسبح) سبحانك»: has no grammatical position, being a parenthetical supplication.
The clause «يكون لي»: is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «أقول ...»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative.
The clause «ليس لي بحقّ»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «كنت قلته ...»: has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «قلته»: is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كنت.
The clause «قد علمته»: is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis.
The clause «تعلم ...»: has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «لا أعلم»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the causal clause.
The clause «إنّك ... علّام ...»: has no grammatical position, being causal.
[Translator's note: Where the source says the conjoined أمّ follows the pronoun "في النسب" (in lineage), this is evidently a misprint for "في النصب" (in the accusative), and it has been rendered accordingly.]
(117) (ما) negating, (قلت) like the first, (لهم) like لي, attached to (قلت), (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi [Note: Or an indefinite noun qualified, in the position of the accusative.. and the clause after it is its naʿt.], (أمرت) like قلت, and (النون) for protection, and (الياء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (أمرت), (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a particle of explanation (tafsīr).. al-ʿUkbarī forbade it from being a particle of explanation because the verb of saying has been stated explicitly..
But one can comment on this that the use of the verb of saying by ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, is in compliance with the requirement of good manners, so that he does not make himself one who commands alongside his Lord.. For this reason it is correct to parse it as explicative. And it is explicative, according to the view of Ibn Hishām, of the verb of saying interpreted as (أمرتهم).], (اعبدوا) like اتّخذوا, (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative, (ربّ) naʿt of the Name of Majesty, accusative like it, and the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied on what precedes the yāʾ, and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi, (الواو) conjunction, (ربّكم) conjoined to ربّي, accusative like it.. and كم is muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن اعبدوا) is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو".. and the nominal clause explains the pronoun in (به).
(الواو) resumptive, (كنت) like the first, (على) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (شهيدا), which is the khabar of كنت, accusative, (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle, (دمت) a defective past verb [Translator's note: the source has "ناقض", evidently a misprint for "ناقص" (defective).] and its noun, (فيهم) like عليهم, attached to the omitted khabar of ما دمت.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما دمت فيهم) is in the position of the accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (شهيدا).
(الفاء) conjunction, (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", containing the meaning of condition, attached to the content of the apodosis, i.e. "I watched over them", (توفّيت) a past verb and its fāʿil, and (النون) for protection, (الياء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, (كنت) like the first, (أنت) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position [Note: Or tawkīd (emphasis) of the attached pronoun in (كنت), in the position of the nominative.], (الرقيب) khabar of كنت, accusative, (عليهم) like the first, attached to الرقيب.
(الواو) resumptive, (أنت) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ, (على كلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to شهيد, (شيء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, (شهيد) khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative.
The clause «ما قلت لهم ...»: has no grammatical position, being a resumption in the course of ʿĪsā's speech.
The clause «أمرتني»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «اعبدوا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «كنت ... شهيدا»: has no grammatical position, being a resumption in the course of ʿĪsā's speech.
The clause «دمت فيهم»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «توفّيتني»: is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «كنت ... الرقيب»: has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أنت ... شهيد»: has no grammatical position, being a resumption in the course of ʿĪsā's speech.
(118) (إن) like the first, (تعذّب) an imperfect verb, jussive, the protasis, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنت", (الفاء) connecting the apodosis, (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters) and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of إنّ, (عباد) khabar, nominative, and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi, (الواو) conjunction, (إن تغفر) like إن تعذّب, (لهم) like the first, attached to (تغفر), (فإنّك) like فإنّهم, (أنت) a pronoun of separation [Note: Or tawkīd of the attached pronoun (الكاف), and it has been borrowed for the position of the accusative.], (العزيز) khabar of إنّ, nominative, (الحكيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «إن تعذّبهم ...»: has no grammatical position, being a resumption in the course of ʿĪsā's speech.
The clause «إنّهم عبادك»: is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the الفاء.
The clause «إن تغفر لهم»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause إن تعذّبهم.
The clause «إنّك ... العزيز»: is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the الفاء.

* Rhetoric:
1- Mushākala (verbal correspondence): in His saying, the Exalted, «وَلا أَعْلَمُ ما فِي نَفْسِكَ», the saying "في نفسك" is for mushākala.
The meaning is: You know what I know, which I hide in my heart, so how much more what I make public; and I do not know what You know, which You hide. He followed in that the path of mushākala, as in the saying of the poet:
«قالوا اقترح شيئا نجد لك طبخه ... قلت اطبخوا لي جبة وقميصا»
(They said: "Propose something, we will cook it well for you." I said: "Cook me a cloak and a shirt.")
Except that in the verse both words occur in the speech of one person, whereas what is in the line of poetry is not so.
1- The art of selection (al-takhyīr): in His saying, the Exalted, «إِنْ تُعَذِّبْهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ عِبادُكَ وَإِنْ تَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ فَإِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ».
It is one of the arts of rhetoric, without equal and difficult to grasp. Its definition is that the poet or prose writer brings a passage of speech or a line of poetry that could permissibly be rhymed with various rhymes, and he selects from them one rhyme, preferred over the rest, and his preferring it is taken as evidence of the excellence of his choice and the soundness of his sense. In this verse, first intuition would require the verse ending to be «إنك أنت الغفور الرحيم», because of its suitability to His saying «إِنْ تَغْفِرْ»; but this illusion arising from that intuition quickly loses its effect when the one under the illusion remembers that these people deserved punishment rather than forgiveness, so the verse ending must be «الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ».
[Translator's note: The source numbers both rhetoric points "1-".]
al-Aṣmaʿī and the Bedouin:
One day al-Aṣmaʿī was reciting «وَالسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهُما جَزاءً بِما كَسَبا نَكالًا مِنَ اللَّهِ» and ended the verse with «والله غفور رحيم». A Bedouin was listening to him, objected and said he had erred. Al-Aṣmaʿī checked the verse, and it was «وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ». He said to the Bedouin: "How did you know that?" He said: "O you: He was mighty, so He judged, so He cut off; had He forgiven and shown mercy, He would not have cut off." Al-Aṣmaʿī was astonished and silenced. So reflect ... !

safi-cedvel:24-24.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا يا موسى) — its i'rab has already been given «1», and likewise (إنّا لن ندخلها) «2» [Translator's note: the source has the footnote markers «1» and «2» without footnote text; they presumably refer to the previous verse (22).]; (أبدا) is an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached (mutaʿalliq) to (ندخلها); (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle; (داموا) is a defective past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the noun of ما دام; (في) is a preposition and (ها) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to the khabar (predicate) of ما دام.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما داموا فيها) is in the position of accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (ندخلها); this adverb is of the kind of badal (substitute) from what precedes it, a substitution of part for whole.
(الفاء) is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; (اذهب) is an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «أنت»; (أنت) is a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent pronoun that is the fāʿil of اذهب; (الواو) is a conjunction; (ربّ) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the latent pronoun أنت, following it in the nominative, and (الكاف) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (قاتلا) is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and (الألف) is a pronoun, fāʿil; (إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters), and (نا) is a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of إنّ; (ها) is a particle of alerting; (هنا) is a demonstrative, an adverb of place, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, attached to (قاعدون), which is the khabar of إنّ, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «قالوا …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يا موسى …» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّا لن ندخلها …» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «ندخلها» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «اذهب …» is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. «إن أردت قتالا فاذهب» ….
The clause «قاتلا» is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause اذهب.
The clause «إنّا هاهنا قاعدون» has no grammatical position, explaining the cause (taʿlīliyya).

safi-cedvel:25-25.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) is a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو», i.e. Moses; (ربّ) is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, with the vocative particle omitted, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the first-person yāʾ, which was omitted for lightening and is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إنّي) is like إنّا «[Note: In the previous verse (24).]»; (لا) is negating; (أملك) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «أنا»; (إلّا) is a particle of restriction; (نفسي) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the yāʾ, and the yāʾ is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) is a conjunction; (أخي) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to نفسي and is parsed like it «[Note: Ibn Hishām mentioned in al-Shudhūr five other possibilities in the i'rab of أخي (Shudhūr al-Dhahab, p. 44, 3rd ed.).]»; (الفاء) is a conjunction linking the effect to the cause; (افرق) is an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is «أنت»; (بين) is an adverb of place, accusative, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (افرق), and (نا) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) is a conjunction; (بين) is like the first; (القوم) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الفاسقين) is a naʿt (adjective) of القوم, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «قال …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The vocative clause «ربّ» has no grammatical position, parenthetical, to seek mercy.
The clause «إنّي لا أملك» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لا أملك …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «افرق بيننا» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause that is the object of the saying.

* Benefits:
The saying of the Exalted «قالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي لا أَمْلِكُ إِلَّا نَفْسِي وَأَخِي»: what Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī mentioned in the i'rab of (وأخي).
There are two views on its position: 1- the accusative, conjoined to نفسي as a mafʿūl bihi, or to the noun of إنّ.
2- the nominative, conjoined to the latent pronoun in أملك, i.e. «and my brother possesses only himself»; it may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar omitted, i.e. «وأخي كذلك».
But the most evident and strongest is the accusative, conjoined to نفسي, because this view is the closest of the views to the mind, the most attached to the meaning and the clearest.

safi-cedvel:26-26.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) is a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is «هو», i.e. Allah; (الفاء) is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; (إنّها محرّمة) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters), its noun and its khabar (predicate); (على) is a preposition and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (محرّمة); (أربعين) is an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to محرّمة «[Note: It may be attached to (يتيهون).]», the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, since it is treated like the sound masculine plural; (سنة) is a tamyīz (specification), accusative; (يتيهون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يتيهون). (الفاء) is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis of an implied condition; (لا) is the prohibitive, jussive-governing lā; (تأس) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «أنت»; (على القوم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تأس); (الفاسقين) is a naʿt (adjective) of القوم, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «قال …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
