The clause «إنّها محرّمة» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. «إن كنت ضيّقا بهم فإنّها محرّمة», and the implied conditional clause with its apodosis is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) …
The clause «يتيهون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the genitive pronoun in (عليهم).
The clause «لا تأس …» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. «إن عظم لديك هذا العقاب فلا تأس» …

* Morphology:
(محرّمة): feminine of محرّم, a passive participle from حرّم … (see verse 85 of Surat al-Baqara). (تأس): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion to suit the jussive; its pattern is تفع with a fatḥa on the tāʾ and the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:27-27.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (اتل) is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «أنت»; (على) is a preposition and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (اتل); (نبأ) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (ابني) is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (آدم) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa because it is a diptote; (بالحقّ) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of اتل «[Note: Or a ḥāl of نبأ … It may also be attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because it is its description, i.e. «اتل ذلك تلاوة متلبّسة بالحقّ والصدق» … This is al-Zamakhsharī's choice.]»; (إذ) is an adverb of past time, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, attached to (نبأ); (قرّبا) is a past verb, and (الألف) is the fāʿil; (قربانا) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (تقبّل) is a past verb in the passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو», i.e. the offering; (من أحد) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تقبّل), and (هما) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لم) is a particle of negation, jussive and conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning]; (يتقبّل) is an imperfect verb in the passive, jussive (majzūm), and the nāʾib fāʿil is «هو»; (من الآخر) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يتقبّل); (قال) is a past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو», i.e. the one from whom it was not accepted; (اللام) is the lām of the oath, for an implied (muqaddar) oath; (أقتلنّ) is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of nominative (marfūʿ), and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the verb is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «أنا» [Translator's note: so in the source, «والفعل»; evidently «والفاعل» (and the fāʿil) is meant]; (قال) is like the first, and the fāʿil is «هو», the one from whom it was accepted; (إنّما) is a restraining particle and the restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa), having no governing effect; (يتقبّل) is an imperfect verb, nominative; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (من المتّقين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يتقبّل), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «اتل عليهم» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «قرّبا …» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تقبّل …» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause قرّبا.
The clause «لم يتقبّل …» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause قرّبا.
The clause «قال …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أقتلنّك» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the implied oath … and the oath clause with its answer is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قال (the second) …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يتقبّل الله …» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying.

* Morphology:
(اتل): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion to suit the indeclinable form; its pattern is افع with a ḍamma on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
Comprehensive and exclusive speech (al-kalām al-jāmiʿ al-māniʿ): in the saying of the Exalted «إِنَّما يَتَقَبَّلُ اللَّهُ مِنَ الْمُتَّقِينَ». This sentence gathers many meanings in brief speech, for it contains the gist of the story from its beginning to its end. The summary of the meaning is that Allah the Exalted accepts obedience only from a God-fearing believer.

* Benefits:
The good soul and the hateful soul. 1 «فَتُقُبِّلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِما»: the verb is in the passive, its form indicating that the matter of acceptance or non-acceptance is entrusted to an unseen power and an unseen manner. This wording benefits us in two matters:
First: that we ourselves should not search for the manner of this acceptance nor delve into it, as the books of tafsīr delved into reports most likely taken from the legends of the "Old Testament".
Second: the suggestion that the one whose offering was accepted had no offence that would warrant resentment against him and plotting his killing; the matter was not in his hands, so there is no justification for the brother to hate his brother. The thought of killing is the furthest thing that occurs to an upright soul in this domain, the domain of worship and drawing near [to Allah].
2 «قالَ: لَأَقْتُلَنَّكَ»: this saying — with this emphasis that bespeaks insistence — appears jarring and provokes disapproval, because it arises without any cause, save that wicked, reprehensible feeling, the feeling of blind envy, which does not dwell in a good soul.

safi-cedvel:28-29.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) is the lām preparing for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa); (إن) is a jussive conditional particle; (بسطت) is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and (التاء) is a pronoun, fāʿil (agent); (إلى) is a preposition and (الياء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (بسطت); (يد) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (الكاف) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (اللام) is the lām of purpose (taʿlīl); (تقتل) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and (النون) is the nūn of protection, and (الياء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «أنت».
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقتلني) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (بسطت).
(ما) is negating, operating like ليس; (أنا) is a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as the noun of ما «[Note: If you make (ما) inoperative, then (أنا) is a mubtadaʾ (subject).]». (الباء) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (باسط) is genitive (majrūr) in form and accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of ما; (يدي) is the mafʿūl bihi of the active participle باسط, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) [Translator's note: printed «لياء» in the source] is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إليك) is like إليّ, attached to باسط; (لأقتلك) is like لتقتلني, and the fāʿil is «أنا».
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أقتلك) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to باسط.
(إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters), and (الياء) is a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of إنّ; (أخاف) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «أنا»; (الله) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (ربّ) is a naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty or a badal (substitute), accusative like it; (العالمين) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, since it is treated like the sound masculine plural.
The clause «بسطت …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تقتلني» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «ما أنا بباسط» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath … and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath.
The clause «أقتلك» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second particle relative (أن).
The clause «إنّي أخاف …» has no grammatical position, explaining the cause (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «أخاف الله …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
(29) (إنّي أريد) is like إنّي أخاف; (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (تبوء) is an imperfect verb, accusative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «أنت»; (بإثم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تبوء «[Note: Or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil, i.e. you return carrying it.]», and (الياء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) is a conjunction; (إثمك) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to إثمي, genitive like it, and (الكاف) is a muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تبوء) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being أريد.
(الفاء) is a conjunction; (تكون) is a defective imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (تبوء), and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «أنت»; (من أصحاب) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the khabar of تكون; (النار) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الواو) is resumptive; (ذلك) is a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address; (جزاء) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الظالمين) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «إنّي أريد …» has no grammatical position, a second explanation of cause.
The clause «أريد …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «تبوء …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «تكون …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تبوء …
The clause «ذلك جزاء …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(باسط): an active participle from the triliteral بسط; its pattern is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
The device of breadth (fann al-ittisāʿ): in the saying of the Exalted «إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ تَبُوءَ بِإِثْمِي وَإِثْمِكَ». It is that the speaker produces speech in which interpretation broadens according to what its words can bear, so that interpretation of it broadens in proportion to people's intellects and the differences in their understandings.
In the verse it lies in his wanting his brother's sin, because its meaning is: I do not want to kill you and then be punished.

safi-cedvel:30-30.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive; (طوّعت) is a past verb, and (التاء) is for the feminine; (اللام) is a preposition and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (طوّعت); (نفس) is the fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (قتل) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (أخي) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, since it is one of the five nouns, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (قتل) is like طوّع, and the fāʿil is «هو», and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (أصبح) is a defective past verb, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (من الخاسرين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the khabar (predicate) of أصبح, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «طوّعت له نفسه …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «قتله» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «أصبح من الخاسرين» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قتله.

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) vocative particle (أيّ) the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative, and (ها) is for alerting (tanbīh) (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, a badal (substitute) of أيّ or a naʿt (adjective) of it (آمنوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) (أوفوا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (بالعقود) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أوفوا), (أحلّت) passive past verb..
and (التاء) is for the feminine (اللام) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أحلّت), (بهيمة) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ) (الأنعام) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) (إلّا) particle of exception (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil) — i.e. «إلّا ما حرّم عليكم بحكم الآيات المتلوّة» (except what has been forbidden to you by the ruling of the verses recited) — [Note: the exception is connected because the animals forbidden in the recited verses are of the same kind as that from which the exception is made, in His saying (بهيمة الأنعام); so in the speech there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e.: «إلا محرّم ما يتلى عليكم» (except the forbidden [part] of what is recited to you).. Some have made it a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), according to the following account: in His saying (إلّا ما يتلى عليكم), if what is meant by it is what comes after it in His saying, Exalted is He, «حرّمت عليكم الميتة والدم ...»: [it is] a disconnected exception, إلا تختصّ الميتة وما ذكر معها بالظباء وخمر الوحش وبقرة [Translator's note: this clause is garbled in the source; it apparently means «إذ لا تختصّ الميتة وما ذكر معها بالظباء وحمر الوحش وبقره», i.e. "since carrion and what is mentioned with it are not specific to gazelles, wild asses and wild cattle"], so the verse becomes: «لكن ما يتلى عليكم أي تحريمه فهو محرّم» (but what is recited to you, i.e. its prohibition, is forbidden) ... etc.], (يتلى) passive imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the alif, and the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (it) (عليكم) like لكم, attached to (يتلى) (غير) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb), of the second-person pronoun in لكم (محلّي) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, and the nūn was dropped because of the iḍāfa (الصيد) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) (أنتم) detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) (حرم) khabar (predicate), nominative (إنّ) particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl), for emphasis (الله) the Divine Name, noun of إنّ, accusative (يحكم) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He) (ما) like the first, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (يريد) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa".
The clause «يأيّها الذين ...»: has no grammatical position, initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «آمنوا ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أوفوا ...»: has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative (resumptive).
The clause «أحلّت لكم بهيمة ...»: has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يتلى ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «أنتم حرم»: in the position of accusative, a ḥāl [Note: al-Zamakhsharī made this ḥāl [refer] to (محلّي الصيد), and Abū Ḥayyān rejected that, saying:
"We have shown the corruptness of this statement, in that livestock animals are permitted absolutely, not restricted by this ḥāl." End quote. So it is a ḥāl of the pronoun in لكم, with a second exception, i.e. «وإلّا الصيد وأنتم حرم» (and except game while you are in a state of iḥrām), because the meaning of (محلّي الصيد) is "game made lawful" (al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ, vol. 3, p. 413 ff.).].
The clause «إنّ الله يحكم ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يحكم ...»: in the position of nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «يريد»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).

* Morphology:
(أوفوا): it contains a weak-letter change by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf) to suit the indeclinable form; its original form is أوفيوا: the ḍamma was transferred from the yāʾ to the fāʾ, then the yāʾ was deleted because it and the wāw of the plural were both quiescent. Its pattern is أفعوا.
(العقود): plural of العقد, which is the abstract tie, meaning a covenant; it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of عقد يعقد, of the ḍaraba class, its pattern being فعل with fatḥa then sukūn; the pattern of العقود is الفعول with ḍamma on the fāʾ.
(بهيمة): a concrete (jāmid) noun for every creature with four legs; its pattern is فعيلة.
(محلّي): plural of محلّ, the active participle of the quadriliteral أحلّ; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(الصيد): the maṣdar of صاد يصيد, of the ḍaraba class.. It may have the meaning of المصيد, i.e. the passive participle; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(حرم): plural of حرام, an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) of the active participle, meaning محرم (one in iḥrām); its pattern is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ, and its plural is فعل with two ḍammas.

* Benefits:
A report about the philosopher al-Kindī: they mention that the philosopher al-Kindī's companions said to him: "O sage, make for us something like this Quran." He said: "Yes, I will make something like part of it." He secluded himself for many days, then came out and said: "By Allah, I am not able, and no one can bear this. I opened the Muṣḥaf and Sūrat al-Māʾida came out; I looked, and behold, it spoke of fulfilment and forbade breaking [of covenants], made a general permission, then made an exception, then told of His power and His wisdom in two lines. No one is able to produce this except in volumes."

safi-cedvel:84-84.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction. (ما) interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject). (اللام) preposition, and (نا) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. (لا) negative particle. (نؤمن) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being نحن. (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نؤمن). (الواو) conjunction. (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the Name of Majesty. (جاء) past verb, and (نا) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being هو, and it is the returning pronoun. (من الحق) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of جاء [Note: Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī explained the ayah in another way: (الواو) is circumstantial, (ما) is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ, and (من الحق) is the khabar, i.e. "What is with us that we do not believe in Allah, while the state is that what has come to us is from the Truth" — the Truth being Allah the Exalted, or the Noble Qur'an.], (الواو) conjunction. (نطمع) like نؤمن. (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle. (يدخل) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and (نا) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (ربّ) fāʿil, nominative, and (نا) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (مع) adverb of place, accusative, attached to (يدخل). (القوم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (الصالحين) naʿt (adjective) of القوم, genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يدخلنا) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition; the implied form is: نطمع في أن يدخلنا ربنا, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (نطمع).
The clause «ما لنا ...»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause answering the vocative [Note: or it is resumptive.].
The clause «لا نؤمن ..»: is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «جاءنا ...»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «نطمع ..»: is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause لا نؤمن [Note: with the verb taken as negated in meaning, i.e. "What is with us that we do not believe and do not hope?"].
The clause «يدخلنا ربنا ...»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).

safi-cedvel:85-85.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction. (أثاب) past verb, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (الباء) a preposition of causation. (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of the genitive.. and the returning pronoun is omitted.], (قالوا) past verb and its fāʿil. (جنات) second mafʿūl bihi, its governor being أثابهم, accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the kasra. (تجري) imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ. (من تحت) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تجري) [Note: or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الأنهار.], and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "from beneath its trees". (الأنهار) fāʿil, nominative. (خالدين) ḥāl, accusative, of the third-person pronoun in (أثابهم), and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ. (في) preposition, and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to خالدين. (الواو) resumptive. (ذلك) demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject) ... and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address. (جزاء) khabar (predicate), nominative. (المحسنين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما قالوا) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (أثابهم).
The clause «أثابهم الله ...»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause يقولون [Note: in ayah (83) of this surah.].
The clause «قالوا ...»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «تجري ... الأنهار»: is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of جنات.
The clause «ذلك جزاء ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

safi-cedvel:86-86.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject). (كفروا) past verb and its fāʿil (agent). (الواو) conjunction. (كذّبوا) like كفروا. (بآيات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كذّبوا). (أولئك) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ ... and the kāf is for address. (أصحاب) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ). (الجحيم) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr).
The clause «الذين كفروا ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «كذّبوا ...»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause كفروا, which is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
The clause «أولئك أصحاب ...»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين كفروا).

safi-cedvel:87-88.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) vocative particle. (أي) the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of the accusative, and (ها) a particle of alerting. (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, badal (substitute) of أي or a naʿt (adjective) of it. (آمنوا) past verb and its fāʿil (agent). (لا) prohibitive particle that puts into the jussive
[Translator's note: the source breaks off here and then repeats the i'rab from the beginning, as follows.]
I'rab:
(يا) vocative particle. (أي) the one addressed, an intended indefinite, indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of the accusative, and (ها) a particle of alerting. (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, badal of أي or a naʿt of it. (آمنوا) past verb and its fāʿil. (لا) prohibitive particle that puts into the jussive. (تحرموا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the sign of the jussive is the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is fāʿil. (طيبات) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the kasra. (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) [Note: or an indefinite noun that is described, in the position of the genitive; the clause after it is a naʿt, and the returning pronoun is omitted.], (أحلّ) past verb. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ). (اللام) preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أحلّ). (الواو) conjunction. (لا تعتدوا) like لا تحرّموا. (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (of inna and its sisters). (الله) the Name of Majesty, noun of inna, accusative. (لا) negative particle. (يحب) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو. (المعتدين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
The vocative clause «يأيها الذين ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لا تحرموا ...»: has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «أحل الله ...»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «لا تعتدوا»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause answering the vocative.
The clause «إن الله لا يحب ...»: has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «لا يحب ...»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna.
(88) (الواو) conjunction. (كلوا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is fāʿil. (من) preposition. (ما) relative noun [Note: or an indefinite noun that is described, in the position of the genitive; the clause after it is a naʿt, and the returning pronoun is omitted.] indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to (كلوا). (رزق) past verb, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (حلالا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the omitted object, i.e. رزقكم إياه الله [Note: it may be a mafʿūl bihi, i.e. "lawful food"; when the qualified noun was omitted, the adjective took its place (see ayah 168 of Surat al-Baqara).], (طيبا) naʿt, accusative. (الواو) conjunction. (اتقوا) like كلوا. (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الذي) relative noun in the position of the accusative, naʿt of the Name of Majesty. (أنتم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject). (الباء) preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (مؤمنون), which is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
The clause «كلوا ...»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the answer to the vocative.
The clause «رزقكم الله»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «اتقوا الله»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause كلوا ...
The clause «أنتم به مؤمنون»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).

safi-cedvel:89-89.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) negative particle. (يؤاخذ) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative. (باللغو) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يؤاخذ). (في أيمان) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to اللغو, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الواو) conjunction. (لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk) with no governing effect. (يؤاخذكم) like the first. (الباء) preposition. (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: or a relative noun whose returning pronoun is omitted, and the clause after it is its ṣila (relative clause).], (عقدتم) past verb and its fāʿil. (الأيمان) mafʿūl bihi.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما عقدتم) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (يؤاخذ).
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition. (كفارة) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (إطعام) khabar (predicate), nominative. (عشرة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (مساكين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa, since it is a diptote, being on the form of the furthest plurals (ṣīghat muntahā al-jumūʿ). (من أوسط) a preposition and its genitive noun, a naʿt (adjective) of a second object [Note: i.e. "feeding ten poor persons a sustenance from the average ..."], (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi. (تطعمون) imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is fāʿil. (أهلي) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ, since it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural; the nūn was deleted for the annexation, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (أو) a conjunction of choice. (كسوة) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to إطعام, nominative like it, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (أو تحرير) like أو كسوة. (رقبة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الفاء) resumptive. (من) a conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (لم) a particle of negation. (يجد) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو. (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (صيام) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being كفارته. (ثلاثة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (أيام) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (ذلك) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ ... the lām is for distance and the kāf for address. (كفارة) khabar, nominative. (أيمان) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (إذا) an adverb of future time stripped of condition, in the position of the accusative, attached to كفارة [Note: i.e. "that is the expiation of your oaths at the time of your swearing".], (حلفتم) like عقّدتم. (الواو) conjunction. (احفظوا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is fāʿil. (أيمان) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الكاف) preposition [Note: or a noun meaning مثل (like), in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) ... i.e. a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar.], (ذا) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq of the verb يبين; and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address. (يبين) like يؤاخذ. (الله) fāʿil, nominative. (اللام) preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يبين). (آيات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the kasra, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (لعل) a particle resembling the verb (of inna and its sisters), for hope (tarajjī), and (كم) the noun of laʿalla. (تشكرون) like تطعمون.
The clause «لا يؤاخذكم الله»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يؤاخذكم» (the second): has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «عقّدتم ...»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «كفارته إطعام ...»: the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you break your oath, then its expiation is feeding".
The clause «تطعمون ...»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «من لم يجد»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لم يجد ...»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: the khabar may be the two clauses of condition and apodosis together.].
The clause «(كفارته) صيام»: is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ذلك كفارة ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and the clause «حلفتم» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «احفظوا»: has no grammatical position, resumptive, ذلك كفارة [Note: it may be resumptive with no grammatical position.]. [Translator's note: the wording of the source here appears garbled; it is rendered as written.]
The clause «يبين الله»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لعلكم تشكرون»: has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «تشكرون»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of laʿalla.

* Morphology:
(إطعام), a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the quadriliteral verb أطعم; its pattern is أفعال, with kasra on the hamza of the verb and the addition of an alif before the last letter.
(أوسط), a derived adjective; its pattern is أفعل, and it may carry the meaning of the elative (tafḍīl).

* Benefits:
- The idle oath (yamīn al-laghw) is that which runs according to habit and does not carry within it intent and resolve ...
We see in the explicit text of the Noble Qur'an that this oath is disregarded and considered outside the scope of binding and solemn oaths. In this context we look toward considering the oath of divorce — which has become part of idle speech, sworn in situations of amusement and in contexts of jest and joking, and it may be to frighten the wife and warn her against some conduct that she or other members of the family may engage in, while it does not carry the intention and purpose of divorce — we look toward considering it idle speech and not taking it into account. And Allah is the Granter of success.

safi-cedvel:2-2.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab was given in the previous verse (لا) prohibitive, governing the jussive (تحلّوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) (شعائر) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) (الله) the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) (الواو) conjunction (لا) redundant (zāʾida), for emphasizing the negation (الشهر) conjoined to شعائر, accusative like it (الحرام) naʿt (adjective) of الشهر, accusative (الواو) conjunction in the three places (لا) redundant, for emphasizing the negation in the three places (الهدي، القلائد، آمّين) nouns conjoined to شعائر, accusative like it, the third being on the basis of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «قتال آمّين» (fighting those heading for) [Note: or «شعائر آمّين البيت» (the rites of those heading for the House), i.e. do not introduce in the months of Hajj anything by which you turn people away from Hajj.], and the sign of the accusative of this last one is the yāʾ (البيت) mafʿūl bihi of the active participle آمّين, accusative (الحرام) naʿt of البيت, accusative (يبتغون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (فضلا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (من ربّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt of (فضلا), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (رضوانا) conjoined to (فضلا), accusative like it (الواو) conjunction (إذا) adverb of future time containing the sense of condition, in the position of accusative, attached to the content of the apodosis, (حللتم) past verb and its fāʿil (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) (اصطادوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (الواو) conjunction (لا) prohibitive, governing the jussive (يجرمنّكم) imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of jussive. And (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (شنآن) fāʿil, nominative (قوم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (أن) maṣdar-forming particle (صدّوا) like آمنوا.. (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (عن المسجد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (صدّوكم), (الحرام) naʿt of المسجد, genitive like it.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن صدّوكم) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, namely the lām, i.e. «لصدّهم إياكم» (because of their turning you away), attached to (يجرمنّكم).
(أن) maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle (تعتدوا) imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تعتدوا) is in the position of accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of the verb يجرمنّكم [Note: it may be in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, i.e. «على الاعتداء عليهم» (to transgressing against them); the preposition is stated explicitly in verse (8) below.].
(الواو) conjunction (تعاونوا) like اصطادوا (على البرّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تعاونوا), (الواو) conjunction (التقوى) conjoined to البرّ, genitive like it, the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddara) on the alif (الواو) conjunction (لا تعاونوا) like لا تحلّوا — and one of the two tāʾs has been dropped from the verb — (على الإثم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تعاونوا), (الواو) conjunction (العدوان) conjoined to الإثم, genitive like it (الواو) conjunction (اتّقوا) like the first تعاونوا (الله) the Divine Name, mafʿūl bihi, accusative (إنّ) particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl) (الله) the Divine Name, noun of إنّ, accusative (شديد) khabar (predicate) of إنّ, nominative (العقاب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The vocative clause «يأيّها الذين ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لا تحلّوا ...»: has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
The clause «يبتغون ...»: in the position of accusative, a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in آمّين.
The clause «حللتم»: in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «اصطادوا»: has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «لا يجرمنّك شنآن ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the vocative.
The clause «صدّوكم»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «تعتدوا»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second particle-relative (أن).
The clause «تعاونوا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause that answers the vocative.
The clause «لا تعاونوا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تعاونوا.
The clause «اتّقوا الله»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تعاونوا.
The clause «إنّ الله شديد ...»: has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(شعائر): plural of شعيرة, a noun for the landmarks of the religion and its sanctities; the yāʾ of the singular was changed into a hamza in the plural; so its pattern in the singular is فعيلة, and in the plural فعائل.
(القلائد): plural of قلادة, a concrete (jāmid) noun; its pattern is فعالة with kasra on the fāʾ; the yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the third letter of قلادة is an alif] was changed into a hamza in the plural, so its pattern is فعائل.
(آمّين): plural of امّ [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently آمّ], the active participle of أمّ يؤمّ, of the naṣara class; its pattern is فاعل, and the ʿayn of the word was assimilated into its lām.
(اصطادوا): in the verb, the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form has been replaced by (طاء) because it comes after one of the velarized letters (aḥruf al-iṭbāq), namely the ṣād; its original form is اصتادوا; its pattern is افتعلوا.
(شنآن): the maṣdar (verbal noun) of شنأ يشنأ, of the fariḥa class; its pattern is فعلان with two fatḥas; if the nūn is made quiescent, it becomes an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha).
(تعتدوا): in it there is a weak-letter change by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf); its original form is تعتديوا: the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt to be heavy, so it was transferred to the dāl and the yāʾ was made quiescent, then it was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
(تعاونوا) the second: one of the two tāʾs was dropped from it; its original form is تتعاونوا; its pattern is تفاعلوا.

* Benefits:
The sacred month:
"The sacred month" means the sacred months, which are Rajab, Dhū al-Qaʿda, Dhū al-Ḥijja and al-Muḥarram.
Allah forbade fighting in them. The Arabs before Islam held them sacred, but they would tamper with them according to their whims, postponing them (yunsiʾūnahā) — i.e. deferring them — by the ruling of some soothsayers, from year to year.
When Islam came, it legislated their sanctity, and established this sanctity on the command of Allah from the day Allah created the heavens and the earth, as He said in [Sūrat] al-Tawba: «إِنَّ عِدَّةَ الشُّهُورِ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ اثْنا عَشَرَ شَهْراً فِي كِتابِ اللَّهِ يَوْمَ خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ مِنْها أَرْبَعَةٌ حُرُمٌ. ذلِكَ الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ», and He established that postponement (al-nasīʾ) is an increase in disbelief. Allah the Exalted has made clear the ruling on fighting in the sacred months in Sūrat al-Baqara.

safi-cedvel:119-119.t:
* I'rab:
(قال الله) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), (ها) a particle of calling attention (tanbīh), (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), (يوم) khabar (predicate), nominative, (ينفع) an imperfect verb, nominative, (الصادقين) a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ, (صدق) a postponed fāʿil, nominative, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar, (جنّات) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative, (تجري) like ينفع, and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, (من تحت) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تجري) [Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of الأنهار, and there is an omitted muḍāf in it, i.e. "from beneath its trees" ...], and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi, (الأنهار) the fāʿil of تجري, nominative, (خالدين) ḥāl, accusative, of the pronoun in (لهم), and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ, (في) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to خالدين, (أبدا) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to خالدين, (رضي) a past verb, indeclinable on the overt fatḥa, (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative, (عن) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (رضي), (الواو) conjunction, (رضوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, (عنه) like عنهم, attached to (رضوا), (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ ... and the lām is for distance and the kāf for address, (الفوز) khabar, nominative, (العظيم) naʿt (adjective), nominative.
The clause «قال الله ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «هذا يوم ...»: is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «ينفع ...»: is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «لهم جنّات ...»: has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of الصّادقين.].
The clause «تجري ... الأنهار». is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of جنّات.
The clause «رضي الله ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «رضوا عنه»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause رضي الله عنهم.
The clause «ذلك الفوز ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(صدقهم), an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb صدق يصدق, of the class of نصر; its pattern is فعل with kasra on the fāʾ. There are other maṣdars: صدق with fatḥa on the fāʾ, مصدوقة, and تصداق with fatḥa on the tāʾ.
(رضوا), it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is رضيوا, with ḍamma on the yāʾ. The ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made vowelless and the vowel was transferred to the ḍād; two vowelless letters met - the yāʾ and the wāw of the plural - so the yāʾ was deleted, and it became رضوا; its pattern is فعوا.

* Benefits:
1- Every noun of time that is vague and refers to the past may be annexed to the clause after it.
As for its i'rab, there is detail in it:
If what comes after it is indeclinable, making it indeclinable on the fatḥa is preferable, in harmony with the indeclinability. From that is the saying of al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī:
على حين عاتبت المشيب على الصبا ... وقلت ألّما أصح والشيب وازع
(At the time when I reproached grey hair over youthful passion, and said: "Have I not yet become sober, when grey hair is a restraint?")
In it there are two transmissions: one «على حين» in the genitive, declined, and the second «على حين» indeclinable on the fatḥa, which is preferable for correspondence with the indeclinability of the verb.
If what comes after it is a declinable verb or a nominal clause, declension is preferable, as occurs in the noble verse «هذا يَوْمُ يَنْفَعُ».

safi-cedvel:120-120.t:
* I'rab:
(لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate), (ملك) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), (السموات) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), (الواو) conjunction, (الأرض) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to السموات, genitive like it, (الواو) conjunction, (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative, conjoined to ملك, (في) a preposition and (هنّ) an attached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما, (الواو) conjunction, (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, (على كلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قدير), (شيء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, (قدير) khabar of the mubtadaʾ هو, nominative.
The clause «لله ملك ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «هو ... قدير»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.

safi-cedvel:53-53.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (يقول) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent) (آمنوا) a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma..
and the wāw is the fāʿil (الهمزة) for interrogation (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh) (أولاء) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) (الذين) a relative noun, khabar (predicate) (أقسموا) like آمنوا (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أقسموا), (جهد) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "striving" [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, being its kind.], (أيمان) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl), and (هم) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna (اللام) the lām of the oath [Translator's note: so in the source; elsewhere this lām after inna is called the shifted lām (al-muzaḥlaqa).] (مع) an adverb of place, accusative (manṣūb), attached to an omitted khabar of inna, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (حبطت) a past verb.. and (التاء) is for the feminine (أعمال) fāʿil, nominative, and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi (الفاء) conjunction (أصبحوا) a defective past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma.. and the wāw is the noun of aṣbaḥa (خاسرين) khabar, nominative [Translator's note: so in the source; خاسرين, as the khabar of أصبح, is accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.].
The clause «يقول الذين ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «هؤلاء الذين ...»: in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أقسموا ...»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إنهم لمعكم»: has no grammatical position, the response to the oath.
The clause «حبطت أعمالهم»: has no grammatical position, resumptive, and it is from the speech of Allah the Exalted, not from the speech of the believers.
The clause «أصبحوا خاسرين»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause حبطت أعمالهم.

* Morphology:
(جهد) an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb جهد يجهد, of the pattern-class (bāb) فتح, its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
The device of al-ighrāb wa-l-ṭurfa (the rare and the novel): in His saying, the Exalted, حَبِطَتْ أَعْمالُهُمْ فَأَصْبَحُوا خاسِرِينَ. It is of three kinds:
1- A kind in which the rarity is in the wording, and it is frequent. 2- A kind in which the rarity is in the meaning. 3- A kind in which the rarity is neither in its meaning nor in its outward wording, but in its interpretation; it is that which, if taken on its outward sense, the speech would be faulty, and if interpreted, the interpretation returns it to a mode of eloquent speech and removes the fault from its outward sense.
The noble verse is of this kind, for someone might say: the word «أصبحوا» ("they became in the morning") is outwardly padding (ḥashw) with no benefit in it, since those who are reported to be losers were in the evening in the same state as in the morning; and whenever you say: "the honey became sweet in the morning", the word أصبح is redundant, of the padding that has no benefit, because it was like that in the evening too. Al-Rummānī devised for this word an interpretation by which a great benefit is obtained which would not be obtained had it not come, namely that when He said [it] — since the sick person who has spent the night suffering severe pain has his state assessed in the morning, and if he wakes recovered and relieved of those pains, good is hoped for him and his recovery and healing from that illness are thought most likely, but if he wakes as he was in the evening, his perishing is certain.. On this basis the word «أصبحوا» has conveyed a fine and beautiful meaning, and has gone beyond being useless padding.
[Translator's note: the sentence "namely that when He said, since the sick person…" is broken in the source and is translated as written.]

* Benefits:
The hypocrites and the Jews..
This verse was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy and his companions, who were hastening to befriend the Jews and draw close to them, justifying that by saying they feared that some harm would befall them, meaning by that that the affair of Muḥammad ﷺ might not be completed and the matter would turn against them as it had been before Muḥammad ﷺ. We learn from this verse that the hypocrites are not to be counted on in anything nor relied upon in any matter, for they are wavering, scaremongering, fearful and agitated; they do not remain steady in any state, and they say what they do not do. They concealed disbelief and displayed Islam, and fought it in secret: وَإِذا خَلَوْا إِلى شَياطِينِهِمْ قالُوا إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ إِنَّما نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِؤُنَ.
So they are harder than the open enemy and more dangerous than others.

safi-cedvel:54-54.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (1) of this surah.], (من يرتدّ منكم) like من يتولّهم منكم [Note: In verse (51) of this surah.], (عن دين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يرتدّ), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (rābiṭa) (سوف) a particle of the future (يأتي) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (بقوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يأتي), (يحبّ) like يأتي, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (الواو) conjunction (يحبّون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (أذلّة) naʿt (adjective) of قوم, genitive (majrūr) like it (على المؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أذلّة, which has been made to carry the meaning of عاطفين ("tender"), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ (أعزّة) a second naʿt of قوم, genitive like it (على الكافرين) like على المؤمنين (يجاهدون) like يحبّون (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يجاهدون) (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (لا) negating (يخافون) like يحبّون (لومة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) (لائم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).. (and the lām) is for distance, and (الكاف) for address (فضل) khabar (predicate), nominative (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (يؤتي) like يأتي, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "huwa", i.e. Allah (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as second mafʿūl bihi (يشاء) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "huwa", i.e. Allah (الواو) resumptive (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative (واسع) khabar, nominative (عليم) second khabar, nominative.
The vocative clause «يأيّها الذين»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «من يرتدّ ...»: has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
The clause «يرتدّ ...»: in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.].
The clause «يأتي الله»: in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يحبّهم»: in the position of genitive as naʿt of قوم.
The clause «يحبّونه»: in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause يحبّهم.
The clause «يجاهدون ...»: in the position of genitive as another naʿt of قوم.
The clause «لا يخافون ...»: in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause يجاهدون [Note: The wāw may be circumstantial (ḥāliyya), the clause being in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يجاهدون.].
The clause «ذلك فضل الله»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يؤتيه ...»: in the position of nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذا [Note: Or in the position of accusative as ḥāl, or resumptive with no grammatical position.]..
The clause «يشاء»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «الله واسع ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(لومة), a maṣdar of single occurrence (maṣdar marra) from لام يلوم, of the pattern-class (bāb) نصر, its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(لائم), active participle of the three-letter verb لام, its pattern is فاعل. In it the wāw is changed to hamza because it comes after the alif of فاعل; its origin is لاوم, and this change is regular in every weak verb.

* Rhetoric:
Antithesis (ṭibāq): between أذلة and أعزّة..

* Benefits:
The joining of the apodosis with the fāʾ..
In this verse the apodosis is joined with the fāʾ in His saying, the Exalted: مَنْ يَرْتَدَّ مِنْكُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ. Here joining it with the fāʾ is obligatory because سوف occurs in the apodosis. Perhaps it is useful to mention the cases in which joining the apodosis with the fāʾ is obligatory. They are:
1- When the apodosis is a nominal clause, as in His saying, the Exalted, وَمَنْ كانَ فِي هذِهِ أَعْمى فَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ أَعْمى.
2- When the apodosis is a request clause (jumla ṭalabiyya) whose verb is an imperative, or an imperfect joined with the lām of command or the prohibitive lā, as in His saying, the Exalted, فَمَنْ كانَ يَرْجُوا لِقاءَ رَبِّهِ فَلْيَعْمَلْ عَمَلًا صالِحاً.
3- That the verb of the apodosis be non-inflecting (jāmid), as in our saying: إن أحسنت فعسى أن يحبك الناس ("If you do good, then perhaps people will love you").
4- That it be joined with (ما), as in our saying: إن عاقبت المسيء فما قصّرت ("If you punished the wrongdoer, you did not fall short").

safi-cedvel:55-55.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) a restraining particle and the restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa) (وليّ) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الله) the Name of Majesty, khabar (predicate), nominative (الواو) conjunction (رسول) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the Name of Majesty, nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative, conjoined to the Name of Majesty (آمنوا) a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) (الذين) like the first, a badal (substitute) of it — or a naʿt (adjective) of it — (يقيمون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (الصلاة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) (الواو) conjunction (يؤتون الزكاة) like يقيمون الصلاة (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) (هم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (راكعون) khabar, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «إنما وليّكم الله»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يقيمون ...»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يؤتون ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the second ṣila clause.
The clause «هم راكعون»: in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).

* Benefits:
Faith is what settles in the heart and is confirmed by deeds..
This verse indicates that faith is not a claim that the tongue sings about; rather it must have a backing in conduct and deeds so that it is a truthful claim. His saying, the Exalted, indicates this: وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكاةَ وَهُمْ راكِعُونَ ... So faith must have practical conduct that expresses it and is a proof of it, and in this there is a distinguishing of the believers from the hypocrites, who claim faith but do not keep up the prayer nor give the zakāt.

safi-cedvel:56-56.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction (من) a jussive-governing conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) (يتولّ) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) (الواو) conjunction in both places (رسول، الذين) two nouns conjoined to the Name of Majesty by the two conjunctions, following it in the accusative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (آمنوا) like the one given in the previous verse (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (rābiṭa) (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl) (حزب) the noun of inna, accusative (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) (هم) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ whose khabar is الغالبون, and the nominal clause is the khabar of inna.], (الغالبون) khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «من يتولّ ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause in the previous verse.
The clause «يتولّ الله ...»: in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.].
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إنّ حزب الله ...»: in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with the fāʾ [Note: Some hold that the apodosis clause is omitted, its implied form being "then He will help them and give them victory", and the mentioned nominal clause has the status of a causal explanation.].

* Morphology:
(يتولّ), in it there is weakening (iʿlāl) by deletion on account of the jussive; its pattern is يتفّع [Translator's note: so in the source; in verse 51 the same word is given the pattern يتفعّ.].
(حزب), a collective noun (ism jamʿ) that has no singular from its own wording; its plural is أحزاب, its pattern is فعل with kasra then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:90-90.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab has already been given [Note: in ayah (87) of this surah.], (إنما) a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa). (الخمر) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ). (الواو) conjunction, in the three places. (الميسر، الأنصاب، الأزلام) nouns conjoined to الخمر, nominative like it. (رجس) khabar (predicate), nominative. (من عمل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of رجس [Note: or attached to an omitted second khabar.], (الشيطان) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (الفاء) conjunction, linking the effect to the cause [Note: it may be linking the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you have believed and affirmed, then avoid it".], (اجتنبوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is fāʿil (agent), and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (لعلكم تفلحون) like لعلكم تشكرون [Note: in the previous ayah (89).].
The clause «يأيها الذين ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «الخمر ... رجس»: has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «اجتنبوه»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause answering the vocative.
The clause «لعلكم ...»: has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «تفلحون»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of laʿalla.

* Morphology:
(رجس), a noun for a foul and filthy deed; its pattern is فعل, with kasra then sukūn; fatḥa then sukūn, and fatḥa then kasra, are also valid.

safi-cedvel:91-91.t:
* I'rab:
(إنما) like the first [Note: in the previous ayah (90).], (يريد) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). (الشيطان) fāʿil (agent), nominative. (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle. (يوقع) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو. (بين) adverb of place, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of العداوة, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (العداوة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative. (الواو) conjunction. (البغضاء) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to العداوة, accusative. (في الخمر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يوقع), and في has the meaning of causation. (الواو) conjunction. (الميسر) maʿṭūf to الخمر, genitive (majrūr).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يوقع) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being يريد.
(الواو) conjunction. (يصدّ) imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (يوقع), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is هو. (عن ذكر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يصدّكم). (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الواو) conjunction. (عن الصلاة) like عن ذكر in i'rab and attachment. (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition. (هل) an interrogative particle containing the meaning of command. (أنتم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject). (منتهون) khabar (predicate), nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
The clause «يريد الشيطان»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يوقع ...»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «يصدّكم»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause that is the ṣila of the particle relative.
The clause «هل أنتم منتهون»: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if that has become clear to you, then will you desist?"

* Morphology:
(منتهون), an active participle from the five-letter verb انتهى, plural of المنتهي. In the plural there is iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is منتهيون, with ḍamma on the yāʾ. The ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made vowelless and the vowel was transferred to the hāʾ; then it was deleted because it met, vowelless, with the wāw of منتهون.

* Benefits:
1- إنما: its origin is إنّ, and the redundant «ما» entered upon it and restrained it from governing:
Its meaning differed from its origin, and it came to convey the affirmation and establishment of a thing in some way and, at the same time, the negation of anything else from it; this is what the rhetoricians called the meaning of «restriction» (ḥaṣr).
Sībawayh has words on this matter; he says:
«Know that the place in which «أنّ» is not permissible is not one in which «إنما» occurs.» Kuthayyir said:
أراني ولا كفران لله إنما ... أواخي من الأقوام كل بخيل
(I see myself — and there is no ingratitude to Allah — befriending, of all peoples, only every miser.)
Note: when the redundant ما enters inna and its sisters, their restriction to nouns is removed, so they enter both the nominal and the verbal clause alike, with the exception of «ليت», which keeps its restriction to nouns.
Important note: if the «ما» attached to these particles is a relative noun or a maṣdar-forming particle, it does not restrain them from governing; rather they remain putting the noun in the accusative and the predicate in the nominative. An example of the relative ما is His saying: ما عِنْدَكُمْ يَنْفَدُ, i.e. "that which is with you runs out". If the «maṣdar-forming ما» follows it, what comes after it is interpreted as a maṣdar in the accusative as the noun of «إن», as in «إن ما تستقيم حسن», i.e. "your being upright is good". In these two cases ما is written separately, unlike the restraining ما, which is written joined, as we learned in what preceded. Something similar has already come up with us in earlier ayahs, so one may refer back to it.
2- The basic use of «هل» is as an interrogative particle, and it is used to ask only in the case of «affirmation», as in: هل قرأت النحو؟ (Have you studied grammar?). Most often a verb follows it, and rarely a noun follows it, as in your saying «هل عليّ مجتهد»؟ (Is ʿAlī diligent?). When it enters the imperfect, it specifies it for the future.
Important note: «هل» may depart from its basic use as an interrogative particle and be for command or prohibition, as occurs in this ayah: «فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُنْتَهُونَ»؟, and for reproach and denunciation and other matters that you will find in the lengthy works of ʿilm al-maʿānī in rhetoric, if you wish more of that.

safi-cedvel:92-92.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction. (أطيعوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is fāʿil (agent). (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (الواو) conjunction. (أطيعوا الرسول) like أطيعوا الله. (الواو) conjunction. (احذروا) like أطيعوا. (الفاء) conjunction. (إن) a conditional particle that puts into the jussive. (توليتم) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the jussive, protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) ... (وتم) a pronoun, fāʿil. (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (اعلموا) like أطيعوا. (أنما) a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa). (على رسول) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) placed first, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (البلاغ) mubtadaʾ (subject) placed later, nominative (marfūʿ). (المبين) naʿt (adjective) of البلاغ, nominative.
The clause «أطيعوا ...»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the previous resumptive clause.
The clause «أطيعوا» (the second): has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the first clause أطيعوا.
The clause «احذروا»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the first clause أطيعوا.
The clause «توليتم ...»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the first clause أطيعوا.
The clause «اعلموا»: is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ ... and in the speech there is concision by omission (ījāz ḥadhf), i.e. "as for your recompense, it is upon Us ...".
The clause «على رسولنا البلاغ»: is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the verb اعلموا, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by (أما). [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in the ayah is أنما.]

safi-cedvel:93-93.t:
* I'rab:
(ليس) an inert (jāmid) defective past verb (of kāna and its sisters). (على) preposition. (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of laysa, placed first. (آمنوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is a pronoun in the position of the nominative, fāʿil (agent). (الواو) conjunction. (عملوا) like آمنوا. (الصالحات) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the kasra. (جناح) noun of laysa, placed later, nominative (marfūʿ). (في) preposition. (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to جناح. (طعموا) like آمنوا. (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, in the position of the accusative, attached to the implied apodosis [Note: the implied form is: إذا ما اتقوا لا يأثمون (when they are mindful, they do not incur sin). The adverb may also be stripped of condition, and then it is attached to what the previous clause indicates, i.e. "they do not incur sin at the time of their mindfulness".], (ما) redundant (zāʾida). (اتقوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was deleted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters ... and the wāw is fāʿil. (الواو) conjunction. (آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات) like the first. (ثم) conjunction, in the two places. (اتقوا وآمنوا، اتقوا وأحسنوا) like the previous اتقوا وآمنوا. (الواو) resumptive. (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (يحبّ) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو. (المحسنين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
The clause «ليس» with its noun and its khabar: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ...»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause آمنوا.
The clause «طعموا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «اتقوا»: is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is implied, i.e. لا يأثمون (they do not incur sin).
The clause «آمنوا» (the second): is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause اتقوا.
The clause «عملوا» (the second): is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause اتقوا.
The clause «اتقوا» (the second): is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause عملوا الصالحات.
The clause «آمنوا» (the third): is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the second clause اتقوا.
The clause «اتقوا» (the third): is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the third clause آمنوا.
The clause «أحسنوا»: is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the third clause اتقوا.
The clause «الله يحب ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يحب المحسنين»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).

* Rhetoric:
1- Takrār or takrīr (repetition): in His saying «إِذا مَا اتَّقَوْا», His saying «ثُمَّ اتَّقَوْا وَآمَنُوا» and His saying «ثُمَّ اتَّقَوْا وَأَحْسَنُوا». That is to emphasize what is being spoken about so that it becomes more firmly rooted in the mind, and as an indication of the relationships to which a person is bound in his life: the relationship of a person with himself, the relationship of a person with others, and the relationship of a person with his Lord; for that reason He followed it with iḥsān (excellence) the third time.

* Benefits:
Among the occasions of revelation:
«لَيْسَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ جُناحٌ فِيما طَعِمُوا»: this ayah was revealed as an answer to those who inquired about the fate of the one who drank wine and consumed gains of gambling before the prohibition.
So this ayah was revealed lifting the sin from them on condition of mindfulness (taqwā) and on condition of faith.

safi-cedvel:94-94.t:
* I'rab:
يأيّها الذين آمنوا: its i'rab has already been given [Note: in ayah (87) of this surah.], (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath. (يبلونّ) imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.. and the nūn is the nūn of emphasis, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (بشيء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يبلونّ). (من الصيد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of شيء. (تنال) imperfect verb, nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (أيدي) fāʿil, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الواو) conjunction. (رماح) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to أيدي, nominative like it, and (كم) muḍāf ilayhi. (اللام) the lām of causation (taʿlīl). (يعلم) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (من) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi. (يخافه) like تناله. (بالغيب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يخاف or of its object.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يعلم) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (بيلونّكم) [Translator's note: so in the source, for ليبلونّكم].
(الفاء) conjunction. (من) a conditional noun that puts into the jussive, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject). (اعتدى) past verb, indeclinable on the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, in the position of the jussive, protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو. (بعد) adverb of time, accusative, attached to (اعتدى). (ذا) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi, and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address. (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (اللام) preposition and (الكاف) for address. (الفاء) linking the apodosis. [Translator's note: the preceding words are repeated in the source in garbled form.] (اللام) preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) placed first. (عذاب) mubtadaʾ placed later, nominative. (أليم) naʿt, nominative.
The clause «يأيّها الذين ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ليبلونّكم»: has no grammatical position, being the answer to an implied oath.. and the oath with its answer has no position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «تناله أيديكم»: is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of الصيد.
The clause «يعلم الله»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «يخافه ...»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «من اعتدى ...»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause answering the vocative.
The clause «اعتدى ...»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: the khabar may be the two clauses of condition and apodosis together.].
The clause «له عذاب»: is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(رماح), plural of رمح, an underived (jāmid) noun; a verb رمح يرمح, of the class of فتح, has been heard derived from it, meaning "he struck him with the spear". Its pattern is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn, and the plural is فعال, with kasra on the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
1- Tankīr (indefiniteness): in His saying «لَيَبْلُوَنَّكُمُ اللَّهُ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الصَّيْدِ». The indefiniteness of شيء is for belittling, signalling that this is not one of the tremendous trials in which the feet of the firmly grounded slip, such as being tested with the killing of souls and the destruction of wealth. Rather, it is of the kind with which the people of Ayla were tested regarding the game of the sea. Its benefit is to draw attention to the fact that whoever does not stand firm in something like this, how will he stand firm amid severe trials?

* Benefits:
- The believer often asks:
How does Allah test His servants when He knows best their condition — He knows their believer and their disbeliever, knows their truthful and their hypocrite, knows their righteous from their wicked, and knows among them the reformer from the corrupter? And likewise the ayahs that touch on Allah's knowledge, such as His saying in this ayah: «لِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَخافُهُ بِالْغَيْبِ».
The jurists and exegetes have views about this; we will review some of them, and the strongest?
The author of «al-Jalālayn» said: what is meant by Allah's knowing, occurring in ayahs like these, is «that He may know with the knowledge of manifestation» (ʿilm ẓuhūr). The purpose of the knowledge of manifestation is to establish the proof against the servants, lest they be taken — as they would claim — unjustly, without Allah subjecting them to examination and testing.

safi-cedvel:3-3.t:
* I'rab:
(حرّمت) passive past verb.. and (التاء) is for the feminine (على) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (حرمت), (الميتة) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ) (الواو) conjunction in the ten following places (الدم، لحم) two nouns conjoined to الميتة, nominative like it (الخنزير) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative, conjoined to الميتة (أهلّ) passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (it) (لغير) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أهلّ) (الله) the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الباء) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أهلّ), (المنخنقة، الموقوذة، المتردّية، النطيحة) nouns conjoined to الميتة, nominative like it (ما) like the first (أكل) past verb (السبع) fāʿil (agent), nominative (إلّا) particle of exception (ما) like the first, in the position of accusative as the excepted (ذكّيتم) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (تم) is the fāʿil (ما ذبح على النصب) like ما أهلّ لغير الله (أن) maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle (تستقسموا) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (بالأزلام) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تستقسموا).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقتسموا..) [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic word is تستقسموا] is in the position of nominative, conjoined to الميتة.
