(ذا) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address (فسق) khabar (predicate), nominative (اليوم) adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative, attached to (يئس), which is an imperfect verb, nominative [Translator's note: so in the source; يئس is a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa] (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as fāʿil (كفروا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (من دين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يئس), and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition (لا) prohibitive, governing the jussive (تخشوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (الواو) conjunction (اخشوا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (النون) is [the nūn] of protection (wiqāya), and the object of اخشوا is omitted, namely the first-person pronoun, i.e.: اخشوني (fear Me). (اليوم) like the first, attached to (أكملت), which is a past verb and its fāʿil (لكم) like عليكم, attached to (أكملت), (دين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (كم) muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (أتممت عليكم نعمتي) like أكملت لكم دينكم (الواو) conjunction (رضيت) like أكملت (لكم) like عليكم, attached to (رضيت) [Note: it may be attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of الإسلام.], (الإسلام) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (دينا) ḥāl, accusative, of الإسلام [Note: if the verb رضيت is given the implied sense of صيّرت and جعلت (I made), then دينا is its second object.].
The clause «حرّمت ... الميتة»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أهلّ ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (ما).
The clause «أكل السبع»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
The clause «ذكّيتم»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the third relative noun (ما).
The clause «ذبح على النصب»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the fourth relative noun (ما).
The clause «تستقسموا ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «ذلكم فسق»: has no grammatical position, causal and resumptive.
The clause «يئس الذين ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كفروا»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لا تخشوهم»: in the position of jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. «إن يظهروا عليكم فلا تخشوهم» (if they prevail over you, then do not fear them).
The clause «اخشون»: in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause فلا تخشوهم.
The clause «أكملت ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أتممت ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أكملت.
The clause «رضيت ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أكملت.
(الفاء) resumptive (من) conditional noun governing the jussive, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (اضطرّ) passive past verb, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he) (في مخمصة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of the nāʾib fāʿil (غير) second ḥāl, accusative (متجانف) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (لإثم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to متجانف (الفاء) linking the apodosis (إنّ) particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl) (الله) the Divine Name, noun of إنّ, accusative (غفور) khabar of إنّ, nominative, (رحيم) second khabar, nominative.
The clause «من اضطّر ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «اضطّر ...»: in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: the khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «إنّ الله غفور ...»: in the position of jussive, the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ [Note: this clause is in reality a causal explanation of the implied apodosis.. the implied form being: «فمن اضطر فلا يخش عقابا لأن الله غفور رحيم» (whoever is compelled, let him not fear punishment, because Allah is Forgiving, Merciful).].

* Morphology:
(المنخنقة): active participle of the five-letter verb انخنق; it is the feminine, its masculine being المنخنق; its pattern is منفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.. It is the animal that died by strangling.
(الموقوذة): passive participle of the verb وقذ يقذ, of the ḍaraba class, meaning to fell or to beat until death; the masculine is موقوذ, on the pattern مفعول.
(المتردّية): feminine of التردّي [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently المتردّي], active participle of the five-letter تردّى يتردّى; its pattern is متفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the doubled ʿayn.
(النطيحة): a derived adjective, the feminine of النطيح, فعيل in the sense of مفعول, from the triliteral نطح.
(السبع): a concrete (jāmid) noun for every animal with fangs; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then ḍamma.
(النصب): a concrete noun for what is worshipped besides Allah; its pattern is فعل with two ḍammas, and the ʿayn may be made quiescent; its plural is أنصاب.
(الأزلام): plural of زلم, with fatḥa or ḍamma on the zāy and fatḥa on the lām, which is القدح with kasra on the qāf; a concrete noun for an arrow without feathers or head.
(فسق): an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of فسق يفسق, of the naṣara class, the ḍaraba class and the karuma class; its pattern is فعل with kasra then sukūn.
(مخمصة): a mīmī maṣdar of the verb خمص يخمص البطن, of the fataḥa class, the fariḥa class and the karuma class, meaning [the belly] became empty and shrank; its pattern is مفعلة with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn.
(متجانف): active participle of تجانف, meaning "to incline"; its pattern is متفاعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Benefits:
النطيحة is a word on the pattern فعيلة. An adjective on the pattern فعيل, when it has the meaning of مفعول, does not take the feminine tāʾ, so masculine and feminine are the same in it; we say امرأة جريح (a wounded woman) and رجل جريح (a wounded man) — this when it is preceded by a qualified noun or there is a contextual indication of it. But if that is absent, it takes the feminine tāʾ, so we say في الميدان ستة جرحى وقتيلة (on the field there are six wounded and one slain woman). There are four other forms in which masculine and feminine are the same when describing, namely:
1- The pattern فعول in the sense of فاعل, such as: رجل صبور وامرأة صبور (a patient man and a patient woman).
2- The pattern مفعال: such as مهذار (one who babbles much), معطار (one who perfumes oneself much), and مقوال, i.e. eloquent; so we say رجل مقوال وامرأة مقوال.
3- The pattern مفعيل, such as: رجل معطير or امرأة معطير, i.e. one who perfumes herself much.
4- The pattern مفعل: رجل مغشم وامرأة مغشم, i.e. one whom nothing deters..
An important benefit: masculine and feminine are the same in maṣdars when they are used as descriptions, so we say: هذا قول حق (this is a true statement) and تلك قضية حق (that is a true matter). Some people deviated and added the tāʾ to maṣdars when the qualified noun is feminine, saying: قضية حقة. This is a common error that should be avoided.

safi-cedvel:31-31.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is a conjunction; (بعث) is a past verb; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (غرابا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (يبحث) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يبحث); (اللام) is the lām of purpose (taʿlīl); (يري) is an imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو», i.e. the crow «[Note: The pronoun may refer to Allah, in which case the preposition phrase is attached to the verb بعث.]», and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (كيف) is an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), its governor being يواري; (يواري) is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is «هو», and it is the owner of the ḥāl; (سوءة) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (أخيه) is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and likewise the pronoun.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يريه) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (يبحث).
(قال) is like بعث, and the fāʿil is «هو»; (يا) is a particle of vocative and lament; (ويلتا) is the one addressed in lament, a muḍāf, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the tāʾ, its appearance prevented by the place being occupied by the fitting vowel; (الألف), converted from the yāʾ, is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الهمزة) is for the interrogative of wonder; (عجزت) is a past verb indeclinable on the sukūn, and (التاء) is a pronoun, fāʿil; (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (أكون) is a defective imperfect verb, accusative, and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «أنا»; (مثل) is the khabar (predicate) of أكون, accusative; (ها) is a particle of alerting; (ذا) is a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (الغراب) is a badal (substitute) of ذا, following it in the genitive.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أكون) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, its implied form being «عن أن أكون» … attached to (عجزت).
(الفاء) is a conjunction; (أواري) is an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أكون «[Note: Al-Zamakhsharī made the verb accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ, and Ibn Hishām explicitly declared him wrong in that … see Shudhūr al-Dhahab, p. 370, 3rd ed.
(2, 3) In the previous verse (30).]», and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «أنا»; (سوءة أخي) is like سوءة أخيه, the sign of the genitive of أخي being the kasra implied on the letter before the yāʾ; (الفاء) is resumptive; (أصبح من النادمين) is like أصبح من الخاسرين «2».
The clause «بعث الله …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أصبح … «3».
The clause «يبحث …» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (غرابا).
The clause «يريه …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «يواري …» is in the position of accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of (يريه) «[Note: The seeing is visual; the hamza made the verb take two objects, and the interrogative suspended (ʿallaqa) the verb of seeing.]».
The clause «قال …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «of lament and its answer» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «عجزت» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the lament.
The clause «أكون …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «أواري …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أكون.
The clause «أصبح من النادمين» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(سوءة): a noun for an ugly deed or ugly thing, derived from ساء يسوء الشيء, "the thing was ugly"; its pattern is فعلة, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(الغراب): a generic noun denoting the well-known bird, and the (ال) in it is for prior reference (ʿahdiyya); its pattern is فعال.
(النادمين): plural of النادم, an active participle from the triliteral ندم; its pattern is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative usage (majāz): in the saying of the Exalted «يا وَيْلَتى», because he addressed what does not possess reason, while the basis of the vocative is that it be for one who possesses reason.

* Benefits:
The saying of the Exalted: «قالَ يا وَيْلَتى أَعَجَزْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِثْلَ هذَا الْغُرابِ فَأُوارِيَ سَوْأَةَ أَخِي».
What Ibn Hishām stated regarding the i'rab of (فأواري):
Al-Zamakhsharī's statement on the saying of the Exalted «فَأُوارِيَ» that أواري is accusative as the answer to the interrogative (i.e. by the implied أن after the fāʾ of causation preceded by an interrogative) is unsound. The reason for its unsoundness is that the answer to a condition is caused by it, and the concealing is not caused by the inability; rather it is accusative by conjunction to (أكون). For this reason the accusative of (تصبح) was disallowed in the saying of the Exalted «أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَتُصْبِحُ الْأَرْضُ مُخْضَرَّةً», because the earth's becoming green is not caused by seeing the sending down of the rain but by the sending down itself. Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī supported Ibn Hishām's view and said:
Do you not see that your saying «أين بيتك فأزورك» means "if I knew, I would visit", whereas the meaning here is not "if I were unable, I would conceal". That is a sound and well-grounded view, as is evident.
[Translator's note: al-ʿUkbarī (d. 616 AH) predates Ibn Hishām (d. 761 AH); the source's wording that he "supported Ibn Hishām's view" is translated as written.]

safi-cedvel:32-32.t:
* I'rab:
(من أجل) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (كتبنا); (ذلك) is a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address; (كتبنا) is a past verb indeclinable on the sukūn, and (نا) is a pronoun, fāʿil (agent); (على بني) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (كتبنا), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, since it is treated like the sound masculine plural; (إسرائيل) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, since it is a diptote; (أنّ) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters), and (الهاء) is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), indeclinable, in the position of accusative as the noun of أنّ; (من) is a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (قتل) is a past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (نفسا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (بغير) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (قتل); (نفس) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (أو) is a conjunction; (فساد) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to نفس, genitive, i.e. «غير فساد»; (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to a naʿt (adjective) of فساد.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه من قتل …) is in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of (كتبنا).
(الفاء) is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (كأنّما) is a restraining particle and the restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa), having no governing effect; (قتل) is a past verb, and the fāʿil is «هو»; (الناس) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (جميعا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of الناس; (الواو) is a conjunction; (من أحياها … جميعا) is like its counterpart above; (الواو) is resumptive; (اللام) is the lām of the oath, for an implied (muqaddar) oath; (قد) is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); (جاء) is a past verb, and (التاء) is the feminine tāʾ; (رسل) is the fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), and (نا) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (بالبيّنات) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (جاء) «[Note: It may be attached to an omitted ḥāl of رسل.]»; (ثمّ) is a conjunction; (إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb; (كثيرا) is the noun of إنّ, accusative; (من) is a preposition and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt of (كثيرا); (بعد) is an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (مسرفون); (ذلك) is like the first; (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (مسرفون); (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), conveying emphasis «[Note: Since the clause has the status of the answer to the oath, being conjoined to the answer to the oath, the lām had to come on the khabar (predicate), because it is the lām of the oath.
(3, 4) The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and its apodosis together.]»; (مسرفون) is the khabar of إنّ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «كتبنا …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «من قتل نفسا» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «قتل نفسا» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «3».
The clause «كأنّما قتل الناس» is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «من أحياها» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause من قتل …
The clause «أحياها» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «4».
The clause «كأنّما أحيا الناس» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «قد جاءتهم رسلنا» has no grammatical position, being the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «إنّ كثيرا … مسرفون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the oath.

* Morphology:
(أحيا): the alif is written in the form of the tall alif even though it is the fourth letter, because it is preceded by a yāʾ.
(مسرفون): plural of مسرف, an active participle from the quadriliteral أسرف; its pattern is مفعل with a ḍamma on the mīm and a kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
Representative simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī): in the noble verse, in the saying of the Exalted «فَكَأَنَّما قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً» …
The basis of the simile is the two acts sharing in the violation of the sanctity of blood, defiance of Allah the Exalted, and audacity in killing, in entailing retaliation and bringing on the great wrath of Allah the Exalted.
The benefit of the simile: deterring and restraining from killing a single soul by depicting it in the image of killing all people, and encouraging and urging the saving of it by depicting it in the image of saving all people.

safi-cedvel:33-33.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) is a restraining particle and the restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa), having no governing effect; (جزاء) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (الذين) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (يحاربون) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الله) is the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) is a conjunction; (رسول) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Name of Majesty, accusative, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) is a conjunction; (يسعون) is like يحاربون; (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يسعون); (فسادا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), interpreted as a derived word, i.e. «مفسدين» «[Note: It may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) … It may also be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. they strive for the sake of corruption.]»; (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (يقتّلوا) is an imperfect verb in the passive, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (أو) is a conjunction; (يصلّبوا) is like يقتّلوا; (أو) is a conjunction; (تقطّع) is an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (يقتّلوا), and it is in the passive; (أيدي) is the nāʾib fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the yāʾ, and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) is a conjunction; (أرجلهم) is conjoined to أيديهم, nominative, and a muḍāf ilayhi; (من خلاف) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to a ḥāl of the hands and feet, i.e. «مختلفة» (on opposite sides); (أو) is a conjunction; (ينفوا) is like يقتّلوا; (من الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ينفوا); (ذلك) is a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address; (اللام) is a preposition and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted ḥāl of خزي — an adjective placed before the noun it qualifies; (خزي) is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ذلك, nominative «[Note: The preposition and its genitive noun (لهم) may be a fronted khabar and (خزي) a postponed mubtadaʾ, the clause being the khabar of the demonstrative ذلك.]»; (في الدنيا) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to a naʿt (adjective) of خزي, the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied on the alif; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لهم) is like the first, attached to an omitted ḥāl of عذاب «[Note: Or attached to an omitted fronted khabar, with (عذاب) a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause [Translator's note: printed «والحملة» in the source] is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the preceding clause لهم خزي.]»; (في الآخرة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to a second ḥāl of عذاب — an adjective placed before the noun it qualifies; (عذاب) is conjoined to خزي by the wāw, nominative like it; (عظيم) is a naʿt of عذاب, nominative. The interpreted maṣdar (أن يقتّلوا) is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ جزاء.
The clause «جزاء الذين …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يحاربون …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «يسعون …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «يقتّلوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «يصلّبوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يقتّلوا.
The clause «تقطع أيديهم …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يصلّبوا.
The clause «ينفوا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تقطّع أيديهم.
The clause «ذلك … خزي» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(فسادا): it occurs in the verse as a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) of the verb أفسد, or as an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb فسد (verse 205 of Surat al-Baqara).
(يسعون): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is يسعاون. The alif came quiescent before the quiescent plural wāw, so it was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescents, and the letter before the wāw was given a fatḥa to indicate the deleted alif, so it became يسعون; its pattern is يفعون with a fatḥa on the ʿayn. The deleted alif is originally a yāʾ, because the maṣdar is السعي.
(خلاف): an aurally transmitted maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb خالف, in the sense of the active participle, i.e. المختلف (opposite), i.e. a right hand and a left foot, and vice versa. Its pattern is فعال with a kasra on the fāʾ.
(ينفوا): it contains iʿlāl by deletion following the course of يسعون, where the alif was deleted from it before the plural wāw; its pattern is يفعوا with a ḍamma on the yāʾ and a fatḥa on the ʿayn, because it is passive.

* Benefits:
1- The saying of the Exalted: «إِنَّما جَزاءُ الَّذِينَ يُحارِبُونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ». إنما is parsed as a restraining particle and the restrained particle, because (ما), when it enters on inna and its sisters, restrains them from operating, and what follows it is parsed as mubtadaʾ and khabar. A verb may follow it, as in the saying of the Exalted: «إِنَّما يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبادِهِ الْعُلَماءُ». As for ليت, when (ما) enters on it, it may be made operative or inoperative, because a verb does not follow it. On this basis the grammarians allowed the nominative and the accusative in the word الحمام occurring in the verse of al-Nābigha, it being a badal (substitute) of هذا, in his saying:
قالت: ألا ليتما هذا الحمام لنا.
(She said: "Would that these doves were ours.")
As for the meaning, it conveys restriction (ḥaṣr), as in the saying of the Exalted: «إِنَّما أَنْتَ مُنْذِرٌ». One must pay attention and distinguish between the restraining ما and the relative ما meaning الذي. The restraining ما is written joined to inna and its sisters, whereas the relative ما is written separate from it and does not restrain it from operating, as in the saying of the Exalted:
«إِنَّما تُوعَدُونَ لَصادِقٌ».
[Translator's note: the source prints this example joined («إِنَّما»), although it cites it as an instance of the separately written relative ما.]
2- The punishment of those who spread corruption in the land. أو in this verse is for specification (bayān), not for choice. This is the second report from Ibn ʿAbbās, and it is the view of most scholars, because the rulings differ, so these punishments were arranged according to the order of the crimes. This is as reported from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning highway robbers; he said: If they kill and take property, they are killed and crucified; if they kill and do not take property, they are killed; if they take property and do not kill, their hands and feet are cut off on opposite sides (i.e. differing), so the right hand and the left foot are cut off; and if they terrorize the road and neither kill nor take property, they are banished from the land. This is the view of Qatāda, al-Awzāʿī, al-Shāfiʿī and the people of opinion (aṣḥāb al-raʾy). They differed about the manner of crucifixion. It was said: he is crucified alive, then pierced in his belly with a spear until he dies. Al-Shāfiʿī said: he is first killed and prayed over, then crucified on the road where people pass, so that it may be a deterrent to others. They differed about the interpretation of banishment from the land. It was said that the imam pursues them, and from every land in which they are found they are banished; this is the view of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz. It was said: they are pursued until the ḥadd punishments are carried out on them; this is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Layth and al-Shāfiʿī. Abū Ḥanīfa and the people of Kufa said: banishment is imprisonment, because prison is a cutting off from the world and its pleasures, a rooting out of the wicked and a riddance of their corruption. And Allah knows best.

safi-cedvel:34-34.t:
* I'rab:
(إلّا) is a particle of exception; (الذين) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as the excepted (mustathnā); (تابوا) is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); (من قبل) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (تابوا); (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (تقدروا) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (على) is a preposition and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تقدروا).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقدروا) is in the position of genitive by the annexation of قبل to it.
(الفاء) is explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya) — or redundant (zāʾida) «[Note: Al-ʿUkbarī allowed the exception to be disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) with (إلّا) meaning لكن, the relative being a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the clause اعلموا, the fāʾ having been added to the khabar because the relative resembles a condition.]» —; (اعلموا) is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (أنّ) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters), for emphasis; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, the noun of أنّ, accusative; (غفور) is the khabar, nominative (marfūʿ); (رحيم) is a second khabar, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله غفور …) stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا.
The clause «تابوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «تقدروا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «اعلموا …» has no grammatical position, being an explanation of cause for something implied (muqaddar), i.e. «هؤلاء المستثنون تقبل توبتهم لأنّ الله غفور رحيم» «[Note: Or it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. «فإن تقبلوا توبتهم فاعلموا أنّ الله غفور».]».

* Benefits:
The door of mercy, repentance and forgiveness. This verse opens the door of repentance and turning back from error, specifying that those who repent before the capacity to punish them and arrest them are saved from the rulings of the previous verse. Most of the exegetes said that what is meant by this exception is the warring polytheist: that if he repents, believes and reforms, nothing of the preceding punishments is demanded of him. Al-Sindī said: As for the warring Muslim, if he repents before he is overpowered, he is like the disbeliever: nothing is demanded of him, unless a specific property is found with him, in which case he returns it to its owners. This is the school of Mālik and al-Awzāʿī; except that Mālik said: he is held liable for blood if its guardian demands it; but as for whatever blood and property he took that their guardians do not demand, the imam does not pursue him for any of that. This was the ruling of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib concerning Ḥāritha ibn Zayd. Al-Shāfiʿī said: by his repentance the ḥadd of Allah is lifted from him, but what belongs to the rights of the children of Adam is not lifted from him by it. As for when he repents after he has been overpowered, the apparent sense of the verse is that the repentance does not benefit him and the ḥadd punishments are carried out on him; and al-Shāfiʿī said: it is possible that every ḥadd belonging to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is lifted by repentance.

safi-cedvel:57-58.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) a vocative particle (أيّ) the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of accusative [Note: And (ها) is for alerting, with no grammatical position.] (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as badal (substitute) of أيّ or naʿt (adjective) of it (آمنوا) a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing (لا تتخذوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn..
and the wāw is the fāʿil (الذين) like the first, in the position of accusative as first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (اتّخذوا) like آمنوا (دين) first mafʿūl bihi, its governing word (ʿāmil) being اتّخذوا, accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (هزوا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الواو) conjunction (لعبا) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (هزوا), accusative (من) a preposition (الذين) like the first, in the position of genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of اتّخذوا (أوتوا) a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma, passive.. and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) (الكتاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أوتوا), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (الكفار) conjoined to the second relative noun, following it in the accusative (أولياء) second mafʿūl bihi, its governing word being تتّخذوا, accusative, and it is prevented from nunation because it is assimilated to the noun with extended alif (al-ism al-mamdūd) on the pattern أفعلاء (الواو) conjunction (اتّقوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative (إن) a jussive-governing conditional particle [Note: إن here is for rousing and inflaming — as Ibn Hishām says — not for the conditioning that implies doubt.] (كنتم) a defective past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). And (تم) a pronoun, the noun of kāna (مؤمنين) khabar (predicate) of كنتم, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The vocative clause «يأيّها الذين ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لا تتّخذوا ...»: has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
The clause «اتّخذوا ...»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أوتوا ...»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the third relative noun (الذين).
The clause «اتّقوا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «كنتم مؤمنين»: has no grammatical position, resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then fear Allah".
(58) (الواو) conjunction (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, attached to (اتخذوا) (ناديتم) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn.. and (تم) a pronoun, fāʿil (إلى الصلاة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ناديتم) [Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl of the fāʿil of ناديتم, i.e. "calling to the prayer".], (اتّخذوا) like آمنوا, and (ها) a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi (هزوا ولعبا) like the first (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), the reference being to the act on their part.. (اللام) for distance, and (الكاف) for address (الباء) a preposition (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl), and (هم) an attached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as the noun of anna (قوم) khabar of anna, nominative (marfūʿ) (لا) negating (يعقلون) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم قوم..) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك.
The clause «ناديتم ...»: in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «اتّخذوها ...»: has no grammatical position, apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ذلك بأنّهم ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive, having the status of a causal explanation.
The clause «لا يعقلون»: in the position of nominative as naʿt of قوم.

safi-cedvel:59-59.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (يا) a vocative particle (أهل) the one addressed (munādā), in construct (muḍāf), accusative (manṣūb) (الكتاب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) (هل) an interrogative particle containing the meaning of negation (تنقمون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ)..
and the wāw is the fāʿil (من) a preposition, and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تنقمون), which carries the meaning of تكرهون ("you resent") (إلّا) a particle of restriction (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle only (آمنّا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, with its fāʿil (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (آمنا).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن آمنّا) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governing word (ʿāmil) being تنقمون, i.e.: "you resent in us our belief in Allah".
(الواو) conjunction (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, conjoined to the Name of Majesty (أنزل) a past verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", and it is the resumptive pronoun (al-ʿāʾid) (إلى) a preposition, and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنزل), (الواو) conjunction (ما أنزل) like the first and conjoined to it (من) a preposition (قبل) a noun, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to the second (أنزل) (الواو) conjunction (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl), for emphasis (أكثر) the noun of anna, accusative, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (فاسقون) khabar (predicate) of anna, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ أكثركم فاسقون) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the Name of Majesty, i.e. "you resent in us our belief in Allah and that most of you are transgressors" [Note: The interpreted maṣdar may be in the position of accusative: a- conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar أن آمنا on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e.: "and the belief that most of you are transgressors". b- it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), the wāw being the wāw of accompaniment, i.e.: "you resent, while most of you transgress", i.e. "together with the transgression of most of you". c- accusative by an implied verb, i.e.:
"and you do not resent that most of you are transgressors".
It may be in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is omitted and placed before it, i.e.: "and known is the transgression of most of you", the clause being resumptive.].
The clause «قل»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The vocative clause «يا أهل الكتاب»: in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «هل تنقمون»: has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
The clause «آمنّا ...»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أنزل إلينا»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (ما).
The clause «أنزل من قبل»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).

* Rhetoric:
Emphasising praise with what resembles blame (taʾkīd al-madḥ bi-mā yushbih al-dhamm): for the exception after the question, which runs in the manner of a rebuke over the faith for which they faulted the believers, gives the impression that what will come after the question is something for which its doer ought to be resented, something he is blamed for; so when what came after the question was something that requires praise of its doer, the speech contained emphasis of praise by what resembles blame.

safi-cedvel:60-60.t:
* I'rab:
(قل هل) their i'rab has already been given [Note: In the previous verse (59).], (أنبئ) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anā" (بشرّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنبّئكم), (من) a preposition (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive (majrūr), attached to شرّ. And (اللام) is for distance, and (الكاف) for address (مثوبة) tamyīz (specification), accusative (manṣūb) [Note: مثوبة ("reward") here is borrowed for sarcasm, so it means punishment.], (عند) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of مثوبة (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "huwa" [Note: (من) may be a badal (substitute) of شرّ, and it may be an indefinite noun qualified (nakira mawṣūfa), the clause after it being a naʿt], (لعن) a past verb, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (الواو) conjunction (غضب) like لعن, and the fāʿil is "huwa" (على) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (غضب), (الواو) conjunction (جعل) like لعن (من) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (جعل) [Note: If the verb is transitive to two objects, it is the second object of (جعل).], (القردة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الواو) conjunction (الخنازير) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to القردة, accusative like it (الواو) conjunction (عبد) like لعن (الطاغوت) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (أولئك) a demonstrative, indeclinable on kasra, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. And (الكاف) is for address (شرّ) khabar, nominative (مكانا) tamyīz, accusative (الواو) conjunction (أضلّ) conjoined to شرّ, nominative (عن سواء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أضل) (السبيل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «قل ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أنبّئكم ...»: in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «(هو) من لعنه الله»: has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لعنه الله»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).
The clause «غضب ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «جعل ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «عبد الطاغوت»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «أولئك شرّ ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(أضلّ), an elative (ism tafḍīl) from ضلّ يضلّ, of the pattern-class (bāb) ضرب, its pattern is أفعل.

* Rhetoric:
1- Putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun: in His saying, the Exalted, مَنْ لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ; He put the majestic Name in place of the pronoun to instil awe, to bring in dread, and to make the matter of the curse appear terrible.
2- Sarcasm (tahakkum): in His saying «مثوبة»; its use here for evil is by way of sarcasm, as in the saying: «تحية بينهم ضرب وجيع» ("their greeting among themselves is a painful blow").
3- Metonymy (kināya): in His saying, the Exalted, أُولئِكَ شَرٌّ مَكاناً; ascribing evil to their place is more eloquent in indicating their evil, for they [the rhetoricians] have stated explicitly that ascribing evil to the place of a thing is a metonymy for ascribing it to the thing itself, as in their saying: "Peace be upon the lofty assembly", and "glory is between his two cloaks". It is as if their evil had left its mark on their place, or had grown so great that it became embodied.
The attribution may also be figurative (majāzī), like "the river flowed".

* Benefits:
A point about the elative (ism al-tafḍīl)..
1- We know that the elative is formed from a three-letter verb that is complete (i.e. not defective), affirmative (not negated), inflecting (not jāmid), active in voice, admitting of degree, and whose adjective is not on the pattern أفعل. The elative is formed from a verb fulfilling these conditions on the pattern أفعل, and it indicates that two things share in a quality and one of them exceeds the other, as in His saying, the Exalted: أَنَا أَكْثَرُ مِنْكَ مالًا وَأَعَزُّ نَفَراً. Three nouns have been irregular, not being on this pattern, and they are: أُولئِكَ شَرٌّ مَكاناً, and the word حبّ, as in the poet's saying: (وحبّ شيء الى الإنسان ما منعا) ("and the dearest thing to man is what has been withheld"), with the knowledge that in this last one it is permissible to use it according to its origin in the rule, so it is permissible for me to say: أنت أحب إليّ من زيد ("you are dearer to me than Zayd").
[Translator's note: only two of the announced three are mentioned in the source; the usual third is خير.]
2- The modes of reading in His saying, the Exalted, وَعَبَدَ الطَّاغُوتَ.
Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī cited the various modes of reading (عبد الطاغوت) occurring in the noble verse; we cite them in order to draw the reader's attention to these modes:
1- It is read with fatḥa on the ʿayn and the bāʾ and the accusative of الطاغوت, as a verb conjoined to لعن, with الطاغوت as mafʿūl bihi.
2- It is read with fatḥa on the ʿayn, ḍamma on the bāʾ and the genitive of الطاغوت; here عبد is a noun with the meaning of a plural, and what follows it is genitive by being in construct with it, and it is accusative by جعل.
3- It is read with ḍamma on the ʿayn and the bāʾ, fatḥa on the dāl and the genitive of what follows; it is a plural of عبد like سقف and سقف, or of عبيد like قتيل and قتل, or of عابد like نازل and نزل, or of عباد like كتاب and كتب, so it would be a plural of a plural like ثمار and ثمر.
4- It is read عبّد الطاغوت, with ḍamma on the ʿayn and fatḥa and doubling on the bāʾ, like ضارب and ضرّب.
5- It is read عبّاد الطاغوت, like صائم and صوّام.
6- It is read عباد الطاغوت, which is clear, like صائم and صيام.
7- It is read وعابد الطاغوت and عبد الطاغوت, as an adjective like حطم.
8- It is read وعبد الطاغوت, as passive, with الطاغوت as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
9- It is read وعبد الطاغوت like ظرف, and it is read وعبدوا as a verb and the wāw.
And الطاغوت is mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
10- It is read وعبدة الطاغوت, which is a plural of عابد like قاتل and قتلة.
[Translator's note: the source text is unvowelled, so several of these readings look identical in Arabic script; they are distinguished only by the vowel descriptions given. Item 9 is broken in the source and is translated as written.]

safi-cedvel:61-61.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قالوا) (جاؤوا) a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (قالوا) like جاؤوا (آمنا) a past verb with its fāʿil (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq) (دخلوا) like جاؤوا (بالكفر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of دخلوا, the bāʾ being for accompaniment (الواو) conjunction [Note: Some — among them Abū Ḥayyān — permitted the wāw to be the wāw of circumstance, the one to whom both ḥāls refer being the same.], (هم) a pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) (قد خرجوا به) like قد دخلوا بالكفر [Note: (به) is a ḥāl, its governing word being خرجوا and the one it refers to being the fāʿil.] (الواو) resumptive (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ) (أعلم) khabar (predicate), nominative (الباء) a preposition (ما) a relative noun [Note: Or a maṣdar-forming particle, the interpreted maṣdar being in the position of genitive, attached to أعلم.] in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (أعلم), (كانوا) a defective past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma, and the wāw is the noun of kāna (يكتمون) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «جاؤوكم»: in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قالوا ...»: has no grammatical position, apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «آمنا»: in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قد دخلوا ...»: in the position of accusative as ḥāl of the fāʿil of قالوا.
The clause «هم قد خرجوا ...»: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, conjoined to the clause قد دخلوا.
The clause «قد خرجوا ...»: in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
The clause «الله أعلم ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كانوا يكتمون»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يكتمون»: in the position of accusative as khabar of كانوا.

* Morphology:
(أعلم), a derived adjective meaning عالم ("knowing"), with no meaning of preference (tafḍīl) in it.

safi-cedvel:95-95.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا لا تقتلوا الصيد) the i'rab of its counterpart has already been given [Note: in ayah (87) of this surah.], (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl (circumstance). (أنتم) a pronoun in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject). (حرم) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ). (الواو) conjunction. (من قتل) like من اعتدى [Note: in the previous ayah (94).], and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (من) preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of قتل. (متعمّدا) a second ḥāl of the fāʿil of قتل. (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (جزاء) mubtadaʾ placed later, and the khabar is omitted, i.e. فعليه جزاء (then upon him is a compensation). (مثل) naʿt (adjective) of جزاء, nominative [Note: or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هو, i.e. "a compensation, it being the like of what he killed" ... and the nominal clause is a naʿt of جزاء.], (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (قتل) past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو. (من النعم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of the omitted object pronoun, i.e. "what he killed, from the livestock" [Note: or attached to an omitted naʿt of جزاء.], (يحكم) imperfect verb, nominative. (الباء) preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يحكم). (ذوا) fāʿil, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the alif. (عدل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (منكم) like the first, attached to an omitted naʿt of (ذوا). (هديا) ḥāl, accusative (manṣūb), of the pronoun in (به) [Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. يهديه هديا; and it is said to be a tamyīz (specification).] (بالغ) naʿt of (هديا), accusative like it. (الكعبة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (أو) a conjunction of choice. (كفّارة) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to جزاء, nominative [Note: or a mubtadaʾ placed later whose khabar is omitted, i.e. عليه كفّارة (upon him is an expiation).] (طعام) ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of كفّارة [Note: or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هو.], (مساكين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa, since it is a diptote, being on the form of the furthest plurals (ṣīghat muntahā al-jumūʿ). (أو) like the first. (عدل) maʿṭūf to كفّارة — or to جزاء — nominative like it. (ذلك) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.. and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address. (صياما) tamyīz, accusative. (اللام) the lām of causation (taʿlīl). (يذوق) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being هو. (وبال) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (أمر) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يذوق) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to something implied that includes the three matters mentioned, i.e. "that was made obligatory so that he may taste the evil consequence of his deed" [Note: it may be attached to the "being established" (al-istiqrār) on which جزاء was built, or to طعام, or to (صياما).], (عفا) past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (عن) preposition. (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to (عفا). (سلف) like قتل. (الواو) conjunction. (من عاد) like من قتل. (الفاء) linking the apodosis. (ينتقم) like يحكم. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (منه) like منكم, attached to (ينتقم). (الواو) resumptive. (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative. (عزيز) khabar, nominative. (ذو) a second khabar, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw, since it is one of the five nouns. (انتقام) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The vocative clause «يأيّها الذين»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لا تقتلوا ...»: has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «أنتم حرم»: is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of تقتلوا.
The clause «من قتله ...»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause answering the vocative.
The clause «قتله ...»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: the khabar may be the two clauses of condition and apodosis together.].
The clause «(عليه) جزاء»: is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «قتل ...»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يحكم به»: is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of جزاء [Note: or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of it, because it is described.].
The clause «يذوق ...»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «عفا الله»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «سلف»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «من عاد»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause عفا الله.
The clause «عاد ...»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: the khabar may be the two clauses of condition and apodosis together.].
The clause «ينتقم»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هو..
The nominal clause (هو ينتقم الله منه) is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «الله عزيز ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(بالغ), an active participle from the triliteral بلغ; its pattern is فاعل.
(الكعبة), a name for the Sacred House of Allah. It was so named because of its cube shape (takʿīb), i.e. its squareness, since every square house is called a كعبة; its pattern is فعلة, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(وبال), a noun for something heavy, especially in what is disliked; its pattern is فعال, with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
1- The dependent implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya al-tabaʿiyya): in His saying «لِيَذُوقَ وَبالَ أَمْرِهِ», where the evil outcome of his violating the sanctity of iḥrām is likened to unwholesome, indigestible food that he tastes.

* Benefits:
1- Among the rites of «iḥrām»..
His saying: «فَجَزاءٌ مِثْلُ ما قَتَلَ». The scholars said what is meant by that is that the expiation of one who kills game during iḥrām is to offer a ransom from the livestock resembling in physical form the game he killed, which two persons of justice and discernment judge and assess. Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿUmar and ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them, judged in the case of the ostrich a «badana» from the camels; Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū ʿUbayda judged in the case of the wild cow and the wild ass a cow; and Ibn ʿUmar and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf judged in the case of the gazelle a sheep. On the basis of this judgement, it may be replaced, for one who does not find it, by feeding the equivalent of that to the poor, or clothing them, or fasting one day for the feeding of each poor person.
2- «ذوا عدل»..
It is agreed upon that «ذو» meaning "possessor" is one of the five nouns according to the opinion of some grammarians, or of the six according to the opinion of others, and that it is declined with letters according to the rule of those nouns and with their conditions. But there are two matters worth pointing out:
The first is that «ذا» may be a demonstrative and may be a relative noun, and it is one of the five nouns only when it means "possessor"; and the one that is of the five nouns, when put in the dual, is declined as a dual, and when put in the plural is declined as a sound masculine plural, taking the wāw in the nominative and the yāʾ in the accusative and genitive. [Translator's note: the source announces two matters but states only the first.]
3- Annexation and definiteness ...
On examining the states of annexation (iḍāfa), we find it is of three kinds.
The first conveys the definiteness of the muḍāf through the muḍāf ilayhi if the muḍāf ilayhi is definite, and its specification if it is indefinite. The first is like كتاب علي (ʿAlī's book) and the second like كتاب تلميذ (a pupil's book).
The second kind:
It conveys specification of the muḍāf without making it definite, and that is when the muḍāf is one of the vague nouns, «such as غير, مثل and شبه».
The third kind: it conveys neither definiteness nor specification, and that is when the muḍāf is an active participle, a passive participle, a resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha), or anything resembling the imperfect verb, i.e. indicating the present and the future, as occurs in the noble ayah «هَدْياً بالِغَ الْكَعْبَةِ».

safi-cedvel:96-96.t:
* I'rab:
(أحل) passive past verb. (اللام) preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أحلّ). (صيد) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (البحر) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). And (طعام) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to صيد by the conjunction, nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (متاعا) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative (manṣūb) [Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because it is the noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar) of the verb متّع ...], (لكم) like the first, attached to (متاعا). (الواو) conjunction. (للسيّارة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (متاعا). (الواو) conjunction. (حرّم عليكم صيد البر) like أحلّ لكم صيد البحر. (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle. (دمتم) defective past verb (of kāna and its sisters)..
(وتم) a pronoun, the noun of دمتم. (حرما) khabar (predicate) of ما دام, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما دمتم حرما) is in the position of the accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (حرّم).
(الواو) resumptive. (اتّقوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma [Translator's note: so in the source; elsewhere such imperatives are said to be indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn.].. and the wāw is fāʿil (agent). (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الذي) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty. (إلى) preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (تحشرون), which is a passive imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil.
The clause «أحلّ لكم صيد ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «حرّم عليكم صيد ...»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «دمتم ...»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «اتّقوا ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «تحشرون ...»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).

* Morphology:
(السيّارة), plural of السيّار, which is the traveller who travels much; an intensive form of the active participle from السير (travelling); its pattern is فعال, with fatḥa on the fāʾ and doubling of the ʿayn, and the pattern of السّيارة is فعّالة, with the addition of the tāʾ at its end.

safi-cedvel:97-97.t:
* I'rab:
(جعل) past verb. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (الكعبة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (البيت) ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of الكعبة or badal (substitute) of it, accusative. (الحرام) naʿt (adjective) of البيت, accusative. (قياما) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, its governor being جعل [Note: if the verb (جعل) means "created", (قياما) is an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial).], (للناس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قياما). (الواو) conjunction, in the three places. (الشهر، الهدي، القلائد) nouns conjoined to الكعبة, accusative. (الحرام) naʿt of الشهر, accusative. (ذلك) demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: the demonstrative may be mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being شرع (He legislated), and the lām of causation is attached to it.]. (واللام) for distance (والكاف) for address. (اللام) for causation (taʿlīl). (تعلموا) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and the sign of the accusative is the deletion of the nūn.. and the wāw is fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تعلموا) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ذلك.
(أنّ) a particle resembling the verb (of inna and its sisters). (الله) the Name of Majesty, noun of anna, accusative. (يعلم) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو. (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi. (في السموات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative ما. (الواو) conjunction. (ما) like the first and conjoined to it. (في الأرض) like في السموات.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله يعلم ...) has taken the place of the two objects of تعلموا.
(الواو) conjunction. (أنّ الله) like the first. (بكل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to عليم. (شيء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (عليم) khabar of anna, nominative.
The clause «جعل الله ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «ذلك لتعلموا»: has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) or causal.
The clause «تعلموا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «يعلم»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of anna.

safi-cedvel:98-98.t:
* I'rab:
(اعلموا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is fāʿil (agent). (أن الله) its i'rab has already been given «1», (شديد) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ). (العقاب) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (الواو) conjunction. (أن الله غفور) like أن الله عليم «2», (رحيم) a second khabar, nominative. [Translator's note: the footnote markers «1» and «2» appear in the source without their footnote text.]
The interpreted maṣdar (أن الله شديد) has taken the place of the two objects of اعلموا.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن الله غفور ..) is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar.
The clause «اعلموا ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

safi-cedvel:4-4.t:
* I'rab:
(يسألون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (الكاف) mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (ماذا) interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: (ما) may be parsed as the mubtadaʾ and (ذا) as a relative noun that is the khabar (predicate), with the clause as its ṣila (relative clause).. but the i'rab above is preferable, because it has been answered with a verbal clause.], (أحلّ) passive past verb, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (it) (اللام) preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أحلّ), (قل) imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (you) (أحلّ لكم) like the first (الطيبات) nāʾib fāʿil, nominative (الواو) conjunction (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), [in the] position of nominative, conjoined to الطيّبات, and it is on the basis of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «صيد ما علّمتم» (the game of what you have trained) or something with that meaning [Note: (ما) may be a conditional [noun] governing the jussive, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ.. and its apodosis is (فكلوا).], (علّمتم) past verb and its fāʿil (من الجوارح) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted third-person pronoun in علّمتم, i.e. «ما علّمتموه من الجوارح» (what you have trained of the hunting animals) (مكلّبين) ḥāl, accusative (manṣūb), of the fāʿil of علّمتم, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ (تعلّمون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (هنّ) an attached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (من) preposition (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (تعلّمونهنّ), (علّم) past verb, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative. (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition (كلوا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (ممّا) like the first (أمسكن) past verb and its fāʿil (عليكم) like لكم, attached to (أمسكن) (الواو) conjunction (اذكروا) like كلوا (اسم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الله) the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) (عليه) like لهم, attached to (اذكروا), (الواو) conjunction (اتّقوا الله) like اذكروا اسم ... (إنّ) particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl) (الله) the Divine Name, noun of إنّ, accusative (سريع) khabar, nominative (الحساب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «يسألونك ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «ماذا أحلّ ...»: in the position of accusative, the second mafʿūl bihi of (يسألون), which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
The clause «أحلّ لهم»: in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ماذا).
The clause «قل ...»: has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أحلّ لكم الطيّبات»: in the position of accusative, the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «علّمتم ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «تعلّمونهنّ»: in the position of accusative, a ḥāl of the fāʿil of علّمتم [Note: it may be resumptive with no grammatical position, or parenthetical on the account that parses (ما) as a jussive-governing conditional, since it intervenes between the condition and the apodosis.].
The clause «علّمكم الله»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
The clause «كلوا»: in the position of jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. «إن صدتم شيئا فكلوا....» (if you hunt something, then eat ...).
The clause «أمسكن ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the third relative noun (ما).
The clause «اذكروا ...»: in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause كلوا ...
The clause «اتّقوا الله»: in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause كلوا.
The clause «إنّ الله سريع الحساب»: has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(الجوارح): plural of جارحة, the feminine of جارح, an active participle applied to the beasts of prey, birds and dogs that hunt; its pattern is فاعل.
(مكلّبين): plural of مكلّب, the active participle of the quadriliteral كلّب, i.e. he sent the dog after the game; its pattern is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the doubled ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:5-5.t:
* I'rab:
(اليوم) adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أحلّ), (أحلّ لكم الطيّبات) like the preceding [Note: in the previous verse (4).], (الواو) conjunction (طعام) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (أوتوا) passive past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) (الكتاب) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (حلّ) khabar (predicate), nominative (اللام) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to حلّ (الواو) conjunction (المحصنات) conjoined to الطيّبات, nominative like it [Note: it may be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: «المحصنات من المؤمنات ... حلّ لكم» (chaste women from among the believers ... are lawful to you).], (من المؤمنات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in المحصنات (الواو) conjunction (المحصنات) like the first (من) preposition (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to a ḥāl of the pronoun in the second المحصنات (أوتوا) like the first (الكتاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أوتوا), (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (إذا) adverb of future time containing the sense of condition [Note: the adverb may be stripped of the conditional sense and attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ المحصنات, i.e. «حلّ لكم حين تؤتونهنّ أجورهنّ» (lawful to you when you give them their dowries).] in the position of accusative, attached to the content of the apodosis (آتيتم) past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and (الواو) is redundant (zāʾida), for prolonging the vowel of the mīm, and (هنّ) a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi (أجور) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هنّ) muḍāf ilayhi (محصنين) ḥāl, accusative, of the fāʿil of آتيتم (غير) second ḥāl of the fāʿil of آتيتم [Note: it may be a ḥāl of the pronoun in محصنين.. or an accusative naʿt (adjective) of محصنين.], accusative (مسافحين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ (الواو) conjunction (لا) redundant, for emphasizing the negation (متخذي) conjoined to غير, accusative like it, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, and the nūn was dropped because of the iḍāfa (أخدان) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «أحلّ لكم الطيّبات»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «طعام الذين ...»: has no [grammatical] position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «أوتوا ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «طعامكم حلّ لهم»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause طعام الذين.
The clause «أوتوا الكتاب (the second)»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «آتيتموهنّ ...»: in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.. and the apodosis of
[Translator's note: at this point the source text breaks off and a displaced passage belonging to the i'rab of verse 6 follows (from «(اطّهّروا)» to the clause «جاء أحد»); the verse-5 text resumes afterwards with «الشرط محذوف ...». It is translated here in the order the source gives it.]
(اطّهّروا) imperative verb, like اغسلوا (الواو) conjunction (إن كنتم مرضى) like إن كنتم جنبا, and the sign of the accusative in مرضى is the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the alif (أو) conjunction (على سفر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted [element] conjoined to مرضى, i.e. «موجودين على سفر» (being on a journey) (أو) like the first (جاء) past verb (أحد) fāʿil, nominative (من) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt of أحد (من الغائط) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جاء), (أو) like the first (لامستم) like قمتم (النساء) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الفاء) conjunction (لم) particle of negation, jussive and conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] (تجدوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (ماء) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) (تيمّموا) like اغسلوا (صعيدا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (طيّبا) naʿt of (صعيدا), accusative like it (الفاء) conjunction of consequence (tafrīʿ) (امسحوا) like اغسلوا (الباء) redundant [Note: it may be a genuine [preposition] of adhesion (ilṣāq), so that, with its genitive noun, it is attached to (امسحوا).. and see the i'rab of this verse in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, verse (63) [Translator's note: so in the source; the parallel verse is al-Nisāʾ 4:43]], (وجوه) genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (أيديكم) conjoined to وجوهكم, following it in the genitive in form..
and a muḍāf ilayhi, the sign of the genitive being the implied kasra (منه) like منكم, attached to (امسحوا). (ما) negating (يريد) imperfect verb, nominative (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative (اللام) redundant (يجعل) imperfect verb, accusative by an implicit أن after the lām, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He) (على) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a ḥāl of حرج — a naʿt that has come before the qualified noun [Note: it may be attached to (يجعل) or يحرج [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently for حرج]; and if the verb is transitive to two [objects], it is the second object.] — (من) redundant preposition (حرج) genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi (الواو) conjunction (لكن) particle of istidrāk (rectification) (يريد) like the first (ليطهّر) like ليجعل, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يجعل) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the first (يريد)..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يطهّر) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the second (يريد).
(الواو) conjunction (ليتمّ) like ليجعل (نعمة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (عليكم) like the first, attached to (يتم).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتّم) is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar (أن يطهّر).
(لعلّ) particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl), for hope (tarajjī), and (كم) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of لعلّ (تشكرون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The vocative clause «يأيّها الذين»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «the condition, its verb and its apodosis»: has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
The clause «قمتم الى الصلاة»: in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «اغسلوا ...»: has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «امسحوا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis.
The clause «كنتم جنبا»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the vocative.
The clause «اطّهّروا»: in the position of jussive, the apodosis of the jussive-governing condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «كنتم مرضى ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the vocative or to the clause كنتم جنبا.
The clause «جاء أحد ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause كنتم مرضى.
[Translator's note: here the verse-5 text resumes, continuing «... and the apodosis of» above.]
the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. «فهنّ حلّ لكم» (then they are lawful to you).
(الواو) resumptive (من) conditional noun governing the jussive, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (يكفر) imperfect verb, jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he) (بالإيمان) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يكفر), on the basis of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «بموجب الإيمان» (in the One who makes faith obligatory), and He is Allah (الفاء) linking the apodosis (قد) particle of realization (taḥqīq) (حبط) past verb (عمل) fāʿil, nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (هو) detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (في الآخرة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what (من الخاسرين) is attached to; [(من الخاسرين)] a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «من يكفر ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يكفر بالإيمان»: in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: the khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «قد حبط عمله»: in the position of jussive, the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «هو ... من الخاسرين»: in the position of jussive, conjoined to the apodosis clause — or resumptive with no grammatical position.

* Morphology:
(متّخذي): plural of متّخذ, the active participle of the five-letter اتّخذ; its pattern is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:35-35.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) is a vocative particle; (أيّ) is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative, and (ها) is a particle of alerting; (الذين) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) of أيّ or a naʿt (adjective) of it; (آمنوا) is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); (اتّقوا) is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) is a conjunction; (ابتغوا) is like اتّقوا; (إلى) is a preposition and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (ابتغوا) «[Note: It may be attached to الوسيلة, because it means seeking a means of approach through it.]»; (الوسيلة) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) is a conjunction; (جاهدوا) is like اتّقوا; (في سبيل) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (جاهدوا), and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (لعلّ) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters), and (كم) is a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of لعلّ; (تفلحون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ),
and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The vocative clause «يأيّها الذين» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «اتّقوا …» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «ابتغوا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the vocative.
The clause «جاهدوا …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the vocative.
The clause «لعلّكم تفلحون» has no grammatical position, explaining the cause (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «تفلحون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of لعلّ.

* Morphology:
(ابتغوا): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by quiescence and iʿlāl by deletion. Its origin is ابتغيوا with a ḍamma on the yāʾ; the ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so it was moved to the ghayn and the yāʾ made quiescent — iʿlāl by quiescence — then the yāʾ was deleted to avoid the meeting of two quiescents, so it became ابتغوا; its pattern is افتعوا.
(الوسيلة): a derived noun on the pattern فعيلة in the sense of مفعولة, from the verb وسل يسل, of the pattern-class وعد.

* Benefits:
Subtle meanings in the Quran. We know that لعلّ conveys hope (tarajjī) and the expectation that something will happen. In the Noble Quran, however, it occurs frequently at the close of verses: «لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ», as in this verse, and «لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ …» etc., as in many verses; but in this context it does not convey the hope that something will occur or the possibility of its happening, but rather conveys its realization and occurrence with certainty, without the slightest doubt. This is a masterly style among the inimitable styles of the Noble Quran.

safi-cedvel:36-36.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters); (الذين) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as the noun of إنّ; (كفروا) is a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle; (أنّ) is like إنّ; (اللام) is a preposition and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as the postponed noun of أنّ; (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; (جميعا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb), of ما.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ لهم ما في الأرض …) is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being «ثبت», i.e. «لو ثبت كون الذي في الأرض لهم».
(الواو) is a conjunction; (مثل) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the relative ما, accusative «[Note: Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be accusative as a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), its governor being the verbal sense in (لو), with the implied form «لو ثبت» … but Abū Ḥayyān rejected this analysis because the meaning is not sound and there is weakness in the expression.]», and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (مع) is an adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted ḥāl, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (اللام) is the lām of purpose (taʿlīl); (يفتدوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (به) is like لهم, attached to (يفتدوا).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يفتدوا) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to what (لهم) is attached to, i.e. to the khabar of أنّ.
