(من عذاب) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يفتدوا); (يوم) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (القيامة) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (ما) is negating; (تقبّل) is a past verb in the passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (منهم) is like لهم, attached to (تقبّل); (الواو) is a conjunction; (لهم) is like the first, attached to a fronted khabar; (عذاب) is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (أليم) is a naʿt (adjective), nominative.
The clause «إنّ الذين كفروا …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «ثبت وجود …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «يفتدوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن). The clause «ما تقبّل منهم» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «لهم عذاب …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause that is the apodosis.

* Morphology:
(يفتدوا): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by quiescence and iʿlāl by deletion. Its origin is يفتديوا with a ḍamma on the second yāʾ … and both kinds of iʿlāl took place in it following the course of (ابتغوا) in the previous verse.

* Rhetoric:
Metonymy (kināya): in the saying of the Exalted «لِيَفْتَدُوا بِهِ». It is a metonymy for the punishment being binding on them and that they have no way of escaping it; for among the concomitants of the punishment being binding is that if they ransomed themselves with all that is in the earth and as much again with it, it would not be accepted from them.
Some called this sentence a representation (tamthīl).

safi-cedvel:37-37.t:
* I'rab:
(يريدون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (يخرجوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (من النار) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يخرجوا).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يخرجوا) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being يريدون.
(الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (ما) is negating, operating like ليس; (هم) is a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as the noun of ما; (الباء) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (خارجين) is genitive (majrūr) in form and accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of ما, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (من) is a preposition and (ها) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to خارجين; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لهم عذاب مقيم) — the i'rab of its counterpart has already been given «[Note: In the previous verse (36).]».
The clause «يريدون» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يخرجوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «ما هم بخارجين …» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يريدون.
The clause «لهم عذاب …» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the ḥāl clause.

* Morphology:
(مقيم): an active participle from the quadriliteral أقام; its pattern is مفعل with a ḍamma on the mīm and a kasra on the ʿayn. It contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by conversion; its origin is مقوم, because the alif is originally a wāw, since it is from the bare verb قام. The kasra was felt heavy on the wāw, so it was made quiescent and the vowel moved to the qāf — which is iʿlāl by quiescence — then the wāw was converted to yāʾ because it was quiescent and the letter before it had a kasra, so it became (مقيم). [Translator's note: the source prints «قبلت الواو ياء», evidently for «قلبت» (was converted).]

safi-cedvel:38-39.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (السارق) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (الواو) is a conjunction; (السارقة) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to السارق, nominative like it; (الفاء) is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) «[Note: Contrary to Sībawayh, because for him the mubtadaʾ must be connected with an adverb, a preposition phrase, or a clause suitable for a conditional particle.]»; (اقطعوا) is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (أيدي) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (هما) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (جزاء) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative «[Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. «جازاهما جزاء»; or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), either of the fāʿil of اقطعوا, i.e. «مجازينهما», or of the muḍāf ilayhi in أيديهما, because it is part of the muḍāf, i.e. «مجازين» with a fatḥa on the zāy.]»; (الباء) is a preposition; (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle «[Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, with the returning pronoun omitted.]»; (كسبا) is a past verb, and (الألف) is a pronoun, fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كسبا) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (جزاء). (نكالا) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, accusative «[Note: It may be a badal (substitute) of جزاء, taking its i'rab.]», its governor being جزاء; (من الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (نكالا); (الواو) is a conjunction; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (عزيز) is the khabar, nominative; (حكيم) is a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «السارق والسارقة …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «اقطعوا …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (السارق) «[Note: The clause may be an explanatory resumption, with the khabar omitted, the implied form being: «حكم السارق … فيما يلي» (the ruling on the thief … is in what follows).]».
The clause «الله عزيز …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause «[Note: Or parenthetical between the conjoined and what it is conjoined to.]».
(الفاء) is a conjunction; (من) is a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (تاب) is a past verb, indeclinable, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (من بعد) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تاب); (ظلم) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) is a conjunction; (أصلح) is like تاب; (الفاء) is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters); (الله) is the Name of Majesty, the noun of إنّ, accusative; (يتوب) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is «هو»; (على) is a preposition and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يتوب); (إنّ الله غفور رحيم) — the i'rab of its counterpart has already been given «[Note: In verse (34) of this surah.]».
The clause «من تاب …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause in the previous verse.
The clause «تاب …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «[Note: The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and its apodosis together.]».
The clause «أصلح» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause تاب.
The clause «إنّ الله يتوب» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يتوب عليه» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «إنّ الله غفور» has no grammatical position, explaining the cause (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(السارق), and its feminine (السارقة): an active participle from سرق يسرق, of the pattern-class ضرب; its pattern is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
1- Loose metonymic trope (al-majāz al-mursal): in the saying of the Exalted «وَالسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهُما» …
What is meant is cutting at the wrist only; it expressed the whole, namely the hand, and meant the part, namely the wrist, so the relation of the trope here is wholeness (kulliyya).
2- Stating the majestic Name explicitly: in the saying of the Exalted «إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ», to signal the reason for the ruling and to reinforce the independence of the sentence.

* Benefits:
The rulings on theft. Theft is taking the property of another, kept in a secure place, secretly … The thing taken must be property of recognized value. The threshold almost agreed upon among Muslim jurists for property whose secret taking from its place of safekeeping counts as theft is what equals a quarter of a dinar.
This property must be kept secure, and the thief must take it from its place of safekeeping and carry it out of it. So, for example, there is no cutting for one entrusted with property if he steals it; a servant permitted to enter the house is not cut for what he steals, because it is not secured from him; nor for the borrower if he denies the loan; nor for fruit in the field until the threshing floor houses it; nor for property outside the house or the chest. The punishment in such cases is not cutting but taʿzīr (and taʿzīr is a punishment short of the ḥadd: by flogging, imprisonment, reprimand, or admonition in some cases, as the judge assesses it).
The cutting is of the right hand up to the wrist; if he repeats, the cutting is of the left foot up to the ankle. This is the agreed amount of cutting; then the jurists' views differ after that about the third and the fourth time.
Doubt (shubha) averts the ḥadd: the doubt of hunger and need, partnership in the property, the confessor retracting his confession — if there are no witnesses — and the witnesses' refusal to testify are all doubts that avert the ḥadd.
The general principle in Islam is averting the ḥadd punishments by doubts. Our master ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, did not cut in the Year of Ashes (ʿām al-ramāda) when famine was widespread; nor did he cut in a particular incident when the slave-boys of Ibn Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa stole a she-camel of a man from Muzayna. He had ordered them to be cut, but when it became clear to him that their master starved them, he averted the ḥadd from them and fined their master twice the price of the she-camel to discipline him.
Details and explanation about theft and cutting:
1- The verse requires cutting the hand of the male and female thief, whatever their status and kind.
2- The ruling is applied only to one who has reached puberty and is sane; as for the boy, no ruling applies to him, and likewise one who is new to Islam and ignorant of the ruling on the thief.
3- The scholars differed about the amount of the threshold (niṣāb) for which cutting is done. Most of the people of knowledge held that it is a quarter of a dinar. This is the view of Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, al-Awzāʿī and al-Shāfiʿī.
It is reported in the two Ṣaḥīḥs from ʿĀʾisha that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The hand of the thief is not cut except for a quarter of a dinar and upward."
Mālik, Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and Isḥāq held that the value is three dirhams.
4- The stolen property must be in a place of safekeeping, such as a house or a chest even if open, or a tent, or a guarded orchard, or livestock with a herdsman; in all of that there is cutting. But if it is not in a place of safekeeping there is no cutting, such as livestock without a herdsman and an orchard without a guard. As for digging up graves, there is cutting for it if the stolen property reaches a quarter of a dinar. This is the view of Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī and Aḥmad.
5- If he steals the first time, his right hand is cut from the kūʿ (i.e. the wrist), the protruding bone next to the thumb; and the second time his left foot is cut from the ankle joint.
The scholars differed: al-Shāfiʿī said that the third time his left hand is cut, and the fourth time his right foot; if he repeats, he is given taʿzīr and imprisoned until his repentance becomes manifest. This is also the view of Mālik, Abū Bakr and Qatāda. It has been established through practical experience that this punishment — cutting the hand of the thief — is among the most effective means of treating this dangerous social disease. Humans have tried many punishments to deter theft, but they did not succeed; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created man and knows what reforms him and what deters and restrains him. One of the heretics criticized the Sharīʿa for cutting the hand of the thief for a quarter of a dinar while its blood-money, if it is cut off, equals five hundred dinars, saying:
يد بخمسمئين عسجد وديت ... ما بالها قطعت في ربع دينار
(A hand whose blood-money is five hundred in gold — why is it cut off for a quarter of a dinar?)
A jurist replied to him, saying:
عزّ الأمانة أغلاها وأرخصها ... ذلّ الخيانة فافهم حكمة الباري
(The honour of trustworthiness made it precious, and the disgrace of treachery made it cheap — so understand the wisdom of the Creator.)
The trustworthy hand is honoured and precious, and its blood-money is (500) dinars if it is cut off in aggression; but the treacherous hand is cheap and is cut off for stealing a quarter of a dinar, so that its owner does not dare to steal more and more, and so that theft does not spread among the members of society, security is lost and ruin becomes widespread.

safi-cedvel:6-6.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab was given just before [Note: in verse (1) of this surah.], (إذا) adverb of future time containing the sense of condition, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the content of the apodosis (قمتم) past verb and its fāʿil (agent) (إلى الصلاة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قمتم) (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) (اغسلوا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is a pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (وجوه) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (الواو) conjunction (أيديكم) a muḍāf conjoined to وجوه, accusative, and a muḍāf ilayhi (الى المرافق) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (اغسلوا) [Note: it may be attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of أيدي, i.e.: «اغسلوا أيديكم مضافا إلى المرافق» (wash your hands, with the elbows added).], (الواو) conjunction (امسحوا) like اغسلوا (الباء) redundant (zāʾida) [Note: or a genuine [preposition] of adhesion (ilṣāq), so that, with its genitive noun, it is attached to (امسحوا).] (رؤوس) genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (أرجلكم) conjoined to وجوه by the wāw, accusative like it, and a muḍāf ilayhi (إلى الكعبين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what the prepositional phrase (إلى المرافق) is attached to, because it is part of the completion of the conjunction; the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ (الواو) conjunction (إن) conditional particle governing the jussive (كنتم) defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ)..
and (تم) a pronoun, the noun of كان (جنبا) khabar (predicate) of كان, accusative (الفاء) linking the apodosis
[Translator's note: at this point the source text breaks off; the continuation of this i'rab (from «(اطّهّروا)» to the clause «جاء أحد») is printed, displaced, inside the entry for verse 5. The text below resumes with the clause list as the source gives it.]
The clause «لامستم النساء»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause جاء أحد.
The clause «لم تجدوا ماء»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لامستم....
The clause «تيمّموا ...»: in the position of jussive, the apodosis of the jussive-governing condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «امسحوا ...»: in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause تيمّموا [Note: it may be parsed as explicative with no grammatical position, explaining the preceding clause تيمموا.].
The clause «ما يريد الله»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لكن يريد»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما يريد.
The clauses «يجعل، يطهّر، يتم»: have no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «لعلكم تشكرون»: has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «تشكرون»: in the position of nominative, the khabar of لعلّ.

* Morphology:
(المرافق): plural of المرفق, a noun for the well-known limb [the elbow]; its pattern is مفعل with kasra on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn, or with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn; the pattern of المرافق is مفاعل.
(الكعبين): dual of كعب, a noun for the bone protruding above the foot on both sides; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(اطّهّروا): the imperative of اطّهّر, meaning تطهّر (to purify oneself); it is an anomalous pattern among the augmented patterns, its pattern being افتعل with a doubled ʿayn.. In it the tāʾ of iftiʿāl was replaced by ṭāʾ because it came after the ṭāʾ, and then the two ṭāʾs were assimilated together.

* Rhetoric:
Kināya (metonymy): in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿أَوْ جاءَ أَحَدٌ مِنْكُمْ مِنَ الْغائِطِ﴾: coming from al-ghāʾiṭ — which is the sunken or low-lying ground — is a metonymy for ritual impurity (ḥadath), following the custom of the Arabs, which was that when one of them wanted to relieve himself, he would go to a low-lying place in the ground and relieve himself there.

* Benefits:
The obligatory acts of wuḍūʾ:
The prayer is a meeting with Allah, a standing before Him — Glory be to Him — a supplication raised to Him, an intimate converse and a confiding; so this station requires preparation: a bodily purification accompanied by a spiritual readiness. Hence wuḍūʾ — as we reckon, and knowledge belongs to Allah. These are its obligatory acts stipulated in this verse:
washing the face, washing the hands up to the elbows, wiping the head, and washing the feet up to the ankles. Around these obligatory acts there are minor juristic disagreements ... the most important of which is: must these obligatory acts follow the order in which they were mentioned, or do they suffice without order? There are two views.. This is for minor ritual impurity; as for major ritual impurity (janāba) — whether through intercourse or a wet dream — it necessitates a full bath.
Between language and legislation: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إِلَى الْمَرافِقِ﴾ — it has been said that إلى means (مع) "with", as in His saying: ﴿وَيَزِدْكُمْ قُوَّةً إِلى قُوَّتِكُمْ﴾. This is a weak view; the correct one is that it is for the end-point of the extent (intihāʾ al-ghāya). Washing the elbows became obligatory only through the Sunna, because that without which an obligation cannot be completed is itself obligatory, since the elbows must be washed for the washing of the hands to be complete. As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَامْسَحُوا بِرُؤُسِكُمْ﴾, some, such as Imam al-Shāfiʿī, considered the bāʾ to be partitive, and considered "part" to be the smallest portion of it; therefore he made wiping a single hair of the head obligatory and held that it suffices in wuḍūʾ. The Ḥanafī imam adopted this view, but he considered the "part" to be a quarter of the head, on the basis of the Sunna of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Imam Mālik considered the bāʾ to be for emphasis, meaning "with all of your heads", and so made wiping the whole head obligatory. Imam Aḥmad has two views: one of wiping the whole head and one of half of it. I have cited this only to show the value of meaning in understanding the rulings, the relation of i'rab to meaning, and that one should not censure the mujtahids for what they have differed on. And His saying, Exalted is He:
﴿وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ إِلَى الْكَعْبَيْنِ﴾ is read with أرجلكم in the accusative; thus it is conjoined to the faces and the hands, i.e. «فاغسلوا وجوهكم وأيدكم وأرجلكم» (so wash your faces, your hands and your feet), and the Sunna that has come with the washing of the feet strengthens this meaning. It has been said that الأرجل is conjoined to the position of الرؤوس, because the bāʾ is redundant and الرؤوس is accusative in position; but the first account is stronger, because conjoining to the form is stronger than conjoining to the position. There is a reading in the genitive that is as well known as the accusative, and it has two accounts:
The first: that it is conjoined to الرؤوس in i'rab, while the ruling differs: the heads are wiped and the feet are washed, i.e. «فامسحوا برؤوسكم واغسلوا بأرجلكم», as in our saying علفتها تبنا وماء (I fed it straw and water), i.e. I fed it straw and gave it water to drink. The conjunction is only because of something uniting the two, namely sufficiency [of nourishment]. Likewise the conjunction in the verse is because of something uniting the two, namely purification. The second account is that the genitive of الأرجل is by an omitted, implied preposition: «وافعلوا بأرجلكم غسلا» (and do washing with your feet); this is permissible in the language and the rules, and it has evidence. Washing is supported by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إِلَى الْكَعْبَيْنِ﴾, because what is wiped is not delimited. A beautiful observation:
He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿إِذا قُمْتُمْ إِلَى الصَّلاةِ﴾, and regarding janāba «وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضى» [Translator's note: so in the source; the words of the verse regarding janāba are «وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ جُنُباً»], because إذا enters upon what is occurring and awaited, while إن enters upon what is expected and possible; hence it is understood that the prayer is always occurring without fail, while janāba is something incidental and not constant. This is part of the precision of expression and the choice of words to suit the meaning. The Noble Quran has reached the utmost in this area: if a person tried to replace a word of the Noble Quran with a synonym or a substitute for it, even if it had a hundred synonyms, he would not find anything more fitting than it in its place in the verse, whether in terms of meaning, harmony, or the concordant melody of the verses of the Noble Quran.

safi-cedvel:62-62.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (ترى) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (كثيرا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) (من) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of (كثيرا), (يسارعون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (في الإثم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يسارعون), by its being made to carry the meaning of يقعون سريعا ("they fall quickly into") (العدوان) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الإثم by the wāw, genitive like it (الواو) conjunction (أكل) conjoined to الإثم, genitive, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (السحت) mafʿūl bihi of the maṣdar أكل, accusative (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath (بئس) a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as fāʿil of بئس [Note: Or an indefinite noun in the position of accusative as tamyīz (specification) of the latent pronoun that is the fāʿil of بئس, the clause كانوا being a naʿt of (ما).], (كانوا يعملون) like كانوا يكتمون [Note: In the previous verse (61).].
The clause «ترى»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يسارعون ...»: in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of كثيرا or a second naʿt of it [Note: It may be a second mafʿūl bihi of the verb ترى if it is taken as mental (qalbī).].
The clause «بئس ما كانوا ...»: has no grammatical position, the response to an implied oath.
The clause «كانوا يعملون»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يعملون»: in the position of accusative as khabar (predicate) of كانوا.

* Benefits:
Among the secrets of eloquence in the Noble Quran..
In the verse there occurs His saying, the Exalted, يُسارِعُونَ فِي الْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوانِ. We know that المسارعة in a thing is hastening to it quickly, but the word المسارعة is used only for good, and from it is His saying, the Exalted, يُسارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْراتِ; its opposite is العجلة ("haste"), which is mostly said of evil. The word المسارعة is mentioned in the verse only for a benefit, namely that they used to rush into these evils as if they were good deeds in their view, so the expression came in agreement with their state and their understanding.

safi-cedvel:63-63.t:
* I'rab:
(لولا) a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) meaning هلّا ("why not"), containing the meaning of rebuke (ينهى) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (الربّانيّون) fāʿil (agent), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw (الواو) conjunction (الأحبار) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to what precedes it, nominative like it (عن قول) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ينهى), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi [Translator's note: so in the source; the pronoun in قولهم is a muḍāf ilayhi, which is also the agent of the maṣdar in meaning.] (الإثم) mafʿūl bihi of the maṣdar قول, accusative (manṣūb) (الواو) conjunction (أكلهم السحت) like قولهم الإثم (لبئس ما كانوا يصنعون) like the previous one [Note: In the previous verse (62).].
The clause «ينهاهم الربانيّون»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «بئس ما كانوا ...»: has no grammatical position, the response to an implied oath.
The clause «كانوا يصنعون»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يصنعون»: in the position of accusative as khabar (predicate) of كانوا.

* Benefits:
His saying, the Exalted, لَوْلا يَنْهاهُمُ الرَّبَّانِيُّونَ وَالْأَحْبارُ.
- لولا in this verse means هلا and is parsed as a particle of urging (ḥaḍḍ). We will present the most important points concerning this particle.
1- It comes as a particle of non-occurrence because of existence (ḥarf imtināʿ li-wujūd), entering a nominal clause, followed by a verbal clause, as in لولا زيد لأكرمتك ("were it not for Zayd, I would have honoured you"): the honouring did not occur because of the existence of Zayd. The noun after it is parsed as mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being كائن ("existing"); this is if the khabar is a general existence (kawn ʿāmm). But if it is a specific existence (kawn khāṣṣ), it must be mentioned, as in: لولا قومك حديثو عهد بالإسلام لهدمت الكعبة ("were it not that your people are recent in Islam, I would have demolished the Kaʿba"), لولا العدو سالمنا لما توقفنا عن القتال ("were it not that the enemy made peace with us, we would not have stopped fighting").
2- If a pronoun follows لولا, it should properly be a nominative pronoun, as in His saying, the Exalted, لَوْلا أَنْتُمْ لَكُنَّا مُؤْمِنِينَ; and لولاي, لولاك and لولاه have been heard rarely, contrary to al-Mubarrad.
Then Sībawayh and the majority said: it governs the pronoun in the genitive, being specific to it, just as حتى and the kāf are specific to the overt noun; لولا is not attached to anything, and the position of the noun it puts in the genitive is the nominative by being a mubtadaʾ, the khabar being omitted. So if you conjoin an overt noun to it, as in لولاك وزيد, its nominative is required, because it does not put the overt noun in the genitive.
3- It comes as a particle of urging and of gentle request (ʿarḍ), and then it is specific to the imperfect or what is interpreted as such, as in (لَوْلا تَسْتَغْفِرُونَ اللَّهَ) (لَوْلا أَخَّرْتَنِي إِلى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ).
4- It comes for rebuke, and then it is specific to the past, as in (لَوْلا جاؤُ عَلَيْهِ بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَداءَ).
5- Interrogation: as in His saying, the Exalted, لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ; this is a weak view stated by al-Harawī, and the stronger view is that it is for rebuke.
2- Enjoining the good and forbidding the evil..
This verse contains a great principle, namely the obligation of enjoining the good and forbidding the evil, and it also makes clear that the scholars are the first to bear this responsibility, and that the scholars' abandoning it is a great sin. It indicates that one who abandons forbidding evil is in the same position as one who commits it. Ibn ʿAbbās said: There is nothing in the Quran more severe in rebuke than this verse. And al-Ḍaḥḥāk says: There is no verse in the Quran more frightening to me than it.

safi-cedvel:64-64.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (قال) a past verb, and (التاء) is for the feminine (اليهود) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) (يد) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) (مغلولة) khabar (predicate), nominative (غلّت) a past verb, passive. And (التاء) is for the feminine (أيدي) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (لعنوا) a past verb, passive, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma.. and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (الباء) a preposition (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (لعنوا), the resumptive pronoun being omitted.], (قالوا) a verb, a past verb [Translator's note: the word "verb" is repeated in the source.], indeclinable on ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما قالوا) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (لعنوا), the bāʾ being causal.
(بل) for invalidating digression (iḍrāb ibṭālī) and for beginning (يدا) mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the alif, the nūn being dropped because of the construct, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (مبسوطتان) khabar, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the alif (ينفق) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (كيف) a non-jussive conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) (يشاء) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "huwa". (الواو) resumptive (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath (يزيدنّ) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of nominative.. and (النون) the nūn of emphasis, (كثيرا) first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) (من) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (كثيرا) (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as fāʿil (أنزل) like غلّت, and the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", and it is the resumptive pronoun (al-ʿāʾid) (إلى) a preposition, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنزل), (من ربّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أنزل), and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi (طغيانا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, its governing word (ʿāmil) being يزيدنّ (الواو) conjunction (كفرا) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (طغيانا), accusative (الواو) conjunction (ألقينا) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, with its fāʿil (بين) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (ألقينا), and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi (العداوة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (البغضاء) conjoined to العداوة by the wāw, accusative like it (إلى يوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ألقينا), (القيامة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (كلّما) an adverb meaning حين ("when"), containing the meaning of condition, attached to the apodosis (أوقدوا) like قالوا (نارا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (للحرب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt of (نارا) [Note: It may be attached to (أوقدوا).], (أطفأ) a past verb, and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (الواو) conjunction (يسعون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يسعون), (فسادا) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "they strive as corrupters" [Note: There are other modes whose i'rab has been given before. See verse (33) of this surah.], (الواو) resumptive (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative (لا) negating (يحبّ) like ينفق (المفسدين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «قالت اليهود»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يد الله مغلولة»: in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «غلّت أيديهم»: has no grammatical position, parenthetical, of imprecation (duʿāʾiyya).
The clause «لعنوا»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the parenthetical clause.
The clause «قالوا ...»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «يداه مبسوطتان»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «ينفق ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: If we were to assume in the clause a pronoun referring back to (يداه), the clause would be in the position of nominative as a second khabar, i.e.: "His hands ... He spends with them...."].
The clause «يشاء»: has no grammatical position, resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: "however He wills to spend, He spends".
The clause «يزيدنّ ...»: has no grammatical position, the response to an implied oath.
The clause «أنزل إليك»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «ألقينا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قالت اليهود.
The clause «أوقدوا ...»: in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi [Note: (كلّ) may be separated from (ما), the maṣdar-forming particle, the interpreted maṣdar being muḍāf ilayhi and the clause being the ṣila of the particle-relative.].
The clause «أطفأها الله»: has no grammatical position, apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يسعون»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ألقينا ...
The clause «الله لا يحبّ ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لا يحبّ ...»: in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).

* Morphology:
(يد) a primitive (jāmid) noun whose final radical (lām), the yāʾ, has been dropped; its plural is أيدي and يدي with ḍamma on the first yāʾ.
(مغلولة), feminine of مغلول, passive participle of the three-letter verb غلّ, its pattern is مفعول.
(مبسوطتان), dual of مبسوطة, feminine of مبسوط, passive participle of the three-letter verb بسط, on the pattern مفعول.
(العداوة), the noun from المعاداة, taken from عاداه, its pattern is فعالة with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(البغضاء), the noun from التباغض or المباغضة, its pattern is فعلاء with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
1- Mushākala (verbal correspondence): in His saying, the Exalted, غُلَّتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ; it is an imprecation against them with blameworthy miserliness and abjectness, or with poverty and misery, or with the literal shackling of hands, in that they become shackled captives in this world and are dragged into the Fire by its shackles in the Hereafter. The correspondence is then in terms of the wording and with regard to the original meaning, as in "He insulted me — may Allah insult him to his last".
2- Metonymy (kināya): in His saying, the Exalted, كُلَّما أَوْقَدُوا ناراً لِلْحَرْبِ أَطْفَأَهَا اللَّهُ; kindling the fire is a metonymy for intending war. When the Arabs agreed to meet for fighting, they made their sign the kindling of a fire on a mountain or a hill, and they called it "the fire of war". Extinguishing it is an expression for repelling their evil, and attributing the extinguishing to Him, the Exalted, is attributing the effect to the original cause.
3- Antithesis (ṭibāq): between kindling and extinguishing ...

* Benefits:
- The baseness of the Jews and their obstinacy..
This verse was revealed concerning Finḥāṣ the Jew. Ibn ʿAbbās said: Allah had extended [provision] to the Jews until they were the wealthiest of people and the most fertile in their region; but when they disobeyed Allah and Muḥammad ﷺ and denied him, He withheld from them the abundance He had extended to them. Thereupon Finḥāṣ said: يد الله مغلولة ("the hand of Allah is chained"), meaning withheld and closed from provision. And when the rest of the Jews did not forbid him and were pleased with his saying, there is no doubt that Allah the Exalted made them partners with him in this statement.
- The scheming of the Jews in misleading..
The verse affirmed that the scheming and plotting of the Jews will not be granted success, and that whenever they set out on the path of war and battles, they will return disappointed. This is affirmed by His saying, the Exalted, كُلَّما أَوْقَدُوا ناراً لِلْحَرْبِ أَطْفَأَهَا اللَّهُ. Let no one be deceived by their winning some rounds in fighting us, for matters are judged by their outcomes and conclusions, and the conclusion will be ruin and loss for them. This is the glad tiding of the noble verse, and beside it is the glad tiding of the Prophet ﷺ in his hadith reported in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim: "The Hour will not come until you fight the Jews, and the stone and the tree will speak, saying: O Muslim, behind me is a Jew; come and kill him — except the gharqad, for it is one of the trees of the Jews."
- A statement on "the hand" (al-yad):
They said: "hand" in the language is mentioned in several senses. The first is the bodily limb, which is known. The second is favour (niʿma); one says: "So-and-so has a hand with me for which I thank him." The third is power (qudra); Allah the Exalted said أُولِي الْأَيْدِي وَالْأَبْصارِ, which they interpreted as "possessors of strength and minds", and one says: "you have no hand in this matter", the meaning being the negation of full power. The fourth is ownership; one says: "this estate is in the hand of so-and-so", i.e. in his ownership, and from it is His saying, the Exalted, الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ عُقْدَةُ النِّكاحِ, i.e. he owns that.

safi-cedvel:99-99.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) negative particle. (على الرسول) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) placed first. (إلّا) particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (البلاغ) mubtadaʾ (subject) placed later, nominative (marfūʿ). (الواو) conjunction. (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative. (يعلم) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil (agent) is هو. (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) [Note: or a maṣdar-forming particle, and the interpreted maṣdar is mafʿūl bihi; or an indefinite noun that is described, and the clause after it is its naʿt (adjective), and the returning pronoun is omitted.], (تبدون) imperfect verb, nominative.. the wāw is fāʿil. (الواو) conjunction. (ما) like the first and conjoined to it. (تكتمون) like تبدون.
The clause «ما على الرسول إلّا البلاغ»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «الله يعلم ...»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يعلم ...»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «تبدون»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما), the nominal or the particle relative.
The clause «تكتمون»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative (ما), or of the particle relative.

* Rhetoric:
1- In the noble ayah: irsāl al-mathal (sending forth a proverb), in His saying «ما عَلَى الرَّسُولِ إِلَّا الْبَلاغُ». It consists of the speaker bringing, in part of his speech, something that runs like a current proverb, of wisdom, description or other.
2- Ṭibāq (antithesis): between «تبدون» and «تكتمون».

* Benefits:
- «ما» in the language of the ḍād has a standing — and what a standing!?
It comes as a relative noun meaning الذي (that which) ...
It comes as maṣdar-forming, and together with the verb that follows it is interpreted as a maṣdar that takes its place in i'rab according to its position in the sentence and according to the governing factors acting on it.
It comes as the Ḥijāzī negative, governing like ليس: it puts the noun in the nominative and the predicate in the accusative, and it is restricted to the nominal clause.
Or it is negative and left without effect (muhmala), and what follows it is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, both nominative; it is also negative for restriction, as in His saying: «وَما عَلَى الرَّسُولِ إِلَّا الْبَلاغُ». It comes as redundant, namely the one attached to «إنّ» and its sisters, restraining them from governing, with some detail, and it is called the restraining and the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa).
This «ما» has taken of the scholars' effort and the ink of their pens what fills volumes of grammar books; whoever wants more should turn to the lengthy works of this science.

safi-cedvel:100-100.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنت. (لا) negative particle. (يستوي) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ. (الخبيث) fāʿil, nominative. (الواو) conjunction. (الطيّب) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الخبيث, nominative. (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (لو) a conditional particle that does not put into the jussive. (أعجب) past verb, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (كثرة) fāʿil, nominative. (الخبيث) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition. (اتّقوا) like اعلموا [Note: in ayah (98) of this surah.], (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb). (يا) vocative particle. (أولي) the one addressed (munādā), muḍāf, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ, since it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural. (الألباب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (لعلّ) a particle resembling the verb (of inna and its sisters), for hope (tarajjī), and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative, noun of laʿalla. (تفلحون) like تبدون [Note: in the previous ayah (99).].
The clause «قل ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لا يستوي الخبيث ...»: is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أعجبك كثرة ...»: is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يستوي.
The clause «اتّقوا ...»: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if you want success, then be mindful of Allah".
The clause «النداء ...» (the vocative clause): has no grammatical position, being parenthetical.
The clause «لعلّكم تفلحون»: has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya) for the command to be mindful.
The clause «تفلحون»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of laʿalla.

* Morphology:
(كثرة) a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the triliteral كثر, of the class of كرم; its pattern is فعلة, with fatḥa then sukūn. There is another maṣdar, كثارة.

* Rhetoric:
1- The explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya): in His saying «قُلْ لا يَسْتَوِي الْخَبِيثُ وَالطَّيِّبُ».
I.e. the lawful and the unlawful are not equal. He likened the lawful to the good in its sweetness and the soul's acceptance of it, to encourage it, and He likened the unlawful to the foul in its repugnance and the soul's aversion to it, to repel from it. He stated explicitly the thing compared to and omitted the thing compared.

safi-cedvel:101-102.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا لا تسألوا) the i'rab of its counterpart has already been given [Note: in ayah (87) of this surah.], (عن أشياء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تسألوا), and the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa, since it is a diptote, assimilated to what ends in the elongated alif of the feminine. [Translator's note: the source has «ملحق بالمنتهي», rendered here according to the evident sense.] (إن) a conditional particle that puts into the jussive. (تبد) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هي. (اللام) preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (تبد). (تسؤ) imperfect verb, jussive, apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil (agent) is هي, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الواو) conjunction. (إن) like the first. (تسألوا) like the first, protasis. (عن) preposition, and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (تسألوا). (حين) adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb) [Note: the adverb came declinable here because what follows it is declinable ... and it may be attached to (تبد).] attached to the second (تسألوا). (ينزّل) passive imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). (القرآن) nāʾib fāʿil, nominative. (تبد) like the first, apodosis, and the sign of the jussive is the deletion of the weak letter. (لكم) like the first, attached to (تبد). (عفا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (عنها) like the first, attached to (عفا). (الواو) resumptive. (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (غفور) khabar (predicate), nominative. (حليم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «يأيّها الذين ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لا تسألوا ...»: has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «تبد لكم ...»: is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of أشياء.
The clause «تسؤكم»: has no grammatical position, being the apodosis not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «تسألوا ...»: is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause إن تبد لكم.
The clause «ينزّل القرآن»: is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «تبد لكم» (the second): has no grammatical position, being the apodosis not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «عفا الله عنها»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive [Note: if the pronoun in (عنها) refers back to أشياء, the clause could validly be a description of أشياء, in the position of the genitive.].
The clause «الله غفور ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
(102) (قد) particle of realization (taḥqīq). (سأل) past verb. (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (قوم) fāʿil, nominative. (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (سألها), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (ثمّ) conjunction. (أصبحوا) defective past verb (of kāna and its sisters), indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is a pronoun, the noun of aṣbaḥa. (الباء) preposition, and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (كافرين), which is the khabar of aṣbaḥa, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
The clause «سألها قوم ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive, giving the reason for the prohibition of asking.
The clause «أصبحوا ...»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Morphology:
(أشياء), plural of شيء, an underived (jāmid) noun; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn. Its plural is شيئا [Translator's note: so in the source; the form intended is presumably شيئاء.], on the pattern فعلاء: the first hamza is the lām (third radical) of the word, and the alif after it and the final hamza are both additional. Then spatial metathesis (al-qalb al-makānī) entered it.. the hamza that is the lām of the word was moved forward, and it became أشياء; its pattern is لفعاء [Note: there are other views on the pattern of أشياء and its morphology, to be consulted in the books of morphology; we have refrained from mentioning them.].
(تبد), contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion owing to the jussive; its pattern is تفع, with ḍamma on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(تسؤكم), contains iʿlāl by deletion owing to the jussive; its pattern is تفلكم.

* Benefits:
1- His saying: لا تَسْئَلُوا عَنْ أَشْياءَ etc. ... «أشياء» is a diptote noun, and the scholars differed about the origin of this word, the form of its plural, and what prevents it from taking tanwīn ...
a- Sībawayh held that its singular is شيء and that it was pluralized as شيئاء; then the lām was moved before the alif out of dislike for the meeting of two hamzas with a vowelless alif between them.
b- al-Farrāʾ held that its singular is شيء and its plural «أشيئاء», and the first hamza was deleted to lighten the pronunciation.
c- As for the school of al-Kisāʾī, it amounts to this: the pattern of أشياء is افعال, and it was made a diptote by analogy with what ends in the elongated alif of the feminine. There are other views and rebuttals that you will find in the book «al-Inṣāf fī Masāʾil al-Khilāf», if you want more of this science.

safi-cedvel:103-103.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) negative particle. (جعل) past verb. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (من بحيرة) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition and its noun, genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الواو) conjunction, in the three places. (لا) redundant, to emphasize the negation, in the three places. (سائبة، وصيلة، حام) nouns genitive in form, accusative in position, conjoined to بحيرة by the conjunctions; the kasra is implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ in the last noun. (الواو) conjunction. (لكنّ) a particle resembling the verb (of inna and its sisters), for rectification (istidrāk). (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative, noun of lākinna. (كفروا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is fāʿil. (يفترون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is fāʿil. (على الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يفترون). (الكذب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb). (الواو) conjunction. (أكثر) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (لا) negative particle. (يعقلون) like يفترون.
The clause «جعل الله ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لكنّ الذين كفروا ...»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كفروا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يفترون ...»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of lākinna.
The clause «أكثرهم لا يعقلون»: is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause يفترون [Note: the clause may be resumptive with no grammatical position.].
The clause «لا يعقلون»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أكثرهم).

* Morphology:
(بحيرة), فعيلة in the sense of مفعولة (passive), used as an underived (jāmid) noun ...
Its derivation is from البحر, and البحر is ampleness.
(سائبة), in form an active participle from ساب يسيب, meaning "to run freely"; and it is said that it is فاعلة in the sense of مفعولة, i.e. مسيّبة (let loose), just as it is said ماء دافق (gushing water) meaning مدفوق (poured out).
(وصيلة), a resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha); its pattern is فعيلة, and it is from sheep or camels, according to a difference of opinion.
(حام), an active participle from حمى يحمي, i.e. "to protect, forbid". It contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, because it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ) whose lām was deleted because of the tanwīn; its pattern is فاع.

* Benefits:
1- Concepts of the Jāhiliyya ...
Whoever wishes to picture the heavy weight of customs and the greatness of the messengers' responsibility in changing the customs of a people who had become habituated to them, elder after elder and generation after generation, let him picture the import of this ayah and its prohibition of things that the Arabs had taken as rites of their religion for hundreds of years, and perhaps thousands; for the ayah made lawful what had been unlawful and made unlawful what had been lawful.
The Messenger ﷺ came to expose the falseness of these beliefs and to return matters to their rightful place, despite the hardship he met on that path from the people and the intensity of their resistance; but Allah guaranteed that He would make His religion prevail, even if the disbelievers dislike it.
It is well known in explaining the vocabulary of this ayah that «البحيرة, السائبة, الوصيلة and الحامي are only names for particular kinds of livestock that the Arabs used to dedicate, for reasons connected with them, dedicating them to their gods and refraining from putting them to work or benefiting from them. Islam eradicated these customs at their root.

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction (اذكروا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) (نعمة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) (الله) the Divine Name, muḍāf [Translator's note: so in the source; i.e. muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct)], genitive (majrūr) (على) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of نعمة [Note: it may be attached to نعمة.] (الواو) conjunction (ميثاق) conjoined to نعمة, accusative like it, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الذي) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ميثاق (واثق) past verb, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", i.e. Allah (الباء) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (واثقكم), (إذ) adverb of the past, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, attached to (واثقكم) [Note: or to an omitted ḥāl of the hāʾ in به.. or in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) of نعمة.], (قلتم) past verb and its fāʿil (سمعنا) verb and agent (الواو) conjunction (أطعنا) like سمعنا (الواو) conjunction (اتّقوا الله) like اذكروا نعمة ...
(إنّ) particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl) (الله) the Divine Name, noun of إنّ, accusative (عليم) khabar (predicate) of إنّ, nominative (marfūʿ) (بذات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to عليم (الصدور) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «اذكروا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the vocative in the previous verse.
The clause «واثقكم ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «قلتم ...»: in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «سمعنا»: in the position of accusative, the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أطعنا»: in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause سمعنا.
The clause «اتّقوا الله»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اذكروا.
The clause «إنّ الله عليم ...»: has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab has been given [Note: in verse (1) of this surah.
(2, 3) in verse (2) of this surah.], (كونوا) defective (nāqiṣ) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the noun of كونوا (قوّامين) khabar (predicate) of the defective verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) قوامين (شهداء) second khabar of the defective verb, accusative (بالقسط) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to شهداء (الواو) conjunction (لا يجرمنّكم شنآن قوم على ألا تعدلوا) the i'rab of its counterpart has been given «2», (اعدلوا) like اذكروا «3», (هو) detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the pronoun refers to the justice understood from His saying اعدلوا (أقرب) khabar, nominative (marfūʿ) (للتقوى) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أقرب (الواو) conjunction (اتّقوا الله إنّ الله خبير) its i'rab has been given [Note: in the previous verse (7).] (الباء) preposition (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (خبير) [Note: (ما) may be a maṣdar-forming particle, with the interpreted maṣdar in the position of genitive.. or a qualified indefinite (nakira mawṣūfa), with the clause after it as its naʿt (adjective).], (تعملون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
The vocative clause «يأيّها الذين ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «كونوا قوّامين»: has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
The clause «لا يجرمنّكم ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the vocative.
The clause «لا تعدلوا»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «اعدلوا»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «هو أقرب للتقوى»: has no grammatical position, causal.. an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «اتّقوا الله»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اعدلوا.
The clause «إنّ الله خبير»: has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «تعملون»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the nominal or the particle relative.

* Rhetoric:
Repetition in the demand for justice: in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿عَلى أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا اعْدِلُوا﴾; this is either because of a difference of occasion — as it has been said that the first was revealed concerning the polytheists and this one concerning the Jews — or for added emphasis on justice and for intensity in extinguishing the flare of rage.

* Benefits:
Establishing justice:
Allah earlier forbade the believers — [in] the verse — to let hatred of those who barred them from the Sacred Mosque lead them to transgression, and that was a summit of self-restraint and magnanimity; but this verse commands the believers to an even greater summit than that: here they are forbidden to let hatred lead them to deviate from justice.. It is a summit higher to ascend, harder on the soul and more arduous.. For it is a stage beyond refraining from transgression and stopping at that; it goes on to establishing justice despite the feeling of hatred and loathing. The first obligation is easier, because it is a negative measure that ends at refraining from transgression; the second obligation is more arduous, because it is a positive measure that drives the soul to practise justice with those who are hated and loathed.

safi-cedvel:9-10.t:
* I'rab:
(وعد) past verb (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (آمنوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (الواو) conjunction (عملوا) like آمنوا (الصالحات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the kasra; and the second object of the verb وعد is omitted, its implied form being الجنّة (Paradise), (اللام) preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) (مغفرة) postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (الواو) conjunction (أجر) conjoined to مغفرة, nominative like it (عظيم) naʿt (adjective) of أجر, nominative.
The clause «وعد الله ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «لهم مغفرة ...»: has no grammatical position, explicative of the second object, as the cause explains the effect: Paradise is caused by forgiveness and the attainment of the great reward..
or it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
(الواو) conjunction (الذين) relative noun, mubtadaʾ (كفروا) like آمنوا, and like it (كذّبوا), (بآيات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (كذّبوا), and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (أولئك) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ.. and (الكاف) is for address (أصحاب) khabar, nominative (الجحيم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
The clause «الذين كفروا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause وعد الله ...
The clause «كفروا ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «كذّبوا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «أولئك أصحاب ...»: in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).

safi-cedvel:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab has been given [Note: in verse (1) of this surah.], (اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم) likewise its i'rab has been given [Note: in verse (7) of this surah.], (إذ) adverb of past time, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) نعمة [Note: or it is a badal (substitute) of نعمة.], (همّ) past verb (قوم) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) (أن) maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle (يبسطوا) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn..
and the wāw is the fāʿil (إلى) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يبسطوا), (أيدي) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يبسطوا) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, namely the bāʾ, attached to (همّ), the implied form being: «همّ قوم ببسط أيديهم ...» (a people intended the stretching out of their hands ...).
(الفاء) conjunction (كفّ) past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (He) (أيديهم) like the first (عنكم) like إليكم, attached to (كفّ), (الواو) conjunction (اتّقوا الله) like اذكروا نعمة ... (الواو) resumptive (على الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يتوكّل), and the prepositional phrase was fronted to give it importance (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, (اللام) the lām of command (يتوكّل) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and it was given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters (المؤمنون) fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The vocative clause «يأيّها الذين ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «اذكروا ...»: has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
The clause «همّ قوم ...»: in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يبسطوا ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «كفّ ...»: in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause همّ قوم.
The clause «اتّقوا الله»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause that answers the vocative.
The clause «ليتوكّل المؤمنون»: in the position of jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition [Note: i.e.: «إن اتّكل الناس على غير الله فليتوكّل المؤمنون على الله» (if people rely on other than Allah, then let the believers rely on Allah).. and see the i'rab of this construction in verse (122) and verse (160) of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān.]..
and the implied conditional clause is resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
1- Kināya (metonymy): in His saying, Exalted is He: «أَنْ يَبْسُطُوا إِلَيْكُمْ أَيْدِيَهُمْ», i.e. to assault you with killing and destruction. So the expression is a metonymy for their assault.
2- Putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun: in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿فَكَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ﴾: making الأيدي overt [instead of a pronoun] is for added reproach.

safi-cedvel:65-66.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl) (أهل) the noun of anna, accusative (manṣūb) (الكتاب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) (آمنوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) (الواو) conjunction (اتّقوا) like آمنوا (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لو (كفّرنا) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, with its fāʿil (عن) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كفّرنا), (سيّئات) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ أهل الكتاب آمنوا) is in the position of nominative as fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being ثبت ("it were established"), i.e.: "if the faith of the People of the Book were established".
(الواو) conjunction (لأدخلنا) like لكفّرنا, and (هم) a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi (جنّات) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra (النعيم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «(ثبت) إيمان أهل الكتاب»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of anna.
The clause «اتّقوا»: in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause آمنوا.
The clause «كفّرنا ...»: has no grammatical position, apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أدخلناهم ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
(66) (الواو) conjunction (لو أنّهم أقاموا التوراة) like its counterpart above (الواو) conjunction (الإنجيل) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to التوراة, accusative (الواو) conjunction (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, conjoined to التوراة (أنزل) a past verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", referring to ما (إليهم) like عنهم, attached to (أنزل), (من ربّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أنزل), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لو (أكلوا) like آمنوا (من فوق) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied object of أكلوا [Note: Or attached to (أكلوا), the whole expression being a metonymy for abundance of provision.], and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (من تحت) like من فوق, and attached to what that is attached to (أرجل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (منهم) like عنهم, attached to an advanced khabar (أمّة) a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) (مقتصدة) naʿt (adjective) of أمّة, nominative (الواو) conjunction (كثير) mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: What permitted beginning with an indefinite noun is that it indicates generality, and it has been qualified by the preposition and its genitive noun.], (منهم) like عنهم, attached to an omitted naʿt of كثير (ساء) a past verb for expressing blame, and the fāʿil is a pronoun necessarily latent, its implied form being "huwa" (ما) an indefinite noun qualified (nakira mawṣūfa), in the position of accusative as tamyīz (specification) of the fāʿil pronoun [Note: ما may be a relative noun in the position of nominative as fāʿil, the clause after it being the ṣila.], (يعملون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «(ثبت) إقامتهم التوراة»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ثبت إيمان....
The clause «أقاموا»: in the position of nominative as khabar of anna.
The clause «أنزل إليهم»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «أكلوا ...»: has no grammatical position, apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «منهم أمّة ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كثير منهم ساء ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the last resumptive clause.
The clause «ساء ...»: in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (كثير).
The clause «يعملون»: in the position of accusative as naʿt of (ما).

* Morphology:
(النعيم), a noun meaning ease of living, its pattern is فعيل.
(مقتصدة), feminine of مقتصد, active participle of the five-letter verb اقتصد, its pattern is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
1- Concision by omission (al-ījāz bi-l-ḥadhf): here it is in two places..
a- Omission of the muḍāf in His saying, the Exalted, وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ أَقامُوا التَّوْراةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ, i.e. they upheld its rulings and its limits and what the two contain of the description of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
b- Omission of the mafʿūl bihi in His saying, the Exalted, لَأَكَلُوا مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِمْ; the object of أكلوا is omitted with the intent of generality, or with the intent of the act itself, as in the saying:
"So-and-so gives and withholds."

safi-cedvel:67-67.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (57) of this surah.], (الرسول) naʿt (adjective) of أيّ, following it in the nominative in form, or a badal (substitute) of it (بلّغ) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (أنزل) a past verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (إلى) a preposition, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزل) (من ربّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أنزل), and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (إن) a jussive-governing conditional particle (لم) a particle of negation (تفعل) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (rābiṭa) (بلّغت) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn.. and (التاء) is the fāʿil (رسالة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi [Translator's note: so in the source; the negative particle (ما) in فما بلّغت is not parsed.] (الواو) conjunction (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) (يعصم) an imperfect verb, nominative, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (من الناس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يعصم), (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl) (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative (لا) negating (يهدي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is "huwa" (القوم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الكافرين) naʿt of القوم, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «يأيّها الرسول ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «بلّغ ...»: has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
The clause «أنزل إليك»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «لم تفعل....»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «بلّغت ...»: in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «الله يعصمك ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «يعصمك ...»: in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «إنّ الله ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لا يهدي ...»: in the position of nominative as khabar of inna.

* Rhetoric:
His saying, the Exalted, وَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ فَما بَلَّغْتَ رِسالَتَهُ, i.e. "and if you do not do it, then you have not done it".
In the identity of the protasis and the apodosis there is a secret without equal, for the Master, Glorified and Exalted is He, intended them to be identical, because not conveying the message is something known to people and settled in their understanding as a great and heinous thing for which its perpetrator is condemned; and because not spreading knowledge among the world is something that deserves blame — so what then of the message? So He made the recompense identical to the condition, so that the extent of the importance of conveying would become clear.

safi-cedvel:68-68.t:
* I'rab:
(قل يا أهل الكتاب) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (59) of this surah.], (لستم) a defective, non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb.. and (تم) a pronoun, the noun of laysa (على شيء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of laysa (حتّى) a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive (تقيموا) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by a concealed أن after حتّى, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) (التوراة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (الواو) conjunction (الإنجيل) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to التوراة, accusative (الواو) conjunction (ما أنزل إليكم من ربّكم) the i'rab of its counterpart has already been given [Note: In the previous verse (67).].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقيموا) is in the position of genitive (majrūr), attached to the khabar of لستم.
(الواو) conjunction (ليزيدنّ.. وكفرا) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In verse (64) of the surah.], (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (rābiṭa) of an implied condition (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing (تأس) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (على القوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تأس), (الكافرين) naʿt (adjective) of القوم, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «قل ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يا أهل الكتاب ...»: in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لستم على شيء»: has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
The clause «تقيموا ...»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أنزل ...»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يزيدنّ»: has no grammatical position, the response to an implied oath.. and the oath with its response has no position, conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «أنزل إليك ...»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
The clause «لا تأس ...»: in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition..
"if that happens to them, then do not grieve".

* Morphology:
(تأس), in it there is weakening (iʿlāl) by deletion on account of the jussive; its pattern is تفع with fatḥa on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying, the Exalted, لَسْتُمْ عَلى شَيْءٍ: in this expression there is evident belittling and contempt; among their proverbs is: "less than nothing". I.e. you stand on nothing worth counting until you uphold the rulings of the Torah and the Gospel.

* Benefits:
The arrogance of the Jews and their obstinacy..
Ibn ʿAbbās said: There came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ Rāfiʿ ibn Ḥāritha, Sallām ibn Mishkam, Mālik ibn al-Ṣayf and Rāfiʿ ibn Ḥarmala, and they said: O Muḥammad, do you not claim that you are upon the creed of Abraham and his religion, and that you believe in the Torah we have and testify that it is true? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Yes, but you have innovated and denied what is in it of the covenant taken from you, and you have concealed from it what you were commanded to make clear to people, so I am free of your innovations. They said: Then we hold to what is in our hands, for we are upon the truth and guidance, and we will not believe you nor follow you. So Allah sent down: قل يا أهل الكتاب لستم على شيء.

safi-cedvel:104-104.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction. (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, in the position of the accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis قالوا. (قيل) passive past verb. (اللام) preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (قيل). (تعالوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, by analogy (qiyāsan).. and the wāw is fāʿil (agent). (إلى) preposition. (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to the verb تعالوا. (أنزل) past verb. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ). (الواو) conjunction. (إلى الرسول) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb تعالوا. (قالوا) like تعالوا. (حسبنا) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (ونا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (ما) like the first, in the position of the nominative, khabar (predicate). (وجد) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, and (نا) a pronoun, fāʿil. (على) preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (آباء) first mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), and (نا) muḍāf ilayhi. (الهمزة) for the interrogative. (الواو) resumptive. (لو) a conditional particle that does not put into the jussive. (كان) defective past verb (of kāna and its sisters). (آباء) noun of kāna, nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (لا) negative particle. (يعلمون) imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is fāʿil. (شيئا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الواو) conjunction. (لا يهتدون) like لا يعلمون.
The clause «قيل ...»: is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تعالوا»: is in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Note: according to the majority, the nāʾib fāʿil is implied, i.e. "the saying", and the clause explains this saying (see ayah 11 of Surat al-Baqara ...).].
The clause «أنزل الله»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (ما).
The clause «قالوا»: has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the non-jussive condition.
The clause «حسبنا ما وجدنا»: is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «وجدنا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
The clause «كان آباؤهم ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لا يعلمون ...»: is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of kāna.
The clause «لا يهتدون»: is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause لا يعلمون ... and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "Do they say that?"

* Benefits:
1- «أَوَلَوْ كانَ آباؤُهُمْ etc.»..
The hamza is the root of the interrogative particles, and for that reason the grammarians devoted a lengthy chapter to it, in which they mentioned the distinctions it enjoys over the other interrogative particles. What concerns us here about this particle is that it may depart from the genuine interrogative to other meanings, which we summarize as follows:
a- Equalization (taswiya): as in «سَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ».
b- Invalidating disapproval (al-inkār al-ibṭālī): as in «أَفَعَيِينا بِالْخَلْقِ الْأَوَّلِ» and «أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِكافٍ عَبْدَهُ».
c- Rebuking disapproval (al-inkār al-tawbīkhī): as in «أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ تَدْعُونَ».
d- Affirmation (taqrīr): as in «أنصرت بكرا؟!» (Did you help Bakr?!) e- Mockery (tahakkum): as in «قالُوا يا شُعَيْبُ: أَصَلاتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَنْ نَتْرُكَ ما يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا».
f- Command (amr): as in أَأَسْلَمْتُمْ, i.e. "submit!".
g- Wonder (taʿajjub): أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلى رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ الظِّلَّ.
h- Finding something slow (istibṭāʾ): أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ!».

safi-cedvel:105-105.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab has already been given [Note: in ayah (87) of this surah.], (عليكم) a verbal noun of command (ism fiʿl amr) meaning الزموا (hold to), indeclinable (mabnī), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنتم. (أنفس) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (لا) negative particle. (يضرّ) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (من) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, fāʿil.
