(ضلّ) past verb, and the fāʿil is هو, which is the returning pronoun. (إذا) its i'rab has already been given [Note: in the previous ayah.], (اهتديتم) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ... (وتم) a pronoun, fāʿil. (إلى الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) placed first. (مرجع) mubtadaʾ (subject) placed later, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (جميعا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the pronoun of address in مرجعكم; its governor is the "being established" (al-istiqrār) that governs the preposition phrase. (الفاء) conjunction. (ينبّئكم) like يضرّكم. (الباء) preposition. (ما) relative noun in the position of the genitive, attached to (ينبّئكم) [Note: or a maṣdar-forming particle, or an indefinite noun described by the clause.], (كنتم) defective past verb (of kāna and its sisters), indeclinable on the sukūn ... وتم) a pronoun in the position of the nominative, noun of kāna. (تعلمون) like يعلمون [Note: in the previous ayah.]. [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in the ayah is تعملون, as in the clause list below.]
The vocative clause «يأيّها الذين ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «عليكم أنفسكم»: has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative, resumptive.
The clause «لا يضرّكم من ضلّ»: has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «ضلّ»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «اهتديتم»: is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of (إذا) to it ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the content of the speech before it, i.e. "if you are guided, then whoever has gone astray does not harm you".
The clause «إلى الله مرجعكم»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive and causal.
The clause «ينبّئكم»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the causal clause before it.
The clause «كنتم ...»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of (ما), the nominal or the particle relative.
The clause «تعملون»: is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كنتم.

* Benefits:
عليكم: a verbal noun of command transferred from a preposition and its genitive noun, meaning الزموا أنفسكم (hold to yourselves).
Discussing verbal nouns (asmāʾ al-afʿāl) requires expansion, which would take us outside the plan of the book; therefore I will confine myself to addressing the transferred verbal noun. Transferred verbal nouns are those that were used for something other than a verbal noun and then were transferred to it.
The transfer may be from «a preposition and its genitive noun», like «عليك نفسك», meaning "hold to yourself".
It may be from an adverb, like «دونك الكتاب», i.e. "take it". It may be from a maṣdar, like «رويد أخاك», meaning "give him respite". Or from an alerting particle, as in «هاك الكتاب», i.e. "take it". Transferred verbal nouns are all heard (samāʿī), so no analogy is made on them.
We will address in other places, to complete them, the other divisions of verbal nouns, the improvised (murtajala) and the deflected (maʿdūla) — so be patient ...!

safi-cedvel:109-109.t:
* I'rab:
(يوم) adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قالوا) [Note: or it is mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر (remember). As for attaching it to the verb (يهدي) in the previous ayah, that is nothing, because of the divergence of the two ideas in the two ayahs, and because the speech in the second ayah is resumed.], (يجمع) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). (الله) fāʿil (agent), nominative. (الرسل) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الفاء) conjunction. (يقول) like يجمع, and the fāʿil is هو. (ما) interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject). (ذا) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, khabar (predicate) [Note: (ماذا) may be a single word, an interrogative noun in the position of the genitive by an omitted bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (أجبتم), and the clause أجبتم is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).], (أجئتم) [Translator's note: so in the source, for أجبتم.] passive past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ... (وتم) a pronoun in the position of the nominative, nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (قالوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is fāʿil. (لا) the lā of generic negation. (علم) noun of lā, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative. (اللام) preposition, and (نا) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to the omitted khabar of lā. (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (of inna and its sisters), and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of the accusative, noun of inna. (أنت) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), for emphasis [Note: it may be a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is علام, and the clause is the khabar of inna ... or a pronoun borrowed for the accusative position, a tawkīd (emphasis) of the kāf.], (علام) khabar of inna, nominative. (الغيوب) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr).
The clause «يجمع الله ...»: is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يقول ...»: is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause يجمع.
The clause «ماذا أجبتم»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ذا) [Note: the returning pronoun is omitted, its implied form being أجبتم به.].
The clause «قالوا ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لا علم لنا»: is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying.
The clause «إنك ... علّام»: has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(أجبتم), contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion owing to the indeclinability on the sukūn: the ʿayn (second radical) of the word was deleted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; its pattern is أفلتم.
(علّام), an intensive form from the verb علم; its pattern is فعّال.
(الغيوب), plural of الغيب ... (see ayah 3 of Surat al-Baqara).

* Benefits:
1- His saying «ماذا أُجِبْتُمْ»..
The grammarians have a lengthy discussion about «ما» and its connection with «ذا». For ease, we summarize all the grammarians' views and confine ourselves to the relied-upon ones among these views. We have found that everything the grammarians said is confined to four ways:
The first: that «ما» comes with «ذا» that is a demonstrative.
The second: that «ما» comes with the relative «ذا».
The third: that «ماذا» as a whole is a generic noun meaning «شيء» (a thing), or a relative noun meaning الذي (that which), as in the saying of al-Muthaqqib al-ʿAbdī:
دعي ماذا علمت سأتقيه ... ولكن بالمغيب نبئيني
(Leave aside what you know — I shall guard against it — but tell me of what is hidden.)
Some held that it means شيء, and others considered that it means «الذي». But they agreed that it is all one word. [Translator's note: the source announces four ways but states only three.]

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīrī); (لم) is a particle of negation and the jussive; (تعلم) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «أنت»; (أنّ الله) is a particle resembling the verb (inna and its sisters) and its accusative noun; (اللام) is a preposition and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (ملك) is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (السموات) is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الواو) is a conjunction; (الأرض) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to السموات, genitive like it; (يعذّب) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (من) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (يشاء) is like يعذّب; (الواو) is a conjunction; (يغفر) is like يعذّب; (اللام) is a preposition; (من) is like the first, in the position of genitive, attached to (يغفر); (يشاء) is like يعذّب.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ لله له ملك …) [Translator's note: so in the source; «أنّ الله له ملك …» is evidently meant] stands in place of the two objects of تعلم.
(الواو) is resumptive; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (على كل) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (قدير); (شيء) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (قدير) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ الله, nominative.
The clause «لم تعلم …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «له ملك …» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «يعذّب من يشاء» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar «[Note: Or an explanatory resumptive clause with no grammatical position.]».
The clause «يشاء …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «يغفر …» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يعذّب.
The clause «يشاء (the second)» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative (من).
The clause «الله … قدير» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
The interrogative departing from its original meaning: in the saying of the Exalted «أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ».
The interrogative here is one of denial, to affirm the knowledge; what is intended by it is to cite that as evidence of His power, the Exalted, over what is to come of punishment and forgiveness, in the most eloquent and complete manner.

safi-cedvel:41-42.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) is a vocative particle; (أيّ) is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative, and (ها) is for alerting; (الرسول) is a badal (substitute) of أي or a naʿt (adjective) of it, following it in the nominative in form; (لا) is the prohibitive, jussive-governing lā; (يحزن) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الذين) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); (يسارعون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; (في الكفر) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يسارعون), by its being made to include the sense of يقعون (they fall into); (من) is a preposition; (الذين) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يسارعون; (قالوا) is a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (آمنّا) is a past verb indeclinable on the sukūn, and (نا) is a pronoun, fāʿil; (بأفواه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (قالوا) «[Note: I.e. their saying was with their tongues and did not go beyond that to their hearts.]», and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (لم) is a particle of negation, jussive and conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning]; (تؤمن) is an imperfect verb, jussive; (قلوب) is the fāʿil, nominative, and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) is a conjunction; (من الذين) is like the first and conjoined to it «[Note: The wāw may be made resumptive, in which case the preposition phrase is attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), and the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) is سمّاعون.]»; (هادوا) is like قالوا; (سمّاعون) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being «هم», nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (اللام) is redundant (zāʾida), for strengthening «[Note: It may be an original preposition, attached to (سمّاعون).]»; (الكذب) is genitive (majrūr) in form and accusative in position, the mafʿūl bihi of (سمّاعون); (سمّاعون) is a second khabar, nominative «[Note: Some allowed it to be a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first (سمّاعون); in that case there is an omitted muḍāf in the preposition phrase after it, i.e. «سمّاعون لكذب قوم آخرين».]», the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (لقوم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the second (سمّاعون) «[Note: It may be attached to الكذب — if the second سمّاعون is a tawkīd — i.e. they lie for the sake of other people … and «سمّاعون لقوم» means they are transmitters of reports.]»; (آخرين) is a naʿt of قوم, genitive like it, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (لم) is like the first; (يأتوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (يحرّفون) is like يسارعون; (الكلم) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (من بعد) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يحرّفون); (مواضع) is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (يقولون) is like يسارعون; (إن) is a jussive conditional particle; (أوتي) is a past verb in the passive, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and (تم) is a pronoun in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (ها) is a particle of alerting; (ذا) is a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (الفاء) is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (خذوا) is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) is a conjunction; (إن) is like the first; (لم) is a particle of negation only; (تؤتوا) is an imperfect verb in the passive, jussive, the protasis, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (فاحذروا) is like فخذوه. (الواو) is resumptive; (من) is a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (يرد) is an imperfect verb, jussive, the protasis, given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescents; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (فتنة) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis; (لن) is a particle of negation and the accusative; (تملك) is an imperfect verb, accusative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «أنت»; (اللام) is a preposition and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted ḥāl of (شيئا), an adjective placed before the noun it qualifies; (من الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to a ḥāl of (شيئا) «[Note: It may be attached to the verb تملك.]»; (شيئا) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative «[Note: It may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because it is its description.]»; (أولئك) is a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (الكاف) is for address; (الذين) is a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as khabar; (لم) is a particle of negation and the jussive; (يرد) is an imperfect verb, jussive, given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescents; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (يطهّر) is an imperfect verb, accusative, and the fāʿil is «هو»; (قلوب) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) is a muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يطهّر) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being يرد.
(لهم) is like له, attached to a fronted khabar; (في الدنيا) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar «[Note: Or attached to an omitted ḥāl of خزي.]»; (خزي) is a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لهم في الآخرة عذاب) is like لهم … خزي; (عظيم) is a naʿt of عذاب, nominative.
The vocative clause «يأيّها الرسول» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لا يحزنك الذين …» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «يسارعون …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative (الذين).
The clause «قالوا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «آمنّا …» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لم تؤمن قلوبهم» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «هادوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the third relative (الذين).
The clause «(هم) سمّاعون …» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of هادوا.
The clause «لم يأتوك» is in the position of genitive as a second naʿt of قوم.
The clause «يحرّفون …» is in the position of genitive as a third naʿt of قوم «[Note: Or it has no grammatical position, resumptive; or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being «هم»; or it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun in سمّاعون.]».
The clause «يقولون …» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يحرّفون «[Note: Or it has no grammatical position, resumptive.]».
The clause «إن أوتيتم هذا» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying.
The clause «خذوه» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «لم تؤتوه» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause that is the object of the saying.
The clause «احذروا» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the second condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «من يرد الله …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يرد الله» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «[Note: The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and its apodosis together.]».
The clause «لن تملك …» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «أولئك الذين …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لم يرد الله» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the fourth relative (الذين).
The clause «يطهّر …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «لهم في الدنيا خزي» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of the demonstrative أولئك «[Note: Or it is the first khabar, and (الذين) is a badal of the demonstrative.]».
The clause «لهم في الآخرة عذاب» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause لهم … خزي.
(42) (سمّاعون) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being «هم», the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (للكذب) is like the first; (أكّالون للسحت) is like سمّاعون للكذب; (الفاء) is resumptive; (إن) is like the first; (جاؤوا) is a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of jussive as the protasis, and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الفاء) is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis; (احكم) is an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «أنت»; (بين) is an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (احكم), and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (أو) is a conjunction; (أعرض) is like احكم; (عن) is a preposition and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أعرض); (الواو) is a conjunction; (إن) is like the first; (تعرض) is an imperfect verb, jussive, the protasis, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «أنت»; (عنهم) is like the first; (الفاء) is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis; (لن) is like the first; (يضرّوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (شيئا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. «شيئا من الضرر» (any harm); (الواو) is a conjunction; (إن حكمت فاحكم بينهم) is like إن جاؤوك فاحكم بينهم; (بالقسط) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (احكم) «[Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl of the fāʿil of احكم: «متلبّسا بالقسط» (in a state of justice).]»; (إنّ الله يحب) is like إنّ الله يتوب «[Note: In verse (39) of this surah.]»; (المقسطين) is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «(هم) سمّاعون» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «(هم) أكّالون للسحت» has no grammatical position, resumptive, or a badal of the resumptive clause.
The clause «جاؤوك …» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «احكم بينهم» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «أعرض عنهم» is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause احكم بينهم.
The clause «إن تعرض عنهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «لن يضرّوك …» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إن حكمت …» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «احكم (the second)» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إنّ الله يحب …» has no grammatical position, explaining the cause (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «يحب المقسطين» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(سمّاعون): plural of سمّاع, which is an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālagha) of the active participle from the triliteral سمع; its pattern is فعّال with a fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(فتنة): in the sense of misguidance; it is an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) from فتن يفتن, of the pattern-class ضرب; its pattern is فعلة, with kasra then sukūn.
(أكّالون): plural of أكّال, an intensive form of the active participle from أكل يأكل, of the pattern-class نصر; its pattern is فعّال with a fatḥa on the fāʾ and a doubled ʿayn.
(السحت): a non-derived (jāmid) noun meaning unlawful wealth; or a maṣdar meaning the unlawful, from سحت يسحت, of the pattern-class فتح; its pattern is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn, and it may be with two ḍammas.
(المقسطين): plural of المقسط, an active participle from the quadriliteral أقسط, meaning to act justly; its pattern is مفعل with a ḍamma on the mīm and a kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
1- The cunning of the Jews. This verse places us with the Jews in terms of their cunning and deviousness: they do not keep a covenant, do not respect a pledge, and are never to be trusted. They dared to distort the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This is not only of the Jews in the time of the Prophet ﷺ; rather it is their habit, and that is their description in every time and place.
2- A strange incident
A man and a woman of the Jews, both muḥṣan (married), committed adultery. Some of them said to others: Come, let us go to Muhammad ﷺ to ask him about the ruling, though he has no ruling. If he rules stoning, we refuse; if he rules otherwise, we accept. So they asked the Prophet ﷺ about that, and Gabriel came down with the verse of stoning (which is abrogated in recitation, not in ruling). They refused, denied it and said the ruling in the Torah is otherwise. So Gabriel directed him to a Jewish man named (Ibn Ṣūriyā), the most learned Jew at that time. The Prophet ﷺ asked them about him; they recognized him and said: he is the most learned of us. The Prophet ﷺ sent for him and he came, and he adjured him by the Torah, by Moses and by Allah besides Whom there is no god, Who saved them from Pharaoh and parted the sea for them, to tell him the truth. He said: Yes. He asked him about the ruling on the muḥṣan adulterer in the Torah, and he told him: stoning. But the Jews, when a weak person committed adultery, carried out the ḥadd on him, and when a noble person committed adultery they were lenient with him; a dispute almost arose over that, so they distorted the Torah and made the ruling flogging and blackening (taḥmīm). They would flog him forty lashes with a whip coated with tar so that his body would turn black, then he would be carried on a riding animal that went round with him among the people, then he would be blackened. The Jews disowned Ibn Ṣūriyā's statements and found it strange that he would expose them in this way. He said: I was compelled to tell the truth for fear of punishment descending upon us. Then the Prophet ﷺ ordered the two adulterers to be stoned, and applied Allah's ruling to them. In this incident is evidence of the truth of prophethood, of the agreement of the Torah with the Noble Quran, and of the cunning and malice of the Jews.
2 [The intensive form of the active participle] Intensiveness in meaning:
There are intensive forms of the active participle in the Arabic language that indicate intensiveness in meaning, and one of these forms occurs in this verse in the saying of the Exalted: «سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ أَكَّالُونَ لِلسُّحْتِ». This indicates how much they listen to lies and how much they consume the unlawful, for they are immersed in sins without restraint or fear. It may be useful to recall the intensive forms of the active participle; they are: 1- فعّال: such as سمّاع and كذّاب.
2- فعول: such as أكول and شروب. 3- فعيل: such as سميع, عليم and بصير.
4- فعل: such as شره and نهم. 5- مفعال: such as مطعان. These forms indicate intensiveness and abundance for the one who performs the act: أكول is one who eats much, and مطعان one who thrusts [or slanders] much.

safi-cedvel:43-43.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (كيف) is an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); (يحكّمون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent), and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (عند) is an adverb of place, accusative (manṣūb), attached (mutaʿalliq) to a fronted khabar (predicate), and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (التوراة) is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (في) is a preposition and (ها) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a fronted khabar; (حكم) is a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الله) is the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (ثمّ) is a conjunction; (يتولّون) is like يحكّمون; (من بعد) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يتولّون); (ذلك) is a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address; (الواو) is circumstantial; (ما) is negating; (أولئك) is a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as the noun of ما, and (الكاف) is for address; (الباء) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (المؤمنين) is genitive in form and accusative in position, the khabar of ما, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «يحكّمونك» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «عندهم التوراة» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يحكّمونك.
The clause «فيها حكم …» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of التوراة.
The clause «يتولّون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «ما أولئك بالمؤمنين» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يتولّون «[Note: It may be cut off as resumptive, so that it has no grammatical position.]».

* Morphology:
(يتولّون): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is يتولّاون. The quiescent alif met the plural wāw, so the alif was deleted, then the letter before the wāw was given a fatḥa to indicate the deleted alif.

* Benefits:
The saying of the Exalted «وَكَيْفَ يُحَكِّمُونَكَ وَعِنْدَهُمُ التَّوْراةُ». كيف in this verse is an interrogative noun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. It may be useful to explain its status in i'rab to complete the benefit: 1- it is a noun always indeclinable on the fatḥa, and it is in the position of nominative as a fronted khabar if a noun follows it, as in our saying: «كيف حالك». It comes in the position of accusative as the fronted khabar of كان or one of its sisters if a defective verb follows it, such as: «كيف كان عملك؟».
It is parsed as in the position of accusative as a ḥāl if a complete verb follows it, as occurs in the verse.
Some parse it as in the position of accusative as a stand-in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) if a complete verb follows it, as in the saying of the Exalted: «أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحابِ الْفِيلِ»; they interpret the speech as meaning «ألم تر أيّ فعل فعل ربك بأصحاب الفيل» (have you not seen what act your Lord did to the people of the elephant), and that is a view not far from correct.

safi-cedvel:12-12.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath (قد) particle of realization (taḥqīq) (أخذ) past verb (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) (ميثاق) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) (بني) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, since it is treated like the sound masculine plural (إسرائيل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, since it is a diptote (الواو) conjunction (بعثنا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.. and (نا) a pronoun, the fāʿil (من) preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of اثني عشر (اثني) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, since it is treated like the dual (عشر) a numeral component, indeclinable on the fatḥa, with no grammatical position (نقيبا) tamyīz (specification), accusative (الواو) conjunction (قال) past verb (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative (إنّ) particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl) and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of إنّ (مع) adverb of place (ẓarf makān), accusative, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of إنّ, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (اللام) preparing for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam) (إن) conditional particle governing the jussive (أقمتم) like بعثنا, and it is in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) (الصلاة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الواو) conjunction (آتيتم الزكاة) like أقمتم الصلاة (الواو) conjunction (آمنتم) like بعثنا (برسل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (آمنتم), and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (عزّرتم) like بعثنا, and (الواو) is redundant (zāʾida), being the prolongation of the vowel of the mīm, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (الواو) conjunction (أقرضتم الله) like أقمتم الصلاة (قرضا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, standing in for the maṣdar, for it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar) [Note: القرض may have the meaning of المقرض — with fatḥa on the rāʾ — and so be an accusative mafʿūl bihi.], (حسنا) naʿt (adjective), accusative (اللام) occurring in the answer to the oath (أكفّرنّ) imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of nominative.. and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anā" (I) (عنكم) like منهم, attached to (أكفرنّ), (سيّئات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (لأدخلنّ) like (لأكفّرنّ), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (جنّات) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra (تجري) imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ (من تحت) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تجري) [Note: or to an omitted ḥāl of الأنهار.], and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi [Note: and it is on the basis of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «من تحت أشجارها» (from beneath its trees).], (الأنهار) fāʿil, nominative. (الفاء) resumptive (من) conditional noun governing the jussive, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) (كفر) like أخذ, in the position of jussive as the protasis, and the fāʿil is "huwa" (he) (بعد) adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative, attached to (كفر), (ذا) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address (منكم) like منهم, attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil of كفر (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) (قد) particle of realization (ضلّ) past verb, and the fāʿil is "huwa", referring to من (سواء) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (السبيل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.. and originally: السبيل السويّ (the straight way).
The clause «أخذ الله»: has no grammatical position, the answer to the implied oath.
The clause «بعثنا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أخذ.
The clause «قال الله»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أخذ.
The clause «إنّي معكم»: in the position of accusative, the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إن أقمتم ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.. and it falls within the scope of the speech.
The clause «آتيتم الزكاة»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أقمتم الصلاة.
The clause «آمنتم برسلي»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أقمتم الصلاة.
The clause «عزّرتموهم»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أقمتم الصلاة.
The clause «أقرضتم»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أقمتم الصلاة.
The clause «أكفّرنّ ...»: has no grammatical position, the answer to the oath.. and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath.
The clause «أدخلنّكم»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the oath.
The clause «تجري ... الأنهار»: in the position of accusative, a naʿt of جنّات.
The clause «من كفر»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كفر»: in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: the khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «ضلّ سواء ...»: in the position of jussive, the apodosis of the jussive-governing condition, joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(نقيبا): an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) resembling the active participle; it is فعيل in the sense of فاعل, derived from التنقيب, which is searching; he was called that because he searches into the conditions and secrets of the people. It may also be an intensive form of the active participle, like عليم and خبير.

* Rhetoric:
1- Making the Majestic Name overt: in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثاقَ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ﴾, to instil awe, to magnify the covenant, and to stress the gravity of breaking it.
2- Iltifāt (shift of person): in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَبَعَثْنا مِنْهُمُ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ نَقِيباً﴾, it is a shift from the third person to the first person, in keeping with the ways of majesty; or because the sending was through the agency of Mūsā, peace be upon him.
3- Fronting the prepositional phrase before the explicit object: for what has been mentioned repeatedly, namely giving importance to what is fronted and creating anticipation for what is postponed.
4- Explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya): in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَأَقْرَضْتُمُ اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً﴾, where spending in the way of good, or giving recommended charity, is likened to a loan, by way of figurative usage.
5- Allusive metonymy (al-kināya al-īmāʾiyya): in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَآمَنْتُمْ بِرُسُلِي﴾; it is an allusive metonymy for striving and supporting the religion of Allah the Exalted and His messengers, upon them be blessings and peace.

* Benefits:
1- His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثاقَ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ﴾ — ولقد: there is disagreement about the wāw. Some said that it is a particle of oath and genitive, and what is sworn by is omitted, i.e. «والله لقد» (by Allah, indeed); this account is the closest to correctness, because it is interpreted according to the original form of the speech. The second account is to consider the wāw resumptive, with the oath omitted, on the implied form «والله لقد». This account involves forced interpretation. It is well known that the lām occurs in the answer to an implied oath, and the clause after it is the answer to the oath, with no grammatical position.
2- The i'rab of the noun after the numeral:
1- The counted noun comes after the numbers from 11 to 99 as a singular in the accusative, and is parsed as a tamyīz (specification); this occurs in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً﴾ and «هذا أَخِي لَهُ تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةً»; so each of كوكبا and نعجة is a tamyīz, accusative.
2- It is parsed as muḍāf ilayhi after the numbers from 3 to 10, and comes as a plural in the genitive, as in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿سَخَّرَها عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيالٍ وَثَمانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُوماً﴾ 3- It is parsed as muḍāf ilayhi and comes as a singular in the genitive after مائة (hundred) and ألف (thousand), as in His saying, Exalted is He:
﴿بَلْ لَبِثْتَ مِائَةَ عامٍ﴾ and His saying: ﴿فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ﴾

safi-cedvel:69-69.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl) (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as the noun of inna (آمنوا): a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) (الواو) conjunction (الذين هادوا) like الذين آمنوا and conjoined to it [Note: (الذين هادوا) may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with الصابئون conjoined to it together with النصارى, and its khabar (predicate) being لا خوف عليهم ...], (الواو) conjunction (الصائبون) [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic word is الصابئون.] mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ), intended to be placed later (ʿalā niyyat al-taʾkhīr), its khabar omitted, indicated by the khabar of inna [Note: This is the choice of Sībawayh and the Basrans.. According to the view of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, it may be conjoined to the position of (inna and its noun). There are other modes in the i'rab of (الصابئون); what we have mentioned is the clearest and strongest of them.], (الواو) conjunction (النصارى) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (الذين هادوا) [Note: Or nominative according to the other analysis of the i'rab given in footnote no. (1) on this page] accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif (من) a relative noun [Note: It may be a jussive-governing conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause لا خوف عليهم in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).. and the clause made up of the condition, its verb and its apodosis is the khabar of inna ...], indeclinable, in the position of accusative as badal (substitute) of (الذين آمنوا) and what is conjoined to it [Note: Or in the position of nominative as badal of الذين هادوا and what is conjoined to it.. It may also be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is لا خوف عليهم, with the fāʾ added, the clause made up of it and the khabar being the khabar of inna.], a badal of part for whole (badal baʿḍ min kull) (آمن) a past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (آمن), (الواو) conjunction (اليوم) conjoined to the Name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr) (الآخر) naʿt (adjective) of اليوم, genitive (الواو) conjunction (عمل) like آمن (صالحا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (الفاء) redundant (zāʾida), because of the resemblance of the relative noun to the condition (لا) negating, non-governing (muhmala) [Note: Or governing like laysa, with (خوف) as its noun....], (خوف) mubtadaʾ, nominative (على) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الواو) conjunction (لا) redundant, to emphasise the negation (هم) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (يحزنون) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «إنّ الذين آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (الذين).
The clause «هادوا»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «الصابئون with its implied khabar»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «آمن بالله»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «عمل ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آمن.
The clause «لا خوف عليهم»: in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ الذين آمنوا and what is conjoined to it.
The clause «هم يحزنون»: in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause لا خوف عليهم.
The clause «يحزنون»: in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

safi-cedvel:70-70.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq) (أخذنا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, and (نا) a pronoun, fāʿil (agent) (ميثاق) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) (بني) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ (إسرائيل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, for it is a diptote (الواو) conjunction (أرسلنا) like أخذنا (إلى) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسلنا), (رسلا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (كلّما) an adverb meaning حين ("when"), containing the meaning of condition, attached to the apodosis [Note: See footnote (1) on page (65).] (جاء) a past verb, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (رسول) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ) (الباء) a preposition (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable [Note: Or an indefinite noun qualified (nakira mawṣūfa), the clause after it being a naʿt (adjective).] in the position of genitive, attached to (جاء), (لا) negating (تهوى) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif (أنفس) fāʿil, nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (فريقا) an advanced mafʿūl bihi, accusative (كذّبوا) a past verb with its fāʿil (الواو) conjunction (فريقا) like the first (يقتلون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «أخذنا ميثاق ...»: has no grammatical position, the response to an implied oath.
The clause «أرسلنا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the response to the oath.
The clause «جاءهم رسول»: in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «لا تهوى أنفسهم»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «كذّبوا»: has no grammatical position, apodosis of a non-jussive condition [Note: The apodosis may be omitted, its implied form being "they disobeyed them and showed them enmity", and the mentioned [clause] is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) answering an implied question, as if it were asked: "What did they do with them?"].
The clause «يقتلون»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis.

* Rhetoric:
Eloquent iltifāt (shift): in His saying, the Exalted, فَرِيقاً كَذَّبُوا وَفَرِيقاً يَقْتُلُونَ, where the imperfect form is preferred for it, by way of narrating the past state, in order to make its terrible image present so as to marvel at it, to draw attention to the fact that this is their continuing habit, and to preserve the verse-endings of the noble verse. The advancing of فريقا in both places is for giving importance to it and arousing the listener's eagerness to know what they did with it.

safi-cedvel:71-71.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction (حسبوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma..
and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle (لا) negating (تكون) a complete (tāmm) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) (فتنة) fāʿil of تكون, nominative (marfūʿ).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن لا تكون فتنة) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of حسبوا.
(الفاء) conjunction (عموا) like حسبوا (الواو) conjunction (صمّوا) like حسبوا (ثمّ) a conjunction (تاب) a past verb (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (على) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تاب), (ثم عموا وصمّوا) like the first (كثير) badal (substitute) of the pronoun in عموا [Note: In that case the pronoun in صمّوا refers to كثير, which comes after it in wording but precedes it in rank, and that is permissible.. They also permitted كثير to be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with what precedes it as khabar (predicate) — and that is weak —.], (منهم) like عليهم, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of كثير (الواو) resumptive (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative (بصير) khabar, nominative (الباء) a preposition (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, the resumptive pronoun being omitted and the clause being the ṣila.], (يعملون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما يعملون) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to بصير.
The clause «حسبوا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يقتلون.
The clause «تكون»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «عموا»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause حسبوا.
The clause «صمّوا»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause عموا.
The clause «تاب الله عليهم»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause عموا.
The clause «عموا»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تاب الله عليهم.
The clause «صمّوا»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the second clause عموا.
The clause «الله بصير ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يعملون»: has no grammatical position, ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(عموا), in it there is weakening (iʿlāl) by deletion; its origin is عميوا: the vowel of the yāʾ was moved to the mīm, then [the yāʾ] was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns.

* Benefits:
1- His saying, the Exalted, ثُمَّ عَمُوا وَصَمُّوا كَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ: many views have circulated about the i'rab of the word (كثير) occurring in the noble verse.
1- What Ibn Hishām permitted is that it be a mubtadaʾ, the clause before it being the khabar.
2- According to Sībawayh, the wāw is a letter indicating plurality, just as the tāʾ indicates the feminine, and on this basis كثير is the fāʿil.
3- Some considered it a badal of the wāw.
4- Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī considered it the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being: i.e. "the blindness and deafness are much".
The strongest view is to consider it a badal of the wāw of the plural, because that requires no forced interpretation and does not conflict with the meaning. When He, the Exalted, said ثُمَّ عَمُوا وَصَمُّوا, the reader might think that they all became blind and deaf; but to remove this misconception and to make clear that the blindness and deafness were not all-encompassing, He said ثُمَّ عَمُوا وَصَمُّوا كَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ. That is like my saying حضر المدعوون كثيرهم ("the invited came, many of them"), i.e. not all of them but most of them. And the speech of Allah remains greater than interpretation, and its secrets remain beyond human knowledge.
Imam al-Nasafī preferred this view in his tafsīr, and said: it is a badal of part for whole (badal al-baʿḍ min al-kull).
Complete kāna and defective kāna..
There is another benefit that occurs in this verse, namely the occurrence of kāna as (complete) in His saying, the Exalted, وَحَسِبُوا أَلَّا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ, and on this basis we parse فتنة as fāʿil. [Kāna] and its sisters were called defective verbs because they lack the khabar to complete their meaning: when I say (كان الوقت) ("the time was") without completing the sentence, the listener asks me to bring the khabar so that the meaning is complete. Therefore kāna and its sisters were called defective verbs because they need the khabar to complete their meaning. But if kāna occurs meaning وجد ("existed, came about"), and the meaning is complete with it and its nominative noun, then it is complete, and what follows it is parsed as fāʿil, as occurs in the noble verse, and from it is the poet's saying:
إذا كان الشتاء فأدفئوني ... فإن الشيخ يبرده الشتاء
(When winter comes, keep me warm, for the old man is chilled by winter.)
I.e. "when winter comes about"; in the verse the meaning is complete with it and its nominative noun, so it is considered complete.

safi-cedvel:72-72.t:
* I'rab:
(لقد كفر الذين) like لقد أخذنا [Note: In verse (70) of this surah.], (قالوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl) (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative (manṣūb) (هو) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is المسيح, the clause being the khabar of inna], (المسيح) khabar of inna, nominative (marfūʿ) (ابن) naʿt (adjective) of المسيح or a badal (substitute) of it, nominative (مريم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, for it is a diptote (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) (قال) a past verb (المسيح) fāʿil, nominative (يا) a vocative particle (بني) the one addressed (munādā), in construct (muḍāf), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, for it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural (إسرائيل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, for it is a diptote (اعبدوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (ربّ) badal of the Name of Majesty, accusative like it, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (ربّكم) like ربّي and conjoined to it. (إنّ) like the first, and (الهاء) the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), indeclinable, in the position of accusative as the noun of inna (من) a jussive-governing conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (يشرك) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يشرك), (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (rābiṭa) (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq) (حرّم) like قال (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (على) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (حرّم), (الجنّة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الواو) conjunction (مأوى) mubtadaʾ, nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (النار) khabar, nominative (الواو) resumptive (ما) negating (للظالمين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted advanced khabar (من) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition (أنصار) genitive in form and nominative in position, a delayed mubtadaʾ.
The clause «لقد كفر الذين ...»: has no grammatical position, the response to an implied oath.
The clause «قالوا ...»: has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إنّ الله هو المسيح»: in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قال المسيح»: in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), with قد implied, the linking element (rābiṭ) being implied as لهم ("to them") [Note: The clause may be an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), so there is no need to imply قد.].
The vocative clause «with its response»: in the position of accusative as the object of the saying.
The clause «اعبدوا ...»: has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.
The clause «إنّه من يشرك ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive — or causal (taʿlīliyya), explaining what precedes [Note: Because either it is from the speech of Allah the Exalted, and so it is resumptive, or it is the completion of the speech of Jesus, peace be upon him.].
The clause «من يشرك ...»: in the position of nominative as khabar of inna.
The clause «يشرك ...»: in the position of nominative as khabar of (من) [Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.].
The clause «قد حرّم الله»: in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «مأواه النار»: in the position of jussive, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «ما للظالمين من أنصار»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.

safi-cedvel:106-108.t:
* [Note: «This ayah and the two after it are among the most difficult of the Qur'an in ruling, i'rab and exegesis, and the scholars still find them difficult and hold back from them ... I say, seeking the help of Allah the Exalted in explaining their i'rab, the derivation of their vocabulary, the morphology of their words, their readings and knowing their composition ...» — end of quotation; the words of al-Jamal in his gloss (ḥāshiya) on al-Jalālayn, abridged.]
I'rab:
(يأيها الذين آمنوا) [Note: its i'rab has already been given in ayah (87) of this surah.], (شهادة) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ). (بين) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) [Note: the testimony was annexed to (بين) by extension and latitude, since (بين) has left the adverbial use for the object use, and that is a metonymy for dispute and quarrelling, because testimony is needed at the time of dispute.], and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi ... The khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ is omitted, its implied form being: "in what has been prescribed for you", and it is placed first [Note: (اثنان) may be the khabar, on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the testimony of two".], (إذا) an adverb of future time stripped of condition, in the position of the accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) شهادة. (حضر) past verb. (أحد) mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first, accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الموت) fāʿil (agent), nominative, on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the causes of death". (حين) adverb, accusative, attached to (حضر). (الوصّية) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (اثنان) fāʿil of the maṣdar شهادة, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the alif. (ذوا) naʿt (adjective) of (اثنان), nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the alif. (عدل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (من) preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted naʿt of (اثنان) [Note: or to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (اثنان), because the indefinite noun has already been described.], (أو) conjunction. (آخران) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (اثنان), nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the alif. (من غير) a preposition and its genitive noun, a naʿt of (آخران), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (إن) a conditional particle that puts into the jussive. (أنتم) a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative, fāʿil of an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned after it [Note: some parsers make it a tawkīd (emphasis) of the fāʿil of the verb ... and that is not necessary, because the attached agent becomes detached if the verb is omitted.], (ضربتم) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.. (وتم) a pronoun, fāʿil. (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ضربتم), by its being made to include the meaning of سافرتم (you travelled). (الفاء) conjunction. (أصابت) past verb ... the tāʾ is for the feminine, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (مصيبة) fāʿil, nominative. (الموت) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (تحبسون) imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the retention of the nūn ... the wāw is fāʿil, and (هما) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, i.e. the two others. (من بعد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تحبسون). (الصّلاة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الفاء) conjunction. (يقسمان) imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the retention of the nūn ... and the alif is a pronoun, fāʿil. (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يقسمان). (إن) like the first. (ارتبتم) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the jussive (majzūm), protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) ... (وتم) a pronoun, fāʿil. (لا) negative particle. (نشتري) imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being نحن. (الباء) preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (نشتري), by its being made to include the meaning of نستبدل (we exchange). (ثمنا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (لو) a conditional particle that does not put into the jussive. (كان) defective past verb (of kāna and its sisters), and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being هو, referring to the one for whom testimony is given or for whom the oath is sworn, understood from the context of the ayah. (ذا) khabar of kāna, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the alif. (قربى) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the kasra implied on the alif. (الواو) conjunction. (لا) negative particle. (نكتم) like نشتري. (شهادة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (of inna and its sisters), and (نا) a pronoun in the position of the accusative, noun of inna. (إذا) a particle of answer with no governing effect. (اللام) it is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), conveying emphasis. (من الآثمين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of inna, and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The vocative clause «يأيها الذين»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «شهادة بينكم ...»: has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «حضر ... الموت»: is in the position of the genitive by annexation.
The implied clause «(ضربتم)»: has no grammatical position, being parenthetical.
The mentioned clause «ضربتم»: has no grammatical position, being explicative (tafsīriyya).
The clause «أصابتكم ...»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the mentioned clause ضربتم ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then call two others to witness".
The clause «تحبسونهما»: is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of (آخران).
The clause «يقسمان ...»: is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause تحبسونهما.
The clause «ارتبتم» with its apodosis: has no grammatical position, being parenthetical ... and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then make them swear".
The clause «لا نشتري ...»: has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath.
The clause «كان ذا قربى»: is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl ... and the answer of لو is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "we would not bear false witness nor sell it for a price ...".
The clause «لا نكتم ...»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause لا نشتري.
The clause «إنا ... لمن الآثمين»: has no grammatical position, being an "istiʾnāf mānī" [Translator's note: so in the source, evidently for istiʾnāf bayānī, an explanatory resumption], and it is the answer to an implied question, i.e. "what will become of you if you do that?"
(107) (الفاء) conjunction. (إن) like the first. (عثر) passive past verb, indeclinable, in the position of the jussive, protasis. (على) preposition. (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (هما) a pronoun in the position of the accusative, noun of anna. (استحقّا) past verb and its fāʿil. (إثما) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنهما استحقا) is in the position of the genitive by the preposition, and the preposition with its genitive noun is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), in the position of the nominative.
(الفاء) linking the apodosis. (آخران) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being الشاهدان (the two witnesses) [Note: the word (آخران) may be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (من الذين استحقّ ...), and beginning with it is permissible because it is specified by the description ... and the khabar may be the clause يقومان, and beginning with it is permissible because it conveys generality.], (يقومان) like يقسمان. (مقام) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, and (هما) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (من) preposition. (الذين) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يقومان [Note: the preposition phrase may be attached to an omitted naʿt of (آخران).], (استحق) past verb. (على) preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (استحق), by its being made to include the meaning of استوجب (made due). (الأوليان) fāʿil, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the alif [Note: al-ʿUkbarī permitted five ways in the i'rab of الأوليان. The first: the fāʿil of استحق. The second:
a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is آخران, on one of the ways of parsing آخران ... and the nominal clause on this way is the apodosis. The third: the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هما, and the nominal clause on this way is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (آخران), which is described by the clause يقومان. The fourth: a badal (substitute) of the pronoun in (يقومان). The fifth:
a description of (آخران), which is described by the clause يقومان.
And by (الأوليان) two particular persons are not intended ... He said — and this is reported from al-Akhfash — in the last four cases the fāʿil of (استحقّ) is implied, namely the bequest understood from the previous ayah.
The fifth way is the one Ibn Hishām relied on in al-Mughnī.], (الفاء) conjunction. (يقسمان) like the first. (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يقسمان). (اللام) the lām of the oath. (شهادة) mubtadaʾ, nominative, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (أحقّ) khabar, nominative. (من شهادة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أحق), and (هما) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) conjunction. (ما) negative particle. (اعتدينا) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ... (ونا) a pronoun, fāʿil. (إنا إذا لمن الظالمين) like إنّا ... لمن الآثمين [Note: in the previous ayah.].
The clause «عثر ...»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the answer to the vocative.
The clause «استحقّا ...»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of anna.
The clause «(الشاهدان) آخران»: is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «استحقّ ... الأوليان»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يقومان ...»: is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause يقومان. [Translator's note: so in the source.]
The clause «شهادتنا أحق ...»: has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath.
The clause «ما اعتدينا»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the answer to the oath.
The clause «إنا ... لمن الظّالمين»: has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
(108) (ذلك) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ; the reference is to the legitimacy of the preceding ruling; and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address. (أدنى) khabar, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the implied ḍamma. (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle. (يأتوا) imperfect verb, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil. (بالشّهادة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يأتوا). (على وجه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl of الشهادة, and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتوا ...) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, its implied form being إلى أن يأتوا, attached to أدنى.
(أو) a conjunction of choice, or meaning "and". (يخافوا) like يأتوا and conjoined to it. (أن) like the first. (ترد) passive imperfect verb, accusative. (أيمان) nāʾib fāʿil, nominative. (بعد) adverb, accusative, attached to (تردّ) [Note: or attached to an omitted naʿt of أيمان.], (أيمان) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن ترد) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being يخافوا.
(الواو) resumptive. (اتّقوا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is fāʿil. (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الواو) conjunction. (اسمعوا) like اتّقوا. (الواو) resumptive. (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative. (لا) negative particle. (يهدي) imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being هو. (القوم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الفاسقين) naʿt of القوم, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
The clause «ذلك أدنى ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يأتوا ...»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «يخافوا»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause that is the ṣila of the particle relative.
The clause «تردّ أيمان»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second particle relative (أن).
The clause «اتّقوا ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «اسمعوا»: has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause اتّقوا ...
The clause «الله لا يهدي ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لا يهدي القوم ...»: is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).

* Morphology:
(آخران), dual of آخر — with fatḥa on the khāʾ — a noun meaning غير (other), having no verb from its own letters; its pattern is فاعل.
(الأوليان), dual of الأولى; its pattern is أفعل, meaning "the nearest", so it is on the form of the elative (ism al-tafḍīl) from the verb ولي يلي, of the class of وثق يثق, and ولي يلي, of the class of ضرب ... The alif was changed into a yāʾ in the dual because it is the fourth letter in the word.
(أدنى), an elative; its pattern is أفعل, from the class of دنا. It contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by conversion: the wāw was converted into an alif because it was vowelled and the letter before it had a fatḥa.
(يخافوا), in the verb there is iʿlāl by conversion; its origin is يخوفوا — with sukūn on the khāʾ and fatḥa on the wāw. Then iʿlāl by making vowelless took place in it, the wāw being made vowelless and the khāʾ given a fatḥa ... and then iʿlāl by conversion took place because the wāw was originally vowelled and the letter before it had a fatḥa, so it became يخافوا.

* Benefits:
1- إذن: it is one of the particles that put the imperfect verb in the accusative. The scholars differed about its origin. Some said it is the conditional «إذا», whose condition was deleted and compensated for by the tanwīn of compensation, and thereupon it came to behave like particles after having been an adverb. Some held that it is compounded of «إذ» and «إن»: if you say to one who will visit you إذن أكرمك (then I will honour you), the origin of the answer is «إذ إن تزورني أكرمك» (since if you visit me I will honour you); the hamza was deleted for lightness and the two words were merged into a single word. Its spelling in the Muṣḥaf is with the alif in all cases, but the spelling of the Muṣḥaf is not taken as a basis for analogy.
For that reason we find that the prevalent practice is to write it with the nūn, whether it governs or is left without effect.
And it is said: it is written with the nūn when it governs, and with the alif when it has tanwīn and is left without effect.
As for when pausing, it is converted to the alif in all cases — so reflect..!
2- The lām has many meanings and divisions, and all of them go back to two divisions: governing and non-governing. The governing is of two kinds: putting into the genitive and putting into the jussive. The non-governing is of eight kinds: the lām of ibtidāʾ (inception), the lām of distance, the lām of wonder, the lām of the answer, the redundant lām, the differentiating lām, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and the lām preparatory for the oath. What concerns us now among these divisions is the lām of the answer, in His saying:
«فَيُقْسِمانِ بِاللَّهِ لَشَهادَتُنا».
The lām in this ayah occurs as the answer to the oath, and of it is His saying: تَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ آثَرَكَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنا». It is one of the non-governing lāms. So reflect!!
